item.title: Varanasi Kachheri Ko Bomb se Udaane Ki Dhamki
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: Based on preliminary information, the District Judge of Varanasi received a fax on Friday morning containing a threat to blow up court premises in 12 districts of Uttar Pradesh. Considering the seriousness of the input, immediate precautionary measures were initiated to ensure public safety.

Following the alert, the District Judge ordered the evacuation of Varanasi Kachahari. Police and security forces were deployed in large numbers across the court campus, and entry and movement were regulated as part of standard security protocols. Lawyers, court staff, litigants, and visitors were safely evacuated in an orderly manner.

Officials clarified that the action was taken purely as a preventive measure, and no official confirmation has been issued so far regarding the credibility of the threat. Security agencies are currently verifying the information. Authorities have appealed to the public to remain calm and avoid speculation, assuring that safety and normalcy remain the top priority.

item.title: Prayagraj mein banenge do naye 4-lane bridges — UP budget se Shastri aur Yamuna bridge project ko milegi raftaar
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Prayagraj: Infrastructure development has received a major push in the latest Uttar Pradesh budget, with key allocations expected to accelerate the construction of two new four-lane bridges in Prayagraj.

According to officials, a new bridge approximately 2,500 meters long will be constructed parallel to the existing Shastri Bridge over the Ganga River at an estimated cost exceeding ₹1,500 crore. The project is aimed at easing pressure on the current bridge, which handles heavy daily traffic.

In addition, another four-lane bridge will be built alongside the old Old Yamuna Bridge, connecting Madauka to Karailabagh in the Naini area. More than ₹800 crore is expected to be spent on this second project, with funds likely to be released soon.

Authorities say the new bridges will play a crucial role in reducing congestion, strengthening regional connectivity, and improving travel routes linking Prayagraj with nearby regions including Varanasi and Madhya Pradesh. Once completed, the infrastructure upgrade is expected to significantly enhance transport efficiency and support economic activity across the corridor.

item.title: Varanasi Kachahari Area Mein Naya Parking Pass System Lagu, Bina Pass Gaadi Khadi Ki To Hogi Sakht Karvayi
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: Traffic police in Varanasi have rolled out a new parking pass system in the Kachahari area to address the persistent issue of illegal and unregulated parking that has been disrupting daily traffic flow.

Under the revised arrangement, advocates will receive special vehicle passes that allow parking only at designated zones near the Kachahari premises. Each advocate will be issued a single pass that clearly displays the COP number and the vehicle registration number. Traffic authorities have warned that any vehicle parked on the road without a valid pass will face strict enforcement action.

The move follows consultations with representatives of the Central Bar Association and the Banaras Bar Association. Traffic Inspector Anurag Tyagi stated that uncontrolled roadside parking had been blocking a significant portion of the road, resulting in frequent congestion in one of the city’s busiest legal corridors.

Pass distribution is scheduled to begin Tuesday at the Central Bar Association hall in the presence of traffic officials and bar representatives. Authorities say the initiative is designed to reclaim road space, streamline vehicle movement, and reinforce the message that public roads are not parking zones.

item.title: Varanasi–Aunrihar route par banega third railway track, ₹497 crore project se badhegi speed aur train capacity
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi : A major railway infrastructure upgrade has been approved for the route between Varanasi City and Aunrihar, as the central government clears construction of a third railway track worth ₹497.07 crore. The project, approved by Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, will expand the existing double line into a triple-line corridor over a stretch of 31.36 kilometres.

#Varanasi : A major railway infrastructure upgrade has been approved for the route between Varanasi City and Aunrihar, as the central government clears construction of a third railway track worth ₹497.07 crore. The project, approved by Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, will… pic.twitter.com/gLWAX7LZCQ

— Dalimss News (@Dalimss_News) February 13, 2026

Rail officials say the upgrade is aimed at reducing congestion on one of the region’s busiest rail sections, which currently handles heavy passenger and freight traffic. The new line will allow faster train movement, reduce detention time, and create space for additional services connecting eastern and northeastern India.

The Varanasi–Aunrihar stretch is a crucial rail link serving trains to cities such as Darbhanga, Raxaul, Kolkata, Gorakhpur, Prayagraj, Lucknow, Mumbai, Pune and New Delhi. Due to high operational pressure, railway authorities had long proposed tripling the route to improve efficiency. With approval now granted, officials expect better punctuality, increased freight handling capacity, and long-term revenue growth.

Railway estimates suggest the upgraded corridor could support an additional 1.99 million tonnes of freight annually. The project is also expected to accelerate economic development in eastern Uttar Pradesh, particularly in Varanasi and Ghazipur districts, while improving passenger convenience and regional connectivity.

item.title: Public Protests Over Defunct Mini Tubewell in Baluabir; Officials Assure New Installation Soon
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: Residents of the Ambiyamandi area in Baluabir Ward staged a protest on Wednesday over a mini tubewell that has reportedly remained non-functional for the past six months. The affected tubewell, located in the Chikwan Tola locality, has caused water supply difficulties for local households, prompting residents to raise slogans and demand immediate action.

According to locals, repeated complaints about the faulty mini tubewell did not yield a permanent solution, leading to growing frustration among the community. The protest remained peaceful as residents urged authorities to resolve the issue at the earliest.

Responding to the concerns, officials stated that the existing mini tubewell was very old and had outlived its utility. They informed that arrangements are being made to install a new and larger tubewell in the area to improve water supply. Authorities further said that the tender process has already been completed and work on installing the new tubewell will begin soon.

Residents have expressed hope that the new installation will address the ongoing water shortage in the locality.

item.title: Varanasi Begins ₹47.84 Crore Green Roads Upgrade With Underground Utility Ducts Under CM GRIDS
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi’s major roads are undergoing a major infrastructure upgrade under the Chief Minister Green Roads Infrastructure Development Scheme (CM GRIDS). In the first phase, six key roads wider than 10 metres are being modernised with underground utility ducts designed to remove hanging wires and prevent repeated road digging.

The project includes secure underground passages for electricity cables and pipelines, storm water drainage systems, pedestrian footpaths, and modern street lighting — aiming to improve safety, traffic flow, and urban aesthetics. Around ₹47.84 crore has been invested in Phase 1, with construction already progressing on major stretches including Tilak Murti–Bharat Sevashram, Ghanti Mill–Sigra Police Station, and Sundarpur main road. A second phase worth ₹7.22 crore has also been approved.

In the first phase, six key roads wider than 10 metres are being modernised with underground utility ducts designed to remove… pic.twitter.com/2GW8kxyFJF

— Dalimss News (@Dalimss_News) February 12, 2026

Officials say the goal is to give Varanasi durable, clutter-free, future-ready roads. The real test will be whether the project delivers long-term relief from damaged roads and chaotic utility wiring.

item.title: Sting Operation Claims Liquor Shops in Varanasi Selling Alcohol After Legal Closing Hours
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
A sting operation conducted in Varanasi has raised serious questions about alleged after-hours liquor sales in multiple areas of the city. According to the investigation, liquor outlets in the Adampur police station area near Golgadda, as well as shops near the Maidagin petrol pump and Nakhas under Kotwali police station limits, were reportedly found selling alcohol after the legal closing time of 10 PM.

The operation claims that customers were able to obtain liquor by knocking on closed shutters late at night, suggesting possible violations of excise regulations. Authorities have not yet issued an official statement regarding the findings.

item.title: Women Farmers in Varanasi Oppose Sports City Project | “Zameen Nahi Denge” Boards in Ganjari Fields
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: In Ganjari area of Varanasi, women farmers have voiced strong opposition to the proposed Sports City and Town City project linked to the upcoming International Cricket Stadium. Their concerns have become visible on the ground through notices placed inside agricultural fields, where they have clearly stated their unwillingness to give up land.

Women Farmers in Varanasi Oppose Sports City Project | “Zameen Nahi Denge” Boards in Ganjari Fieldshttps://t.co/Sp2mMzb9Od pic.twitter.com/QysR4Q9oie

— Dalimss News (@Dalimss_News) February 12, 2026
One of the boards put up by the farmers carries the message “Jaan de denge, zameen nahi denge” (We will give our lives, but not our land). The notice reflects the intensity of feeling among women farmers who say the land proposed for the project is central to their livelihood and family security.

According to official plans, the Sports City and Town City are part of a broader development vision aimed at improving sports infrastructure and urban facilities around the stadium. While authorities project long-term development and economic growth, farmers argue that agricultural land remains their primary source of income and independence.

Women farmers, in particular, say the loss of land would directly affect household stability, food security, and future generations. Many of them have expressed concern over the lack of clarity regarding consultation, compensation mechanisms, and rehabilitation options.

#VARANASI : Striking visual has emerged from the fields of Ganjari in Varanasi, where farmers have put up boards conveying their firm opposition to giving up agricultural land for the proposed Sports City and Town City project. The area is already witnessing construction of an… pic.twitter.com/LMi6eFBw1w

— Dalimss News (@Dalimss_News) February 11, 2026

Notably, the resistance has so far taken a symbolic form. There have been no large protests or demonstrations at the site. Instead, farmers have chosen to communicate their stand through boards placed in their own fields, making their position visible to anyone passing through the area.

The situation in Ganjari currently reflects a contrast between development planning and ground-level sentiment. This report documents the present scenario. Further coverage will focus on detailed interactions with women farmers to understand their expectations regarding dialogue, compensation, and participation in decision-making related to the proposed project.

item.title: 24-Year-Old Dhananjay Singh Shootout Case Reopens | Doctor & Pharmacist Called for Crucial Cross-Examination
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: A 24-year-old high-profile shootout case involving former MP Dhananjay Singh has resurfaced in Varanasi as the MP-MLA court resumes crucial hearings. The case relates to a 2002 attack near Taksal Cinema in the Cantonment area, where Singh and his associates were injured in a firing incident.

Special Judge (MP-MLA Court) Yajuvendra Vikram Singh has allowed an application under Section 311 filed by Dhananjay Singh, summoning two key witnesses connected to the defence’s plea of alibi — Dr. Arvind Kumar Singh and pharmacist Subhakar Yadav. Both are scheduled to be re-examined today via video conferencing.

The defence claims that at the time of the incident, accused Abhay Singh and Sandeep Singh were undergoing treatment at a government hospital in Lucknow. The renewed cross-examination is expected to test the authenticity of that claim.

This case, registered in 2002 and pending trial since 2003, is considered one of the oldest matters in the MP-MLA court. Although evidence from both sides concluded in 2021, a stay order from the Allahabad High Court delayed the final judgment. After the related proceedings concluded in August 2025, arguments in the main case resumed.

The court has remarked that the matter cannot be delayed further and that witness examination will proceed without adjournments. Legal observers say today’s hearing could be decisive in determining whether the alibi defence holds weight in this decades-old case.

The original incident occurred on October 4, 2002, when armed assailants allegedly opened fire on Dhananjay Singh’s convoy. Several people were injured, and a case was registered naming multiple accused, including political figures. While four accused were acquitted in a related gangster case in 2025 due to lack of evidence, the main trial continues.

With renewed momentum in court, attention remains focused on whether this long-pending case is finally approaching judgment.

item.title: Hi-Tech Trauma Center Proposed at Harahua to Cut Highway Accident Deaths, Boost Emergency Care Near Varanasi Ring Road
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: In a major step toward improving emergency healthcare infrastructure, a proposal to set up a hi-tech trauma center at Harahua has been finalized and will soon be sent to the Uttar Pradesh government for approval. The center is planned to strengthen medical response along the busy Varanasi–Jaunpur highway and the Ring Road, where heavy traffic and frequent accidents remain a serious concern.

Official data shows that Ring Road–linked areas, including Juthi Sahko, witnessed over 261 road accidents in the past year. Currently, victims often lose critical time being transported to city hospitals, affecting survival during the vital “golden hour.” The proposed trauma facility aims to deliver immediate advanced care with modern emergency equipment, trained medical teams, and rapid response systems.

Once operational, the center is expected to significantly reduce fatalities and improve survival rates, offering relief and reassurance to thousands of commuters and residents. The move reflects a proactive push by the administration to strengthen road safety and emergency preparedness in Varanasi.

item.title: Pulwama Anniversary Sparks Debate: Shiv Sena Leader Comments on Youth, Valentine’s Day in Varanasi
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: On the sixth anniversary of the Pulwama attack, Shiv Sena leaders in Varanasi expressed strong opinions regarding Valentine’s Day celebrations and the influence of Western culture on Indian youth. Speaking to media, Ajay Chaubey, Vice President of Shiv Sena in the state, emphasized the importance of preserving Sanatan Dharma and Indian cultural values amidst modern developments.

Chaubey noted that while young people are increasingly influenced by Western traditions like Valentine’s Day, it is crucial to remember India’s cultural heritage, including patriotism and respect for women. He cited that February 14 also marks the execution day of freedom fighters Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev, highlighting the day’s historical and patriotic significance.

The Shiv Sena leaders warned that they would take action if young people were found engaging in inappropriate behaviour during Valentine’s Day celebrations. They stressed that while the administration is responsible for maintaining law and order, the community also has a role in protecting culture and morality. Chaubey stated that Shiv Sena members will monitor public spaces, including parks, hotels, and malls, to prevent any acts that disrespect women or Indian cultural values.

The leaders also announced plans for a confidential campaign where symbolic effigies representing Western influence will be burnt, aiming to raise awareness among youth and encourage adherence to Indian traditions.

Shiv Sena’s statements reflect a continued emphasis on safeguarding cultural identity while balancing development and modern influences in the city.

item.title: Sensation in Varanasi: Brother and Sister Found Dead in Parade Kothi Hotel
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI – Sensation prevailed in the Parade Kothi area under the jurisdiction of Sigra Police Station on Tuesday, after a man and a woman were found dead inside their hotel room. The discovery has sent shockwaves through the local business community and travelers staying near the Cantt Railway Station area.

The Incident The deceased have been identified as Subba (42) and Dhanalakshmi (38), residents of Secunderabad, Andhra Pradesh. According to hotel records and identity documents recovered from the scene, the two were siblings who had arrived in the holy city on February 8 for worship and sightseeing.

The matter came to light when the duo failed to check out on Tuesday morning. After repeated calls to the room went unanswered and the door remained locked from the inside, the hotel management alerted the Sigra Police.

Police and Forensic Investigation Upon receiving the information, DCP Kashi Zone Gaurav Banshwal and other senior officials rushed to the spot. The police opened the door using a duplicate key and found both individuals lying on the floor.

A forensic team was immediately summoned to collect evidence. Preliminary findings suggest:

Suspected Suicide: A packet of suspected poisonous substance and various medicines were found near a table in the room.

No Suicide Note: While over ₹2 lakh in cash and identity documents (Aadhaar, PAN, and Driving License) were recovered, no suicide note was found at the scene.

Last Seen: Hotel staff reported that the pair appeared normal and had dinner on Monday night before retiring to their room.

Current Status Speaking to the media, DCP Gaurav Banshwal stated that while the initial evidence points toward suicide by consuming a toxic substance, the exact cause of death will only be confirmed after the post-mortem report. The police are currently attempting to contact the family members of the deceased in Andhra Pradesh to ascertain the motive behind this extreme step.

The bodies have been sent to the divisional hospital for further procedures. Local authorities are also scanning CCTV footage from the hotel to ensure no third party was involved.

item.title: Varuna River revival needs public action, not just government plans
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
The Varuna River has been an integral part of Banaras for centuries, supporting local communities and shaping the city’s cultural identity. In recent years, concerns have grown over the river’s condition, with visible pollution and untreated sewage affecting several stretches. Addressing this challenge now requires a shift from isolated efforts to collective action.

While various initiatives and plans have been undertaken to improve the river’s health, lasting change depends on consistent maintenance and public participation. Preventing waste disposal into the river, reducing sewage inflow, and maintaining cleanliness along the riverbanks are essential steps. Awareness among residents, shopkeepers, youth groups, and social organisations can play a crucial role in ensuring that restoration efforts lead to meaningful results. Banaras has repeatedly demonstrated its ability to transform challenges into success stories. The revival of the Varuna River can be the next such example. This is a sincere appeal to the citizens of Banaras to come forward, take ownership of the river’s future, and work together for its restoration. With shared responsibility and sustained effort, the Varuna can once again become a clean and living river for generations to come.

item.title: Varanasi sets Feb 12 deadline to make Panchkroshi route pothole-free
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: With Mahashivratri approaching on February 15, the VMC has shifted into high gear to ensure a smooth experience for devotees undertaking the Panchkroshi Yatra.

The Mayor has set a strict deadline of February 12 to make all roads leading to major Shiva temples (including Kashi Vishwanath and Mahamrityunjay) and the Panchkroshi route pothole-free.

Special cleaning campaigns will be conducted at all 'Padavs' (stops) on the pilgrimage route. The administration aims to keep the entire route "Plastic-Free."

Instructions have been issued to fix street lights and address sewer overflow issues immediately to prevent any inconvenience to the massive crowds expected.

item.title: VMC waives license fees for rickshaws and handcarts, relief for daily wage earners in Varanasi
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: In a landmark decision aimed at supporting the city’s daily wage earners, the Varanasi Municipal Corporation (VMC) has announced a complete waiver of license fees for cycle rickshaws, trolleys, and handcarts.

The Executive Committee, in a meeting chaired by Mayor Ashok Kumar Tiwari, decided that rickshaw pullers and handcart owners will no longer need to pay any license fees. Furthermore, they are now exempt from the tedious process of visiting the corporation office to renew or obtain permits.

The VMC also decided to simplify the bylaws for various other establishments. The licensing process for guest houses, home stays, private hospitals, nursing homes, and hotels will now be streamlined and moved online. Mayor Tiwari emphasized that the move is designed to end the harassment of small-scale workers and ensure "Ease of Doing Business" for local traders. The decision brings immediate financial and administrative relief to thousands of families in Kashi who rely on daily labor for their livelihood.

item.title: Kashi me aaya naya sports trend! Varanasi me banenge Pickleball courts
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi is all set to embrace an international sports culture as the popular American game Pickleball makes its way to the ancient city of Kashi. Soon, dedicated pickleball courts will be developed at selected locations in the city, adding a modern recreational dimension to Varanasi’s rapidly evolving urban landscape.

Along with the courts, special gaming zones will be created where people of all age groups—youth, professionals, and senior citizens—can enjoy fun-filled sports activities. Known for its fast pace, easy rules, and inclusive nature, pickleball has gained massive popularity across the world, and now Kashi is ready to join this global trend.

This initiative not only promotes fitness and an active lifestyle but also strengthens Varanasi’s image as a city that beautifully balances heritage with modern development. With new sports infrastructure, gaming zones, and recreational spaces, the city is opening fresh opportunities for community engagement, tourism, and youth participation in sports.

From ghats to gaming courts, Kashi is redefining itself—where tradition meets trend, and spirituality walks hand in hand with sport and wellness.

item.title: Yogi Adityanath gives 24-hour ultimatum to land mafia over illegal encroachments
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath issued a strong warning against land mafia, stating that illegal encroachment on government land will not be tolerated under any circumstances. He said he has given a clear 24-hour ultimatum to those who have unlawfully occupied public land to vacate it immediately.

The Chief Minister made it clear that anyone who fails to comply within the given time frame will face strict legal action. He emphasized that government land belongs to the public and cannot be misused for personal gain. Yogi Adityanath also directed officials to identify encroachments across the state and take swift action to reclaim such land.

His statement signals a tough stance by the state government against land grabbing and reinforces its commitment to law and order in Uttar Pradesh.

item.title: ₹944 Crore Jaunpur Four-Lane Bypass Approved to Boost Connectivity with Varanasi
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Jaunpur/Varanasi: Eastern Uttar Pradesh is set for a major infrastructure upgrade after approval of a ₹944 crore four-lane bypass in Jaunpur aimed at easing city congestion and improving regional connectivity. The 12.205-km corridor will begin near Basaratpur on the Varanasi–Lucknow National Highway and extend to Purvanchal University in Siddiqpur.

The bypass will directly connect NH-731 with NH-135A, strengthening road links between Jaunpur, Varanasi and Azamgarh. The project includes a 200-metre bridge over the Gomti River, two major and three minor underpasses for pedestrians and local movement, 8.76 km of service roads, and 7.2 km of slip roads. Flyovers and a major interchange are also planned to ensure uninterrupted traffic flow.

Officials say the project is expected to significantly reduce travel time by diverting heavy vehicles away from city roads, improving safety and easing daily congestion. Beyond traffic relief, the bypass is projected to stimulate economic activity by enhancing trade routes and logistics connectivity across Purvanchal.

Construction and future roadside commercial development are also expected to generate employment, positioning the corridor as a long-term growth engine for the region.

Addressing the media, Rajput said he does not feel any regret over the act of holding the minister hostage. He dismissed suggestions that the matter should have been discussed in private, saying there was no reason to seek a closed-door meeting.

The MLA clarified that he was not demanding any personal favors such as a contract, post, or political benefit. Instead, he claimed his actions were aimed at highlighting public issues that were being ignored. According to Rajput, when the voices of the people are not heard through normal channels, public representatives are forced to take strong and visible steps.

His statement has created a stir in political circles. While critics have raised concerns over the legality and seriousness of such actions, his supporters argue that the MLA was fighting for the rights and problems of common people. The incident has reignited debate over political responsibility, protest methods, and the boundaries of acceptable conduct in public life.

item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: A fruit vendor was allegedly assaulted by a group of men late at night in the Adampur police station area, leaving him seriously injured. The incident occurred around 11 pm when the victim, Sanjay Kumar Sonkar, a resident of Kajjakpura, was returning home after finishing work.

According to Sanjay’s statement, he had reached near Teliyana Phatak when he saw five men fighting among themselves. Moments later, the group suddenly turned on him and attacked him without provocation. He was beaten severely and suffered multiple injuries.

Following the assault, the victim’s family rushed to the police station and filed a written complaint against five unidentified persons. Acting swiftly, police detained three suspects and launched a formal investigation into the matter.

The injured vendor is currently undergoing medical treatment. Police officials say further legal action is underway and efforts are being made to identify and apprehend the remaining accused.

item.title: Nationwide Strike by Gig Workers Disrupts Food and Delivery Services
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Gig workers associated with online delivery apps and platform-based services launched a nationwide strike on February 3, demanding better working conditions and legal recognition. The protest has affected food and quick-commerce deliveries in several cities, causing delays and temporary service disruptions.

The strike was called by the Gig and Platform Workers Union, which is pressing for a separate central law to formally recognize gig and platform workers. Union representatives say workers face arbitrary ID blocking, lack of transparency in platform rating systems, and unstable income, leaving them without adequate legal safeguards.

As part of the protest, gig workers are scheduled to gather at Jantar Mantar around 1 pm to demonstrate and submit a charter of demands to authorities. Union leaders stated that despite repeated assurances from stakeholders, little progress has been made toward structural reforms, prompting workers to escalate their agitation.

Workers argue that gig employment has expanded rapidly in India, yet labour protections have not kept pace with the sector’s growth. They are seeking fair income standards, social security benefits, and protection from sudden account deactivation, which they say can instantly cut off livelihoods.

The strike has already led to noticeable disruptions in online food and grocery deliveries in multiple urban centers. Industry observers say the protest highlights growing tensions between platform companies and their workforce, raising broader questions about regulation and labour rights in India’s gig economy.

item.title: Varanasi: DM Cracks Down After Dalimss News Highlights Martyr Family Negligence
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: Swift administrative action has been taken after Dalimss News highlighted the disappearance and delay of an honorarium file meant for the wife of a decorated martyr. District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar has suspended clerk Jainul after he was found prima facie responsible for withholding the file related to the ₹65,000 honor amount of Shaurya Chakra awardee martyr Mahendra Pratap Singh.

The issue surfaced when the martyr’s wife, Uma Singh, a resident of Mahmoorganj, arrived at the collectorate in distress after being told that her file was missing. She alleged that the file had gone missing between clerks Jainul and Manoj Pandey. The matter drew public attention after Dalimss News reported the incident, prompting immediate administrative intervention.

Within a day of the report, the missing file was traced and restored. Officials completed the formalities and forwarded the file to the treasury. By Monday afternoon, the honorarium amount was credited to Uma Singh’s bank account, and she was officially informed by the collectorate.

The District Magistrate has ordered a detailed inquiry into the episode, assigning the investigation to the ADM (Protocol). Based on preliminary findings, clerk Jainul has been suspended and attached to the joint office of the collectorate pending further proceedings. The action has triggered strong reactions within collectorate and tehsil offices, serving as a warning against administrative negligence.

DM Satyendra Kumar stated that lapses in matters concerning martyrs and their families are unacceptable. He emphasized that strict accountability will be ensured and such negligence will not be tolerated under any circumstances.

item.title: Varanasi to Get ₹74.52 Crore Parking, Shopping Complex and Hotel Project
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi is set to get a major urban upgrade with the construction of a multi-level parking facility, shopping complex, and hotel at a total cost of ₹74.52 crore. The project aims to ease parking congestion while boosting the city’s commercial infrastructure and municipal revenue.

The Varanasi Municipal Corporation has raised ₹50 crore through municipal bonds to finance two major projects. Near Sigra Stadium, a G+6 commercial building will be constructed at a cost of ₹40.52 crore. It will include underground parking, a market complex, and hotel facilities. The building will spread across 2,600 square meters and provide parking space for 56 cars and 22 two-wheelers.

Another commercial complex will be developed on 2.5 acres of land at the animal hospital campus on Kabirchaura Road. This G+2 building will cost ₹34 crore, for which the corporation has already issued bonds worth ₹25 crore.

Officials estimate that these projects together will generate over ₹1 crore in monthly revenue. Shops will be leased at market rates for 30 years, with provisions for periodic rent hikes. The bond amount is expected to be recovered within 50 months, while the repayment period is seven years. Over this duration, the corporation anticipates total earnings of around ₹84 crore.

Meanwhile, the Shaheed Udyan Park in Sigra is also undergoing redevelopment at a cost of ₹7.49 crore. The renovation work is targeted for completion by June 30, 2026, further enhancing public spaces in the city.

Mayor Ashok Kumar Tiwari and Municipal Commissioner Himanshu Nagpal recently inspected the project sites, reaffirming the civic body’s focus on infrastructure development and sustainable revenue generation.

Varanasi: In Varanasi, the anti-corruption case involving the arrest of a bribery-taking sub-inspector has taken a new turn. Police officers and inspectors who reached the police station to support the arrested officer are now under the scanner themselves.

After the Anti-Corruption Unit caught the sub-inspector red-handed while accepting a bribe, several cops allegedly gathered at Lalpur–Pandeypur police station and created pressure on the investigating team. A local advocate has filed a complaint on the IGRS portal and written to the Police Commissioner, demanding action against those officers for misconduct and indiscipline.

The complaint alleges that the officers tried to influence the investigation, created chaos at the police station, and attempted to shield the accused. CCTV footage and social media videos of the incident are being cited as evidence.

Senior police officials have taken note of the complaint, and an internal inquiry is expected. Authorities have said that no one will be spared if found guilty, reinforcing the government’s zero-tolerance policy against corruption.

item.title: War of Words Between UP Ministers OP Rajbhar and Anil Rajbhar Sparks Political Buzz
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Two cabinet ministers of the Uttar Pradesh government, Om Prakash Rajbhar and Anil Rajbhar, came face to face with sharp verbal attacks in Varanasi on Monday, turning political differences into a public spat.

The controversy began when OP Rajbhar made a strong statement alleging that votes are being “sold” in the country. Challenging his critics, he used the phrase “maa ka doodh piya hai to batao,” which immediately sparked backlash. He also made indirect remarks about Anil Rajbhar and his family’s past, escalating tensions within the ruling alliance.

Hours later, Anil Rajbhar responded, expressing clear discomfort with the language used. He said that mothers should not be dragged into politics, adding that such statements are inappropriate and against political decorum. Anil clarified that he had not named any individual earlier and stressed that alliance partners should be handled with restraint and respect.

The war of words exposed growing unease within the government camp, especially on sensitive issues like UGC regulations, caste politics, and alliance coordination. While OP Rajbhar defended his remarks as bold and honest, Anil Rajbhar urged maturity and discipline in public discourse.

The incident has triggered political buzz in Uttar Pradesh, with opposition parties watching closely and social media reacting sharply. The clash highlights internal friction at a time when unity within the government remains crucial.

item.title: Varanasi IIA Welcomes Budget 2026‑27 Infrastructure Initiatives but Calls MSME Allocation Insufficient
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi, February 2026: The Indian Industries Association (IIA), Varanasi chapter, has expressed a cautiously optimistic response to the Union Budget 2026‑27, describing it as balanced and development-oriented, while highlighting both achievements and areas where expectations were unmet.

IIA representatives praised the government’s focus on regional infrastructure development, including projects such as inland waterways and ship repair facilities in Varanasi, which are expected to boost local industrial capacity. The association also welcomed the ₹100 crore sanction for the development of Ramnagar Industrial Area, viewing it as a step forward for regional economic growth.

However, the IIA emphasized that the allocation of ₹10,000 crore for the MSME sector fell short of expectations. Pankaj Agarwal, IIA Varanasi Chairman, stated that while the budget reflects a vision for self-reliant India and job creation, the MSME sector—crucial for employment and local entrepreneurship—requires more substantial support.

The association highlighted the potential of improved logistics and industrial infrastructure to encourage investment, increase efficiency, and create more employment opportunities in the region. “While we appreciate the government’s focus on development and infrastructure, MSMEs remain the backbone of local industry, and adequate funding is essential for their growth,” said Agarwal.

Overall, the IIA’s reaction can be summarized as cautiously optimistic, balancing approval for regional development initiatives with a call for enhanced support for MSMEs, which continue to play a pivotal role in Varanasi’s industrial landscape.

Varanasi, February 2026: A national seminar was organized at DAV PG College to mark 100 years of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) under the theme “Panch Parivartan and the Future of India.” The event brought together academicians, social thinkers, and representatives to discuss India’s future direction and social transformation.

The seminar was attended by J. Nand Kumar, National Coordinator of Pragya Pravah, an affiliate organization of the RSS. While interacting with Dalimss News, Nand Kumar made significant remarks regarding public responsibility and national interest.

He stated that acting with personal self-interest is harmful for the nation and society. He emphasized that criticism directed toward the state or government should be exercised responsibly, regardless of the stature of the individual involved. He added that such conduct is inappropriate even if it comes from highly respected religious authorities.

The seminar focused on the idea of “Panch Parivartan” (five transformations) and its role in shaping India’s future, highlighting the importance of ethical leadership, unity, and collective social responsibility.

Organizers said the event was part of ongoing discussions marking the RSS’s 100-year journey and its broader vision for India’s social and cultural development.

item.title: Uttar Pradesh Govt Approves Urban Redevelopment Policy 2026 to Transform Old City Areas
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Lucknow, February 2026: The Uttar Pradesh government, led by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, has approved a comprehensive Urban Redevelopment Policy‑2026 aimed at revitalizing old, underutilized, and dilapidated structures in the state’s urban centres. The policy specifically targets buildings that are 25 years or older and seeks to unlock latent development potential in prime urban spaces.

Under the new framework, the Housing and Urban Planning Department has been authorized to implement redevelopment projects that will unlock underused land, encourage private investment, and bring improved infrastructure to congested city areas. The government will facilitate the submission and review of redevelopment proposals by private developers, with an emphasis on collaboration with stakeholders and streamlined approval processes.

Many parts of Uttar Pradesh’s cities presently contain dilapidated or legally tangled buildings that have remained unused due to lack of resources, ownership disputes, or poor maintenance. The new policy aims to transform these into productive assets—such as modern residential, commercial, or mixed‑use spaces—through coordinated redevelopment plans.

To further support urban transformation, the government has also revised development fees, making it more feasible for developers to undertake projects in core city areas while balancing affordability for residents. These structural adjustments are expected to boost urban density, enhance housing supply, and stimulate economic activity in key metropolitan pockets.

The policy aligns with the state’s broader vision of planned urban growth, which includes improving livability, upgrading civic amenities, and ensuring sustainable expansion of Uttar Pradesh’s expanding cities. By encouraging the redevelopment of older urban spaces, officials hope to better utilize land resources and alleviate pressures on city outskirts.

Experts believe that the Urban Redevelopment Policy‑2026 could have long‑term benefits for the real estate sector, urban infrastructure, and investment climate in the state, provided implementation is backed by clear timelines and active public‑private partnerships.

item.title: World Wetlands Day: Indian Army, Namami Gange Lead Massive Cleanliness Drive Along Ganga in Varanasi
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: On the occasion of World Wetlands Day, the Indian Army, in collaboration with the Namami Gange initiative, carried out a large-scale cleanliness and awareness अभियान along the banks of the River Ganga in Varanasi. The campaign was organised by the 137 Battalion of the 39 Ganga Task Force along with the Namami Gange Ganga Vichar Manch, Metropolitan Unit.

Under the leadership of Army Subedar Dhanesh Kumar Yadav and Namami Gange district coordinator Shivam Agrahari, an extensive cleanliness drive was conducted from Gayaghat to Badri Narayan Ghat. Army personnel, along with volunteers and municipal corporation workers, actively participated in cleaning the riverbanks through collective labour.

During the campaign, hundreds of devotees who had arrived from different states were made aware that the purity of the Ganga is directly linked to human existence. They were urged to support ongoing efforts aimed at maintaining a clean and pollution-free Ganga. The drive echoed with slogans such as “Ganga Maiya Ki Jai” and “Bharat Mata Ki Jai,” inspiring public participation in cleanliness initiatives.

Simultaneously, a special campaign titled “Swachhta Hi Seva, Safai Hi Pooja Hai” was launched at Trilochan Ghat. As part of this initiative, ancient Shiva temples located within traditional structures (madhis) at various ghats in Kashi will be cleaned till Mahashivratri. The cleaning work began at an ancient Shiva temple located in a madhi at Trilochan Ghat.

Shivam Agrahari stated that special focus is being given to temples where regular maintenance is lacking. He added that the campaign has been ongoing for several years with the objective of preserving Kashi’s heritage and highlighting the spiritual significance of ancient Shiva temples.

Several volunteers and local residents, including Bhim Singh, Jai Vishwakarma, Anurag Sonkar, Praveen Yadav, Sunita, Mantara, Rajendra, Kallu and Geeta Devi, actively took part in the campaign, making it a collective effort toward cleanliness, heritage conservation, and environmental awareness.

item.title: If Pakistan Boycotts India Match in T20 World Cup 2026: ICC Rules, Points, Penalties Explained
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
In a rare and controversial development ahead of the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026, Pakistan has announced that it will boycott its scheduled group-stage match against India on February 15, 2026, despite confirming its participation in the tournament. The World Cup is co-hosted by India and Sri Lanka, with Pakistan’s group games to be played in Colombo.

Sporting Consequences

If Pakistan does not take the field against India, the match will be treated as a forfeit under ICC playing conditions:

India will be awarded two points for the fixture without any play taking place.

Pakistan will receive zero points, effectively losing ground in the group standings.

Pakistan’s net run rate will be negatively affected because, per ICC rules, the defaulting team’s full quota of overs is counted in calculating net run rate when a match is forfeited.

These sporting penalties could make it harder for Pakistan to qualify for the next stage, although arrangements such as pre-seeded Super Eight groups may affect the broader tournament implications.

Financial and Commercial Impact

The India vs Pakistan fixture is among the most commercially lucrative in cricket, generating massive broadcast, sponsorship, and advertising revenue worldwide. Analysts estimate that the cancellation of this match could lead to advertisement revenue losses of around ₹200–250 crore ($24–30 million) for broadcasters.

Because of this economic fallout:

The International Cricket Council (ICC) could withhold Pakistan’s share of annual revenue distribution — a significant source of funding for the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB).

The PCB might also be required to compensate broadcasters and commercial partners for projected losses.

Possible ICC Sanctions and Broader Repercussions

Beyond immediate sporting penalties, ICC has warned of broader consequences if Pakistan proceeds with the boycott:

Financial penalties or disciplinary action under ICC rules.

Restrictions on player movement such as limiting No Objection Certificates (NOCs) for Pakistani players participating in foreign leagues like the Pakistan Super League (PSL).

Reputational damage and strained relations with other cricket boards, potentially affecting future bilateral or multilateral series.

ICC officials have stressed that selective participation undermines the spirit of global competition and could impact the long-term development of cricket in Pakistan and the broader international ecosystem.

Diplomatic and Sporting Context

India and Pakistan have not played a bilateral series since 2012 due to political tensions, which have frequently seeped into sporting relations. Decisions surrounding this boycott echo similar past instances in cricket where teams have declined fixtures over security or political stances.

The world now watches closely to see whether Pakistan will formally walk away at the coin toss on match day and how the ICC will balance regulatory action, commercial realities, and the political sensitivities surrounding cricket’s most-anticipated rivalry.

item.title: UP Govt Renames Two Villages Ahead of Panchayat Polls; ‘Urmura Kirar’ Now Harinagar, ‘Hajipur’ Becomes Siyarampur
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Lucknow: The Uttar Pradesh government, headed by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, has approved the renaming of two villages in the state just ahead of the upcoming Panchayat elections, officials confirmed. The decision was taken in response to long-standing local demands and cultural considerations.

Under the new order, the village of Urmura Kirar in the Shikohabad tehsil and Vasudevmai Gram Panchayat of Firozabad district will officially be known as Harinagar. Likewise, the Hajipur Gram Panchayat located in the Bhrawan development block of Hardoi district has been renamed Siyarampur.

The state government’s announcement noted that both changes were made following requests from local residents and leaders, who felt the new names better reflected their cultural heritage and community identity. Authorities have also directed district officials to begin updating administrative records, signage, and official documentation to reflect the new village names.

Local representatives and villagers have welcomed the decision, calling it a recognition of local sentiment. They said the renaming honors historical and cultural values while strengthening community pride.

This move is part of a broader trend in Uttar Pradesh, where the government has previously changed place names to reflect historical and cultural narratives, including renaming larger cities and regions in recent years.

item.title: Violence at Sonbhadra Toll Plaza: Advocate Aarti Pandey’s Family Assaulted After Dispute, 2 Arrested
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Violence broke out at the Lodhi Toll Plaza in Uttar Pradesh’s Sonbhadra district after an argument between toll staff and a family traveling through the checkpoint escalated into an alleged assault. The incident involved advocate Aarti Pandey, who was traveling with her family at the time.

According to the complaint filed with police, the family had been waiting at the toll plaza for more than 10 minutes. When Aarti Pandey questioned the delay, a verbal exchange reportedly took place between her and toll employees. The situation soon escalated, with toll workers allegedly stepping out of their booths, abusing the family, and physically attacking them.

Eyewitness accounts suggest that multiple family members were beaten and pushed to the ground during the altercation. Three people sustained injuries in the incident, including a woman whose condition is said to be serious. The injured were provided medical treatment following the clash.

Police registered a case soon after receiving the complaint and launched an investigation. Authorities confirmed that two toll plaza employees have been arrested in connection with the incident. Officials said further inquiry is underway to establish the full sequence of events and identify the involvement of any additional persons.

The incident has raised concerns over safety and conduct at toll plazas, with local residents calling for strict action and improved monitoring to prevent similar occurrences in the future.

item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
The railway administration has extended the cancellation period of several key passenger trains connecting Uttar Pradesh and Bihar due to operational difficulties and technical reasons. According to an official release issued by the Public Relations Department of North Eastern Railway, Varanasi, a total of six passenger trains will remain off the tracks until mid-February.

The sudden cancellation of these trains is expected to cause inconvenience to daily commuters, students, and small traders who depend on these services for regular travel. Railway authorities have advised passengers to check the status of their trains through official enquiry numbers or the National Train Enquiry System before heading to the station.

As per the notification, Gorakhpur Cantt–Varanasi City Passenger (15129) will remain cancelled from February 2 to February 16, while Varanasi City–Gorakhpur Cantt Passenger (15130) will not operate from February 1 to February 15. The Siwan–Gorakhpur Cantt Passenger (55041/55042) has been cancelled on different dates between February 1 and February 16. Additionally, the Siwan–Samastipur Passenger trains (55122/55121) will remain cancelled in both directions from February 2 to February 16.

Railway officials have assured that efforts are being made to restore normal operations at the earliest, while passengers are urged to plan their journeys accordingly.

item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: Panic gripped passengers onboard an IndiGo Airlines flight travelling from Hyderabad to Varanasi on Sunday after a threatening message was found inside the aircraft’s toilet. The handwritten word “Blast,” scribbled on a piece of paper, triggered an immediate security alert and led to an emergency landing at Varanasi airport.

The incident occurred on IndiGo flight 6E 6719. As soon as the message came to the crew’s notice, the pilot promptly informed Air Traffic Control (ATC) at Varanasi. Considering the potential threat, authorities decided to carry out an emergency landing as a precautionary measure.

Even before the aircraft touched down, security agencies at Varanasi airport were placed on high alert. After landing, the plane was taken to the isolation bay located on the eastern side of the runway. Teams from CISF, the bomb disposal squad, fire brigade, and other security agencies were already stationed there. All 237 passengers were instructed to deboard the aircraft immediately.

Following the bomb threat, parts of the airport campus, including the departure area, were temporarily evacuated to ensure safety. Each passenger was asked to carry their hand baggage while exiting the plane. Dog squads were deployed to thoroughly check bags, and passengers were subjected to individual security checks.

Hyderabad resident Vijay Kumar, one of the passengers, said the situation was terrifying. He described it as the first time in his life he had experienced such intense security measures after landing. He added that elderly passengers, women, and small children onboard were visibly shaken and frightened.

Another passenger, Vikas Jaiswal from Mirzapur, revealed that during the investigation, passengers were asked to write English capital letters from A to Z, numbers from 1 to 10, and provide signatures. At the time, officials did not explain the reason. Later, passengers learned that the exercise was conducted to match handwriting samples with the text written on the threatening note found inside the aircraft.

After a detailed search and security clearance, authorities confirmed that no explosive material was found. However, the incident caused considerable fear and anxiety among passengers, many of whom said it felt like “everything could end at any moment.” The matter is now under investigation to trace the source of the threat and identify the person responsible for placing the note on the flight.

item.title: Clothes Drying Fight Turns Deadly: Young Mother Dies After Rooftop Fall in Varanasi
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: A tragic incident occurred in the Shivpur police station area of Varanasi, where a dispute over drying clothes on a rooftop escalated into a deadly confrontation between two women. The incident resulted in the death of a 22-year-old woman, while another woman sustained serious injuries.

According to police, the argument began when two women living in the same rented house got into a heated quarrel over using the rooftop to dry clothes. The verbal dispute soon turned violent, with both women allegedly throwing clothes at each other and engaging in a physical altercation. During the scuffle, one woman pushed the other. As she fell, the victim reportedly grabbed the other woman’s sari in an attempt to save herself, causing both of them to fall from the second floor of the building.

After the fall, both women were critically injured. Hearing the noise, local residents rushed to the spot and informed the police. By the time help arrived, one woman had succumbed to her injuries, while the other was found severely injured with fractures in her waist, arms, and legs. She was immediately admitted to the district hospital for treatment.

The deceased has been identified as Jyoti Prajapati (22), wife of Tej Bahadur. The couple lived in a rented house in Hatiya village of Murdaha market along with their two daughters, including a two-month-old infant. The injured woman, identified as Shamsul Begum alias Suman, was also residing in the same building. Locals said that disputes between the two women over drying clothes on the rooftop were frequent.

Jyoti’s husband told the police that the argument broke out on Saturday evening when both women went to the rooftop at the same time. What began as a verbal exchange soon turned into a physical fight, leading to the fatal fall.

Police reached the spot soon after receiving information and sent Jyoti’s body for postmortem examination. Preliminary findings suggest that she suffered a severe head injury, which caused her death on the spot. Meanwhile, the injured woman remains under medical care.

After the incident, Jyoti’s husband was seen in deep distress, struggling to cope with the loss while caring for his young daughters. Neighbors described Jyoti as a friendly and calm person, while alleging that tensions often arose between the two women.

Shivpur Station House Officer Virendra Kumar Sonkar said that an FIR has been registered against the accused woman based on the complaint filed by the victim’s husband. The matter is under investigation, and further legal action will be taken after the completion of medical and legal procedures.

item.title: Viral Video Shows Gold Extracted From Old Phones
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Imagine pulling a gold bar out of your old cellphone! A viral video in China showed how a man extracted almost 192 grams of pure gold using mostly SIM cards and old chips.

At the current price, that bar is worth more than $28,000. Sounds like easy money, right? But before you smash your phone, here’s the catch: the creator, named Qiao, admitted that to get that amount he had to process 2 tons of electronic waste. Yes, mountains of old bank cards and cellphones.

According to expert Sun Yafei, gold is used in microscopic layers so that circuits do not fail, not for luxury. The most curious part is that, after all the work and the money spent on dangerous chemicals, Qiao’s real profit was barely 10 grams. Your SIM card has less gold than a grain of sand, so you’d better not play alchemist at home.

item.title: Auto Overturns Near Bhelupur Water Tank After Wheel Comes Off
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
An accident occurred near the Bhelupur water tank in Varanasi when the wheel of an auto-rickshaw suddenly came off, causing the vehicle to lose balance and overturn. At the time of the incident, three people were travelling in the auto.

Local residents rushed to the spot after hearing the noise and helped the injured passengers. They were later taken to a nearby hospital for treatment. Fortunately, no serious injuries were reported.

Police reached the scene and cleared traffic to prevent congestion. Preliminary investigation suggests that poor vehicle maintenance may have caused the accident. Authorities have advised auto drivers to regularly check their vehicles to avoid such mishaps in the future.

item.title: Police Action Against Drug Trafficking Network, ₹6 Crore Assets Attached
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
In a major action against organized crime, the Sonbhadra Police have seized properties worth nearly Rs 6 crore belonging to codeine-based cough syrup smuggler Bhola Prasad Jaiswal. The assets were allegedly acquired through illegal drug trafficking activities.

Superintendent of Police Abhishek Verma said that the action was taken under laws related to organized crime and illegal narcotics. He stated that the seized properties were generated through unlawful means and were being used to support criminal networks.

Police officials added that investigations are ongoing and more actions may follow. The crackdown is part of a wider drive to curb drug smuggling and organized crime in the region.

item.title: Varanasi Set for Major Health Infrastructure Project
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi is set to witness a major boost in its healthcare infrastructure with the proposed construction of a state-of-the-art super-speciality hospital on nearly seven acres of land in the city. According to reports, the project aims to strengthen advanced medical facilities and improve access to specialised treatment for patients not only from Varanasi but also from nearby districts and regions.

To make way for this ambitious healthcare project, residential quarters housing around 120 employees will be dismantled. The decision has been taken as part of a redevelopment plan to utilise the land more effectively for public health services. Officials have indicated that alternative arrangements will be made for affected employees as per government norms.

Once completed, the super-speciality hospital is expected to offer advanced medical services, modern infrastructure, and improved patient care facilities, significantly reducing the need for patients to travel to metro cities for specialised treatment. This project reflects the government’s continued focus on strengthening health infrastructure in eastern Uttar Pradesh and positioning Varanasi as a major medical hub.

The initiative marks a significant step towards better healthcare accessibility, modernisation of medical services, and long-term urban development in the holy city.

item.content:encoded: In a significant development in the codeine-based cough syrup trafficking case, the Sonbhadra Police have seized properties linked to jailed accused Bhola Jaiswal in Varanasi. The action was carried out under Section 107 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), following due legal procedure. According to officials, the seized properties are suspected to have been acquired through proceeds of the illegal cough syrup trade. The operation covered multiple locations within Varanasi, where assets registered in the name of Bhola Jaiswal and his family members were identified and sealed as part of the investigation. Police authorities stated that the seizure is part of a broader probe aimed at dismantling the financial network behind the alleged racket. Further examination of financial records is underway, and additional action may follow based on the outcome of the investigation and court directions.

item.title: India Can’t Become Hindu Nation by Insulting Muslims: Dhirendra Shastri
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Katha Vachak Dhirendra Shastri has said that India cannot become a Hindu nation by abusing or insulting Muslims. Addressing people during a religious discourse, he stated that true strength of Sanatan Dharma lies in self-improvement rather than hatred towards others. Shastri emphasized that Hindus must first correct their own shortcomings if they wish to see India as a Hindu nation. “Only by removing the weaknesses within Sanatan Dharma can India become a Hindu nation,” he said.

He also called for unity among Hindus and urged people to end divisions based on caste. “Stop caste-based discrimination. We are all Hindu brothers,” Shastri added. His remarks have sparked discussion on social media, with many interpreting the statement as a call for internal reform and harmony rather than confrontation.

item.title: Gau Raksha Par Bada Sawal: Shankaracharya Cites Export Figures
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal_
item.content:encoded:
Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Questions ‘Gau Rakshak’ Image of UP Government, Cites Meat Export Data

Varanasi — Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand, in his continued remarks to Dalimss News, also questioned the public image of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath as a strong advocate of cow protection, alleging that the image does not fully match official trade figures and ground realities.

Speaking on the issue of gau raksha, the Shankaracharya said the perception of strict cow protection in the state is largely a “public image,” and claimed that available government and trade data indicate that a significant share of India’s bovine meat exports are linked to Uttar Pradesh. He argued that this raises serious questions about enforcement and monitoring.

He further stated that authorities often describe the export category as buffalo meat, but claimed that when comparing livestock population patterns of cows and buffaloes in the state, there are inconsistencies that, in his view, warrant deeper scrutiny. Based on this comparison, he alleged that cow slaughter may be occurring under misclassification, and called for transparent verification of records.

Swami Avimukteshwaranand also said that his office and associated religious groups receive videos and messages from different places where meat products are allegedly labeled as originating from Uttar Pradesh. He said such material is being collected and reviewed, and he urged authorities to investigate the supply chains thoroughly.

He reiterated his previously announced 40-day deadline to the state government to demonstrate concrete action against cow slaughter and beef trade, stating that measurable enforcement outcomes would be the true test of commitment to gau raksha.

No official response has yet been issued by the Uttar Pradesh government regarding these specific allegations. The claims are likely to trigger further debate and calls for data-based clarification from concerned departments.

item.title: Snan Se Inkaar Nahi — Shankaracharya Ne Bataya Asli Karan
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Explains Why He Did Not Take Holy Dip Despite Deputy CM’s Request

Varanasi — Addressing questions about why he did not take the holy dip at the Prayagraj Magh Mela despite a later request from the Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister, Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand clarified that he never refused the offer, but had placed a condition related to accountability and apology.

Speaking to Dalimss News, the Shankaracharya said his objection was not about the ritual bath itself, but about the alleged misbehavior of police personnel toward batuks (young religious students) accompanying him. He stated that he expected the local administration to acknowledge the incident and apologize to those affected.

According to him, he and his followers waited at the site for 11 days to give authorities sufficient time to review the matter and correct what he described as a mistake. He said that despite the long wait, no official representative came forward to apologize or formally address the complaint.

Swami Avimukteshwaranand said he never rejected the Deputy CM’s request for the snan (holy dip), but believed that an apology and corrective assurance toward the batuks was necessary first. Since that did not happen, he chose not to proceed with the ritual at that time.

He described the episode as an issue of dignity and respect toward religious students and said such matters should be handled with sensitivity by the administration.

No detailed official version of the incident has been issued publicly so far.

item.title: Boatmen Protest at Rajghat Over Proposed Electric and Hydrogen Jetties
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: Traditional boatmen operating at Rajghat staged a protest on Thursday after they were reportedly informed about plans to remove their boats to make way for proposed electric and hydrogen-powered jetties. The move has raised serious concerns among local boat operators, who fear the decision may threaten their livelihood.

According to the protesting boatmen, they were asked to vacate the space currently used for traditional boat operations as part of a modernisation initiative aimed at introducing eco-friendly water transport facilities on the Ganga. While the project is being seen as a step towards sustainable tourism and cleaner transport, boatmen allege that their interests have not been adequately considered.

Raising slogans and gathering near the ghat area, the protesters demanded that the administration hold discussions with representatives of the boatmen community before implementing any such decision. They said thousands of families in Varanasi depend directly or indirectly on traditional boat services for their income.

“We are not against development, but it should not come at the cost of our survival,” said one of the boat operators, adding that alternative arrangements or designated areas must be provided before displacing existing boats.

Boatmen also expressed apprehension that the introduction of modern jetties could gradually reduce demand for traditional boats, impacting the cultural and historical identity of river tourism in the city.

Officials, however, have maintained that development projects are being planned with a long-term vision for Varanasi’s riverfront and tourism infrastructure. Sources indicated that efforts may be made to balance traditional practices with modern facilities.

The situation remains tense, with boatmen urging authorities to reconsider the decision and initiate dialogue to find an inclusive solution.

item.title: Congress Backs Shankaracharya After Magh Mela Row, BJP Govt Targeted
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Congress Pradesh President Ajay Rai and National General Secretary Avinash Pandey met Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand at Vidya Math in Varanasi on Friday and sought his blessings.

During the meeting, Ajay Rai discussed the recent controversy related to the Magh Mela and expressed concern over the alleged mistreatment of the Shankaracharya. He said that Kashi is not just a city but a center of spiritual and cultural traditions, and any disrespect to saints hurts the country’s heritage.

Rai accused the BJP government of insulting Sanatan traditions and said that such actions would not be forgiven by the people. He claimed that the Modi-Yogi government is against religious leaders and spiritual values.

Avinash Pandey also condemned the incident and said that disrespecting saints is against democratic and constitutional values. He added that Congress stands firmly with Swami Avimukteshwaranand and will continue to raise its voice for the protection of religious freedom and dignity.

Congress leaders stated that the party will strongly oppose any attempt to suppress religious voices and will keep fighting to safeguard India’s cultural and spiritual heritage.

item.title: Padma Shri Awardee and Renowned Surgeon Prof. T.K. Lahiri Admitted to ICU
item.dc:creator: sushant_gaurav
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI, 30 Jan 2026 — Prof. T.K. Lahiri, a Padma Shri awardee and one of India’s most respected cardiothoracic surgeons, has been admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) at Sir Sunderlal Hospital, Banaras Hindu University (BHU).

According to reports, the veteran doctor has been unwell for the past 17 days, leading to his hospitalization today. Known for his legendary dedication and selfless service to patients, news of his admission has drawn immediate concern from the medical fraternity and the Varanasi community.

BHU Vice-Chancellor Reviews Situation Following the news of his admission, BHU Vice-Chancellor Prof. Ajit Kumar Chaturvedi visited Sir Sunderlal Hospital to personally assess the situation. During his visit, Prof. Chaturvedi met with the medical team to review the treatment protocol being administered to the senior surgeon.

The Vice-Chancellor expressed his deep concern and conveyed his best wishes, hoping for Prof. Lahiri’s speedy and complete recovery.

A Life of Service Prof. Lahiri is a celebrated figure in the medical world, often recognized by residents of Varanasi for his simplicity—frequently seen walking to the hospital or refusing private practice to serve the common people. The hospital administration is closely monitoring his condition.

item.title: SP MP Ramji Lal Suman Visits Manikarnika Ghat, Alleges Heritage Damage
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Samajwadi Party MP Ramji Lal Suman visited Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi to review the ongoing redevelopment work and alleged demolition of heritage structures. He reached the ghat by boat and inspected the site where damaged idols were reportedly found.

Addressing party workers later, Suman accused the government of hiding facts and misleading the public. He rejected claims that the damaged idols were created using artificial intelligence, calling them far from reality. He said that while the President speaks about protecting heritage, the ruling party is allegedly destroying ancient sites in Kashi.

Referring to an earlier incident where an SP delegation was stopped from visiting the area, Suman said elected representatives are being prevented from accessing ground realities. He questioned why leaders are restricted from inspecting public projects.

The MP also expressed concern over the demolition of structures linked to Ahilyabai Holkar’s legacy, calling it unfortunate and harmful to India’s cultural heritage. He demanded transparency and urged the government to protect religious and historical sites instead of damaging them in the name of development.

item.title: Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Speaks to Dalimss News After Returning from Magh Mela, Raises Concerns Over Treatment of Hindu Symbols
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi — Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand, in an exclusive interaction with Dalimss News after returning from the Magh Mela, expressed dissatisfaction over recent developments related to Hindu religious symbols and said that many followers of Sanatan Dharma feel hurt.

Speaking after his return, the Shankaracharya stated that he stayed at the Magh Mela site for four days expecting authorities to acknowledge and correct what he described as mistakes. However, according to him, no concrete response or acceptance came from the administration during that period.

He said that after waiting for dialogue and corrective action, he decided to leave the site and indicated that the matter would be raised again during the next Magh Mela gathering if concerns remain unaddressed.

During the conversation, Swami Avimukteshwaranand emphasized that his immediate focus will now be on promoting and strengthening efforts related to cow protection (gau mata raksha). He described it as a key priority area for upcoming religious and social initiatives.

He also called for greater sensitivity from authorities toward religious sentiments and symbols, adding that issues repeatedly raised by Sanatan representatives should be addressed through proper dialogue and mutual understanding.

The statement has drawn attention among followers and religious groups, with further reactions expected in the coming days.

item.title: Varanasi Airport Tunnel Work Halted After Water Seepage During Excavation
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Construction work on the six-lane tunnel beneath the Varanasi airport runway has been temporarily halted after water seepage was detected during excavation. The incident occurred while groundwork was underway near the Babatpur area, prompting authorities to stop work at the affected site as a precautionary measure.

The tunnel is part of a major infrastructure project aimed at rerouting National Highway-31 underground to facilitate the expansion of Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport. The work is being carried out by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

According to information gathered from the site, water emerged during deep excavation, raising concerns about soil conditions and groundwater levels in the area. Following standard safety protocols, construction activities were suspended at that particular location to allow for technical assessment.

Local residents have indicated that the region has historically had a relatively high groundwater table, which may explain the seepage. Engineering experts are currently evaluating the source of the water and determining suitable mitigation measures, such as enhanced drainage or controlled dewatering, before work resumes.

Officials have clarified that the project itself has not been cancelled and that halting work is a routine safety step in large-scale infrastructure development. Further progress will depend on geological studies and the implementation of necessary technical solutions.

Authorities maintain that safety and structural integrity remain the top priority and that construction will continue only after conditions are deemed secure.

item.title: Varanasi Municipal Corporation Steps Up Park Beautification and Pond Conservation Drive
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
The Varanasi Municipal Corporation has intensified efforts to beautify city parks and conserve ancient ponds and water bodies. On Thursday, Municipal Commissioner Himanshu Nagpal conducted a detailed inspection across several wards to review ongoing development and public facilities.

During the visit, he ordered immediate cleaning of waste and floral offerings from the Pisach Mochan Kund and emphasized the importance of preserving the city’s cultural heritage. He also inspected Pisach Mochan Park, Ram Katora Park, and Buddha Park, directing officials to repair damaged open gym equipment for public use.

The Commissioner reviewed sanitation arrangements using a mobile app to verify staff attendance and found the system satisfactory. He also took strict action against roadside encroachments, imposing a fine of Rs 3,000 on shopkeepers for blocking roads and footpaths, and warned them against future violations.

Officials stated that regular monitoring will continue to ensure better civic amenities and improved urban management in Varanasi.

item.title: Anganwadi Workers Announce Big Protest in Lucknow on 8 March
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Anganwadi workers across the state have announced a major protest to press for an increase in honorarium and a reduction in excessive workload.

The workers allege that despite being the backbone of grassroots welfare delivery, their salaries remain disproportionately low compared to the responsibilities assigned to them.

According to representatives of the Anganwadi unions, workers are burdened with multiple duties beyond their core responsibilities, including data entry, surveys, election-related work, and administrative tasks.

They argue that this growing workload has not been matched with fair compensation or adequate support from the government.

The unions have warned that if their long-pending demands are not addressed, Anganwadi workers from across the state will gather in Lucknow on 8 March to register their protest. They have described the proposed demonstration as a decisive step to draw the government’s attention to issues affecting their livelihoods and working conditions.

The workers maintain that their demands are not new and have been raised repeatedly in the past, but assurances have failed to translate into concrete action. They have urged the government to initiate dialogue and take immediate steps to improve salaries and rationalise work responsibilities.
