item.title: Varanasi Airport Mega Project: Runway Ke Neeche Banega 6-Lane Tunnel
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi is witnessing one of the most ambitious infrastructure projects in eastern India, as construction begins on a six-lane tunnel beneath the runway of Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport. Once completed, vehicles will move through the tunnel while aircraft operate on an extended runway above it—an engineering feat rarely seen in the country.

The project involves shifting National Highway-31 underground near Babatpur, allowing the airport runway to be extended from its current length of 2,745 metres to 4,075 metres. The expansion is expected to significantly enhance aircraft operations, including the handling of larger aircraft and improved landings during low-visibility conditions such as dense fog.

The total estimated cost of the project stands at approximately ₹652 crore, out of which around ₹362 crore is allocated specifically for the tunnel and associated infrastructure. The work is being executed under the supervision of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

To ensure safety and uninterrupted movement, the tunnel is being equipped with modern facilities, including CCTV surveillance, security sentry posts, a dedicated drainage system, and sump wells for water management. These measures aim to keep the tunnel operational even during heavy rainfall or monsoon conditions.

Beyond airport expansion, the project is expected to ease traffic congestion on the Lucknow–Varanasi corridor and improve overall connectivity in Purvanchal. Officials describe the development as a long-term investment in regional mobility, aviation capacity, and economic growth.

item.title: Varanasi: Businessman Duped of Rs 9.84 Lakh in Online Profit Scam
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
A businessman from the Sigra area of Varanasi was cheated of Rs 9.84 lakh in a cyber fraud case on the pretext of earning profits in online business. The victim, Haunsla Prasad Mishra, said he received a call from an unknown number, where the caller claimed to be associated with an online product-selling company and promised 15 percent profit.

After nearly two months of communication, the fraudster convinced the businessman to invest money. Between June 16 and June 19, the victim transferred the amount in five installments through RTGS and online payment methods to a bank account provided by the caller. However, neither the promised profit nor the invested amount was returned, and the accused later switched off his mobile phone.

Sigra police have registered a case against unknown persons and started an investigation. Officials said efforts are underway to trace the accused and take further legal action.

item.title: 64-Hour Traffic Diversion in Varanasi from Jan 30–Feb 1 for Sant Ravidas Jayanti Celebrations
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Traffic movement in Varanasi will remain restricted for 64 continuous hours in view of the Sant Ravidas Jayanti celebrations. The city administration has imposed a major traffic diversion from the morning of January 30 till midnight of February 1 on routes leading to the Sant Ravidas Temple at Sir Govardhan.

With a large number of devotees arriving ahead of the celebrations, authorities have barred regular vehicles from entering the temple zone to ensure smooth traffic flow and public safety. Several routes including Bhagwanpur, Ramna, Ravidas Gate, Lanka, Naria, and areas near BHU will face diversions, while only vehicles related to the event will be allowed near the temple.

Police and traffic officials have advised commuters to follow diversion plans and use alternate routes to avoid inconvenience during the festival period.

item.title: UGC Bill Dissent Intensifies in Varanasi as Organisations Demand Immediate Consultation
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Dissent over the proposed UGC Bill is escalating, as multiple organisations and legal voices have issued a strong caution to the authorities, calling for immediate consultation and reconsideration of the legislation. Opposing groups argue that the bill, in its current form, raises concerns about administrative overreach and the absence of adequate procedural clarity. Memorandums submitted to district officials highlight the need for clear safeguards, warning that unresolved ambiguities could lead to broader unrest and institutional uncertainty.

Legal experts have echoed these concerns, noting that reforms of this scale require consensus-building and transparency. According to them, policies affecting higher education must be carefully structured to avoid inconsistent interpretation and unintended consequences.

The government, however, maintains that the UGC Bill seeks to improve regulatory efficiency and ensure accountability across institutions. Critics respond that without meaningful engagement with stakeholders, the intent of reform may be overshadowed by resistance and mistrust.

As pressure mounts, organisations opposing the bill have indicated that further steps may follow if their concerns are not addressed. With positions hardening on both sides, the situation remains fluid, and the coming days are expected to be crucial in determining the future course of the UGC Bill debate.

While the government maintains that the UGC Bill is aimed at strengthening regulation and improving accountability in higher education, critics insist that the objectives must be matched with inclusive dialogue. They warn that ignoring dissenting voices could escalate opposition beyond institutional corridors.

With the issuance of what many describe as an ultimatum, attention is now on the authorities’ response. Observers note that the next phase of the debate will depend largely on whether meaningful engagement takes place or whether the standoff over the UGC Bill continues to deepen.

item.title: After 3 Days of Protest, Sangathans Celebrate Holi as Supreme Court Issues Stay Order
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
After three continuous days of protest, the atmosphere shifted dramatically as various organizations (sangathan) marked the moment with Holi celebrations following the Supreme Court’s stay order. What had been days of sustained agitation and demonstrations turned into scenes of colour, relief, and collective celebration, symbolising a temporary pause in the movement.

Members of the organizations stated that the Supreme Court’s stay order was seen as a significant development that acknowledged the concerns raised during the protest. The celebration of Holi was not merely festive but symbolic — reflecting hope, unity, and faith in the constitutional process after days of persistent struggle.

Leaders of the sangathan clarified that while the celebration expressed happiness over the stay order, the movement itself is not over. They emphasized that their demands remain intact and that they will continue to closely monitor future developments. The peaceful transition from protest to celebration highlighted the democratic nature of the agitation and the collective resolve to continue the fight for justice through lawful and constitutional means.

item.title: Varanasi Students Intensify UGC Bill Protest
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Students in Varanasi intensified their protest against the proposed UGC Bill as a large-scale protest march and memorandum submission were organized at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith from 10 a.m. onwards. Raising slogans and carrying placards, the students expressed strong opposition to the draft regulations, calling them discriminatory and harmful to the interests of marginalized communities and the future of higher education.

The protestors stated that the UGC Bill, in its present form, threatens the principles of social justice, academic autonomy, and equal opportunity. They demanded an immediate rollback of the draft and urged the authorities to hold wider consultations with students, teachers, and academic experts before implementing any such policy. A memorandum highlighting their concerns was submitted to the university administration, seeking its intervention and support.

Amid the ongoing nationwide debate, the latest observations by the Supreme Court have added a new dimension to the issue, giving fresh momentum to the students’ movement. Protest leaders said they would continue their democratic struggle until their voices are heard and concrete assurances are given. The demonstration remained peaceful, reflecting the students’ resolve to safeguard constitutional values and the future of India’s education system.

item.title: Ajay Rai Slams New UGC Rules
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
leader Ajay Rai has raised serious concerns over the newly implemented UGC rules, calling them anti-student and harmful to the future of higher education. Reacting to the changes, Rai said that instead of strengthening universities, the new regulations centralise power and reduce the autonomy of educational institutions. He alleged that the government is trying to control universities through policies that ignore ground realities faced by students, teachers, and researchers.

Ajay Rai emphasized that frequent changes in UGC norms regarding appointments, examinations, admissions, and academic structure are creating confusion across campuses. According to him, students from rural and economically weaker backgrounds will be the worst affected, as the rules may increase inequality in access to quality education. He also questioned whether stakeholders like teachers’ associations and student bodies were consulted before framing these regulations.

The Congress leader demanded that the government immediately review the UGC rules and hold wide consultations to protect academic freedom. He stated that education should be a platform for innovation, debate, and inclusive growth—not political control. Rai further warned that if the government fails to amend these rules, opposition parties will continue to raise the issue on the streets and in Parliament.

“Education is the backbone of the nation. Any decision taken without listening to students and teachers will damage the country’s future,” Ajay Rai said.

item.title: Varanasi Launches ‘Zero Waste’ Model Wards Initiative to Make Kashi India’s Cleanest City
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: In a bid to propel Kashi to the top of India's cleanest cities list, the Varanasi Municipal Corporation (Nagar Nigam) has announced a major initiative to transform six selected wards into "Zero Waste" Model Wards.

Key Initiatives: * Mandatory Segregation: Residents in these wards must segregate waste into wet and dry categories at the source. Sanitation workers (Safai Mitras) have been instructed to refuse collection if the waste is not segregated. * High-Tech Monitoring: To ensure 100% coverage, the corporation is utilizing GIS mapping for beat-level staff monitoring and GPS tracking for waste collection vehicles. * Zero Waste Goal: The aim is to process all waste generated in these zones either locally or immediately at processing plants, ensuring no garbage piles up. The city has already eliminated 26 open garbage spots and beautified them. Expansion in New Wards: * The corporation has also streamlined cleaning in the 25 newly expanded wards. * M/s Lion Security Guards Services has been contracted (since December 2025) to handle door-to-door collection in these areas. * Officials confirmed that the city has achieved a daily waste processing capacity of 1,215 tons, a significant milestone for the project.

Isi kram mein Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapeeth (MGKVP) ke chhatron dwara aaj subah 10 baje ek virodh march aur gyaapan mahaprayas ka aayojan kiya ja raha hai. Virodh march ke dauran campus aur aas-paas ke ilaakon mein suraksha ke vishesh intezam kiye gaye hain, taaki koi bhi avaanchit sthiti paida na ho. Chhatron ka kehna hai ki yeh andolan shantipurn aur loktantrik tareeke se kiya ja raha hai, lekin jab tak maangein nahi maani jaati, tab tak awaaz uthti rahegi.

item.title: Pindara Mahotsav| Culture, Marathon & Welfare Events
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi is set to witness a vibrant celebration of culture, tradition, and folk heritage with the grand organization of Pindara Mahotsav 2026, scheduled from 30 January to 01 February 2026. Organized with the support of the Uttar Pradesh Tourism Department, the festival aims to bring the rich folk culture, music, dance, and rural traditions of Varanasi and other regions of Uttar Pradesh to the forefront.

The festival will be inaugurated on 30 January 2026 at 11:00 AM by the Hon’ble Minister of Tourism and Culture, Government of Uttar Pradesh, marking the beginning of a three-day cultural extravaganza. On the opening day itself, a marathon race (for men and women) will also be organized from 9:00 AM to 10:00 AM, adding an element of fitness and social participation to the celebrations.

On 01 February 2026, the District Disability Welfare Department will distribute assistive devices to specially-abled individuals, while under the National Rural Livelihood Mission, sewing machines will be distributed to women beneficiaries to promote self-reliance and empowerment.

The Pindara Mahotsav will also feature exhibitions from various departments including basic education, Anganwadi, health, animal husbandry, agriculture, rural development, and disability welfare, providing information and benefits to the general public.

The cultural evenings will showcase mesmerizing performances by renowned artists and folk groups, presenting folk dances, traditional songs, and classical music, celebrating the artistic diversity of the region. The event promises to be a perfect blend of culture, social welfare, and community participation, strengthening the bond between tradition and development.

item.title: Acid Attack Survivor Prof. Mangala Kapoor Honoured with Padma Shri for Literature and Education
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: In an exclusive conversation with Dalimss News, renowned academician and music scholar Prof. Mangala Kapoor expressed her heartfelt gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the central government for considering her for the prestigious Padma Shri award. Calling it a moment of deep honour, she said the recognition belongs not only to her but to everyone who stood by her during her long and difficult journey.

Recalling the most traumatic phase of her life, Prof. Kapoor revealed that she survived an acid attack at the tender age of 13. The incident left her physically scarred and emotionally shattered. For nearly six years following the attack, she underwent multiple surgeries. During this period, she remained confined to her home, avoiding social interaction and struggling to find the courage to face the world.

“My entire family was worried. I had stopped talking to people and lost all confidence,” she said. It was her parents who encouraged her to take a step towards healing. Her father, recognising her natural inclination towards music and her melodious voice, suggested formal training in music — not as a career plan, but as a way to help her regain confidence and communicate with people again.

https://youtu.be/-PPQrY7MbN0

What began as therapy soon turned into passion. Music became Prof. Kapoor’s emotional refuge, giving her mental peace and strength. Alongside her training in music, she pursued academic studies, completing her BA, MA, and higher education in the field. However, the path was far from easy. She recalled facing insensitive comments and stares from people because of her facial injuries, which often caused emotional distress.

Despite the challenges, Prof. Kapoor went on to build an extraordinary academic career. She joined Mahila Mahavidyalaya, Banaras Hindu University (BHU), as a professor and served the institution for nearly 30 years. During her tenure, numerous students completed their PhDs under her guidance. She has authored five books and is currently working on her sixth, in addition to her autobiography titled Seerat, in which she has documented her life journey.

Prof. Kapoor has also received three state-level awards for her contributions to music and education. Her name being considered for the Padma Shri, she said, is a recognition of perseverance, resilience, and purpose. She added that despite ongoing health challenges, she remains committed to working for the betterment of society.

Reflecting on the emotional toll of her journey, she acknowledged that she battled depression multiple times and faced financial and physical hardships, often without support beyond her immediate family. “No one stood by me except my parents,” she said, adding that her father’s unwavering belief and the healing power of music helped her survive the darkest phases.

“I feel I have lived many lives in one lifetime — first as a victim, then as a fighter, and finally as a professor at BHU,” she said. Prof. Kapoor credited her parents, brother, teachers, and her gurus for their constant support and expressed deep gratitude to Goddess Saraswati for guiding her path.

Speaking strongly against acid attacks, Prof. Kapoor said perpetrators fail to understand the lifelong trauma faced by victims. She called for the strictest possible punishment under the law for those who commit such crimes, so that justice serves as a deterrent.

Ending with a powerful message for acid attack survivors, she said, “Never believe that your life is over. Someone may take away your face and inflict immense pain, but they can never take away your talent. Believe in yourself, hold on to your strength, and keep fighting. You are capable of achieving wonders.”

item.title: Varanasi Students Protest UGC Draft on Caste Discrimination, Academic Activities Disrupted at MGKVP
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: Students in Varanasi staged a strong protest on Wednesday against the University Grants Commission’s (UGC) proposed draft regulation on caste-based discrimination complaints, expressing fears that the new framework could disturb academic harmony if implemented without clear safeguards.

The protest took place at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (MGKVP), where student groups gathered on campus, raised slogans, and briefly disrupted academic activities. Due to the demonstration, parts of the university remained closed for several hours, affecting routine classes and administrative work.

According to protesting students, the draft regulation, in its current form, lacks clarity on key procedural aspects. They argued that the absence of precise legal definitions and a mandatory preliminary inquiry mechanism could lead to confusion and arbitrary action against students and faculty members. Protesters warned that such ambiguity may create fear and mistrust within the academic environment.

Student representatives clarified that their opposition is procedural, not ideological. While acknowledging the importance of addressing caste-based discrimination and ensuring justice for marginalised communities, they stressed that grievance redressal mechanisms must also protect the principles of natural justice and the rights of all stakeholders.

The Varanasi protest is part of a wider national debate on the UGC draft regulation. Legal experts and academics across the country have also raised concerns, stating that unclear rules may discourage free academic engagement and long-term trust within universities. Supporters of the draft, however, argue that stricter regulations are necessary to ensure timely and effective justice in discrimination cases.

Students at MGKVP have now urged the UGC and the central government to hold wider consultations with students, teachers, and legal experts before finalising the regulation. They have demanded amendments that ensure transparency, fairness, and balance, while maintaining a healthy academic atmosphere based on dialogue and mutual trust.

The protest remained peaceful, but student leaders indicated that further demonstrations could follow if their concerns are not addressed.

item.title: Varanasi Students Begin Indefinite Hunger Strike Demanding UGC Rollback, Anshan Crosses 24 Hours
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: Students in Varanasi have launched an indefinite hunger strike demanding the rollback of recent University Grants Commission (UGC) policies, which they claim threaten their academic future. The protest, which entered its 24th hour on Wednesday, has intensified pressure on authorities as students remain firm on their demands despite growing health concerns.

The anshan is being held with placards and slogans highlighting issues of academic pressure, uncertainty, and alleged exclusion under the new UGC norms. Protesters say the policies were introduced without adequate consultation with students and stakeholders, leading to widespread dissatisfaction across campuses.

According to student representatives, the new regulations disproportionately affect students from marginal backgrounds and could undermine equality within the higher education system. “This is not just a protest, it is a fight for our rights, education, and future,” said one of the students participating in the hunger strike.

Despite fatigue and the physical toll of a prolonged fast, the protesting students have refused to call off the anshan. They have appealed to the UGC and the central government to engage in dialogue and reconsider the decisions before the situation worsens.

The protest has remained peaceful so far, but student leaders warned that the movement could expand if their concerns continue to be ignored. With the hunger strike crossing the 24-hour mark, the message from the students is clear — they will not back down until the UGC rollback demand is addressed.

The developments in Varanasi reflect a broader sense of unrest among students nationwide over changes in higher education policies, raising questions about consultation, transparency, and inclusivity in decision-making.

item.title: Swami Avimukteshwaranand Quits Prayagraj Magh Mela After Mauni Amavasya Incident, Targets Yogi Govt
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Prayagraj: Amid the ongoing controversy at the Prayagraj Magh Mela, Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati has taken a significant decision to leave the religious congregation and return to Kashi. The move comes in the aftermath of the Mauni Amavasya incident, which the seer described as deeply hurtful and insulting, holding the administration responsible for the events.

Addressing the media at his camp before departure, Swami Avimukteshwaranand levelled serious allegations against the local administration, accusing it of attempting to placate saints by offering facilities while failing to address the alleged assault and humiliation that took place on Mauni Amavasya. He said the incident caused a deep wound to his conscience and amounted to an attack on his dignity.

The Shankaracharya alleged that instead of acknowledging the wrongdoing, the administration was trying to lure saints with benefits to compromise their principles. “The administration’s intent is still not right. They want to trap us by distributing government favours, but they have not spoken a single word about the violence and insult that occurred,” he said, adding that continuing at the Magh Mela under such circumstances was against his inner conscience.

Taking a sharp dig at Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Swami Avimukteshwaranand said the Mauni Amavasya episode had caused the greatest pain to followers of Sanatan Dharma. “This is the biggest sorrow that Sanatan Dharmis have suffered under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Who will compensate for this pain — which leader or which party — remains to be seen,” he remarked.

Describing the Mauni Amavasya incident as the most painful moment of his life, the seer said the administration appeared unwilling to discuss the alleged crime, while public opinion would ultimately decide the issue. He asserted that the question of victory or defeat would be determined by time and by the judgment of devotees and the general public.

Swami Avimukteshwaranand’s departure has added a new dimension to the controversy surrounding the Magh Mela, intensifying political and religious debate and raising questions over administrative handling of sensitive religious events.

item.title: MGKVP Varanasi Students Protest Against UGC Draft Rule on Caste Discrimination Complaints, Campus Shut
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: Students of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (MGKVP) on Wednesday staged a protest against the University Grants Commission’s (UGC) proposed draft regulation related to handling complaints of caste-based discrimination, forcing the university campus to remain closed for the day.

Raising slogans and carrying placards, protesting students termed the proposed regulation “student-unfriendly” and warned that its current structure could create an atmosphere of fear and mistrust within universities. They alleged that the draft lacks adequate safeguards and may be misused, potentially impacting both students and faculty members.

Student leaders clarified that their opposition is not against addressing caste-based discrimination, which they acknowledged as a serious and sensitive issue, but against what they described as the absence of a balanced and transparent grievance-redressal mechanism. They demanded clear definitions within the regulation, a mandatory preliminary inquiry before action, and safeguards to prevent false or motivated complaints.

“The issue is not about denying justice to victims of discrimination, but about ensuring fairness for all stakeholders,” said one student leader during the protest.

The demonstration comes amid a broader national debate over the draft regulation. Several legal experts and academicians have raised concerns about its compatibility with principles of natural justice, due process, and academic freedom. Critics argue that without proper checks, the regulation could lead to arbitrary action and damage the academic environment.

Supporters of the draft rule, however, maintain that strict provisions are essential to ensure timely justice for marginalised communities and to address long-standing grievances within higher education institutions.

With protests now spreading to university campuses, students at MGKVP have urged the UGC and the central government to hold wider consultations with stakeholders before finalising the regulation. As discussions intensify, the issue underscores the challenge of balancing social justice with fairness, transparency, and trust in India’s higher education system.

item.title: Varanasi Banks Affected as UFBU Leads Protest Demanding 5-Day Work System
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Banking services across Varanasi came to a standstill on Tuesday as bank employees and officers staged a coordinated protest demanding the implementation of a five-day workweek. The demonstration was organized under the banner of the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU), reflecting a nationwide movement against increasing work pressure, staff shortages, and mounting mental stress faced by banking personnel.

The protest was held peacefully outside the State Bank of India’s main branch in the city, where a large number of employees and officers gathered to express their dissatisfaction. Similar demonstrations were also organized at the Union Bank of India’s zonal office at Chandra Tower, highlighting the widespread participation of banking staff from various public sector banks.

Union leaders stated that the demand for a five-day workweek is not new. It has been discussed multiple times in earlier bipartite agreements, and even the Indian Banks’ Association had expressed its agreement in principle. However, despite repeated assurances, the central government has yet to take a final decision, leading to growing frustration among bank employees. Speakers at the protest alleged that promises made to bank staff have remained limited to paperwork, with no concrete implementation on the ground.

Addressing the gathering, union representatives emphasized that bank employees are working under intense pressure due to staff shortages and expanding responsibilities, while continuing to provide uninterrupted services to the public. They argued that a five-day workweek would significantly improve work-life balance, reduce stress, and ultimately enhance the quality and efficiency of banking services.

Union leaders also warned that if their legitimate demands are not addressed soon, the agitation may be intensified and expanded at the national level. They stressed that many government departments and several countries have already adopted a five-day work system, and the banking sector should not be treated differently.

The ongoing agitation has already impacted banking operations, with banks remaining closed for several consecutive days due to holidays and strike-related disruptions. According to union officials, talks held on January 22 and 23 failed to yield any consensus, further escalating the situation. Normal banking operations are expected to resume from January 28, but unions have made it clear that the issue is far from resolved.

The protest remained peaceful throughout, with no reports of untoward incidents. However, the growing unrest among bank employees signals a significant challenge for authorities, as the demand for a five-day banking system continues to gain momentum across the country.

item.title: Varanasi Witnesses Rare Sanskrit Cricket Match as Batuks Bring Tradition to the Pitch
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: In a rare blend of tradition, culture, and modern sport, an extraordinary cricket match was organized in Kashi on Tuesday, capturing the attention of spectators from all walks of life. What made the match truly special was that Sanskrit batuks, dressed in dhoti-kurta, played cricket while wearing kanthi malas, tilak, and tripund, and the entire match commentary was delivered in pure Sanskrit.

The unique event was organized on the occasion of the 82nd foundation day of Shastrarth Mahavidyalaya (Dashashwamedh). This year, the match was hosted at Jai Narayan Inter College ground in Ramapura. Students well-versed in Sanskrit participated in the competition, giving the event a distinctive cultural identity.

Adding to the visual appeal, several batuks appeared on the field dressed in the attire inspired by Chanakya, instantly drawing the curiosity and admiration of the audience. As boundaries and sixes were struck, the Sanskrit commentary echoed across the ground, turning a regular cricket match into a lively cultural spectacle.

The commentators skillfully described every moment of the game in Sanskrit, ensuring that the excitement of the match remained intact while also showcasing the richness of the ancient language. Spectators, including locals and students, were seen enjoying both the sport and the linguistic uniqueness of the event.

Participants said the match was not only about winning or losing but about expressing their love for Sanskrit and Indian traditions through sports. The event successfully demonstrated that Sanskrit is not confined to classrooms or scriptures but can seamlessly connect with contemporary activities like cricket.

Such initiatives, organizers said, help promote sportsmanship while also creating awareness and respect for Sanskrit among the younger generation. The Sanskrit Batuk Cricket Competition stood as a powerful example of how sports can serve as a bridge between culture, tradition, and modern life.

The event left a lasting impression on everyone present, proving that when heritage meets the pitch, the result is both inspiring and unforgettable.

item.title: Varanasi Waste Collection Initiative Struggles with On-Ground Execution
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi Municipal Corporation’s initiative to manage daily garbage through door-to-door collection and QR code tracking is facing significant challenges, with many residents reporting gaps in implementation.

The project, executed in partnership with Varanasi Waste Solution Private Limited, involved installing QR codes at households to track garbage collection. While the system was launched with much fanfare, residents say that in practice, the collection is inconsistent.

Anil Kumar Gupta, a resident of Hanuman Phatak, said, “The QR code was installed at our house last year, but no employee has ever come to scan it or collect garbage. We continue to throw waste in the same spots on the street.” Similarly, Ram Naresh Jaiswal stated that while garbage is occasionally collected from his house, the QR code is never scanned.

Local councillors have raised concerns about the effectiveness of the system. Abhijeet Bhardwaj Laki, councillor from Prahlad Ghat Ward, described the arrangement as “highly inadequate and unsatisfactory.” He said only about 40% of households in his ward have regular garbage collection, while the remaining 60% do not, forcing residents to dump waste on streets and alleys.

Despite multiple complaints to the municipal corporation and even letters sent to higher authorities in Lucknow, Bhardwaj said no effective solution has been implemented. He urged municipal officials to ensure proper collection before releasing payments to the private company responsible.

Former and current councillor of Ward 63, Haji Waqas Ansari, echoed these concerns. He noted that several private companies have been appointed over time, but many collect payments without completing the work. “Across the city, only 30-40% of households are receiving regular door-to-door collection. Meanwhile, the municipal corporation continues to pay large sums, ranging from ₹21 to ₹28 crore, to the implementing agency,” he said.

Ansari also highlighted issues with the digital tracking system. “Supervisors often show daily collection data from PDFs without physically visiting households. Payments are processed based on this, which undermines transparency and accountability.”

Residents and councillors warn that the gap between reported and actual collection affects the city’s cleanliness ranking. “Varanasi is falling behind in cleanliness surveys because ground-level work is not visible, despite efforts from the Prime Minister and Chief Minister at higher levels. Private agencies are taking advantage of this situation,” Ansari added.

The municipal corporation has yet to comment on these reports. With garbage continuing to pile up in streets and alleys, residents and local representatives stress the need for stricter monitoring and more accountable collection processes.

item.title: Varanasi Police Install Awareness Boards Near Kashi Vishwanath Temple to Curb Middlemen, Devotees Urged to Follow Queue System
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: In a major step to protect devotees from cheating and harassment, the Varanasi Police Commissionerate has installed public awareness boards near the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, warning people to remain alert against middlemen operating in the name of temple darshan.

The notice clearly advises devotees to stand in the designated queues and follow the official system for smooth and hassle-free darshan. It also urges pilgrims not to fall prey to brokers who demand money in exchange for special or faster entry.

To strengthen enforcement and quick grievance redressal, contact numbers of senior police officials including the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Station House Officer, and the local outpost in-charge of Dashashwamedh have been prominently displayed on the boards. Devotees have been encouraged to immediately report any suspicious activity or involvement of middlemen.

Police officials stated that this initiative aims to ensure a safe, fair, and transparent darshan system, especially during peak pilgrimage days, weekends, and festivals when heavy crowds are witnessed near the temple premises.

The move has been welcomed by pilgrims, who said that such steps will help maintain order and improve the overall experience at one of the country’s most revered religious sites.

item.title: Varanasi BJP Booth President Resigns, Calls UGC Law Harmful for Future Generations
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
In a significant political development from Varanasi, opposition to the proposed UGC law has surfaced within the Bharatiya Janata Party. BJP booth president Vikas Kumar Mishra from Pachraon booth under Chiraigaon Mandal resigned from his post, protesting against the law and calling it harmful to future generations.

Vikas Mishra submitted his resignation letter to the BJP mandal president, stating that he was completely opposed to the party’s support for laws such as the UGC Act and the SC/ST Act. He described these legislations as divisive and against his social, moral, and ideological principles. According to him, continuing in the position would go against his self-respect and conscience.

Mishra, whose family has long been associated with the BJP, said he had raised concerns with several party leaders before resigning but received no clear response. Following the resignation, he claimed pressure was mounted on him to withdraw and delete the letter. The resignation letter was later shared by him on social media platforms, triggering mixed reactions from users.

He further alleged that the proposed law could lead to harassment of upper-caste students and demanded provisions against false complaints. BJP booth-level members supporting him warned that if the bill is not withdrawn, protests could intensify. The incident highlights growing internal dissent within the BJP over the UGC-related legislation in Uttar Pradesh.

item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
In a major development linked to the Varanasi codeine cough syrup case, police have arrested Vikas Singh Narve, a close associate of main accused Shubham Jaiswal. Vikas was apprehended near the Nepal border in Siddharthnagar while allegedly trying to flee the country.

A special team of the Varanasi Police carried out the operation. Officials said a lookout notice and red corner notice had already been issued against him. After the arrest, police began the process of bringing Vikas Singh Narve to Varanasi for further interrogation.

According to investigators, Vikas had played a key role in introducing Shubham Jaiswal to Amit Singh Tata and also facilitated meetings with a dismissed constable. Police believe his arrest could lead to more disclosures in the ongoing smuggling investigation.

Repeating the sentiment of “Old is Gold,” fans said Sunny Deol’s powerful and screen presence and iconic patriotic roles still dominate their hearts, even as the sequel introduces new performances.

item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi, the eternal city on the banks of the sacred Ganga, continues to blend tradition with creativity as artists transform ghat-side walls into vibrant works of art. Through colorful murals and detailed paintings, the stories of Kashi’s rich cultural heritage, spiritual traditions, and everyday life are being brought alive for devotees, tourists, and locals alike.

This artistic initiative not only enhances the visual appeal of the ghats but also serves as a powerful medium to preserve history and convey social messages. From depictions of ancient rituals and saints to reflections of harmony, cleanliness, and heritage conservation, each artwork tells a story rooted in the soul of Varanasi.

As the city witnesses a growing influx of visitors from across India and the world, these paintings create a deeper emotional connection between people and the ghats, turning the riverfront into an open-air art gallery. Such efforts highlight how art can play a meaningful role in urban beautification while respecting the spiritual essence of one of the world’s oldest living cities.

Through creativity and tradition walking hand in hand, Varanasi once again proves that its heritage is not just preserved in temples and scriptures, but also painted on its walls for future generations to see, feel, and remember.

item.title: Varanasi’s Khushi Singh Wins Silver and Bronze at National Muay Thai Championship 2026
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: Khushi Singh from Varanasi delivered an impressive performance at the 7th UMAI National Senior Muay Thai Championship 2026, winning one silver and one bronze medal. The championship was held in Hyderabad, Telangana, from January 22 to January 25, 2026, and witnessed participation from top senior athletes across the country.

Khushi Singh is the daughter of Tej Bahadur Singh and hails from Shrirampur Siyaraha village under Pindra block of Varanasi district. The national-level event was organized by the United Muay Thai Association of India (UMAI) in collaboration with the Telangana Amateur Muay Thai Association (TAMTA), with the aim of promoting Muay Thai martial arts and providing a competitive platform for senior players.

Athletes from various states competed across different weight categories, including WWC and WMC title fights. Khushi’s success is the result of her hard work, dedication, and rigorous training. Her achievement has brought pride not only to her family but also to her village and the entire Varanasi district.

Her journey stands as a strong message that girls from small villages can excel at the national level. Khushi Singh’s performance has emerged as a source of inspiration for young athletes aspiring to make their mark in sports.

item.title: Grand Preparations Underway for Guru Ravidas Jayanti at Seer Govardhanpur, Varanasi
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: Preparations for the birth anniversary of Sant Shiromani Shri Guru Ravidas are in full swing at Seer Govardhanpur in Varanasi. Ahead of the main celebration scheduled on February 1, sevadars from Punjab and Haryana have arrived in large numbers to manage arrangements for devotees coming from across the country and abroad.

Large community kitchens have started functioning near the Guru Ravidas temple, where Punjabi sweets and traditional snacks such as boondi and mathri are being prepared by skilled cooks brought specially from Punjab and Haryana. Trucks loaded with grains, oil, ghee, and spices have reached the site, while fresh vegetables have been procured directly from nearby villages, benefiting local farmers as well.

For satsang and religious gatherings, a German hanger pandal is being set up. Security arrangements have been strengthened with around 200 CCTV cameras installed from the temple to the pandal area, along with police deployment and metal detector checks at entry points. Temporary police posts, health camps, and fire brigade vehicles have also been arranged to ensure the safety and convenience of devotees during the grand celebrations.

item.title: High Alert Ahead of Republic Day 2026
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal_
item.content:encoded:
High Security Alert Issued Ahead of Republic Day 2026, Agencies Warn of Possible Terror Threat

Varanasi / Lucknow: Security agencies across the country have been placed on high alert ahead of Republic Day 2026 following fresh intelligence inputs indicating a possible terror threat aimed at disrupting national celebrations.

According to the inputs, terror groups are allegedly planning coordinated, high-impact attacks in multiple regions of India with the intention of creating panic and disturbing Republic Day events. The intelligence assessment suggests that the conspiracy involves targeting key locations in Delhi, Jammu & Kashmir, and other sensitive areas, while religious and high-footfall locations are also believed to be on the radar.

The alert mentions that the operation, reportedly code-named “26-26”, is aimed at executing attacks around January 26, coinciding with Republic Day celebrations. Security agencies have been advised to strengthen surveillance, enhance monitoring, and ensure strict implementation of safety protocols across airports, railway stations, public places, government buildings, and major event venues.

In view of the potential threat, all concerned departments and stakeholders have been directed to maintain heightened vigilance, increase patrolling, and conduct thorough checks. Security arrangements at sensitive installations have been reviewed, and additional forces have been deployed in critical zones.

Authorities have also emphasized the importance of inter-agency coordination, real-time intelligence sharing, and rapid response mechanisms to prevent any untoward incident. Emergency response teams and disaster management units have been placed on standby to ensure quick action if required.

Security agencies have appealed to the public to remain alert, avoid spreading rumours, and immediately report any suspicious activity to local authorities. Citizens have also been advised to cooperate with security checks and follow safety instructions during Republic Day events.

item.title: Bike Stolen in Phulpur Area, FIR Filed After 9 Days
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal_
item.content:encoded:
A bike theft case has come to light in the Phulpur police station area of Varanasi, where an FIR was registered nine days after the incident. The theft occurred on January 15, 2026, when the victim had gone to watch a local match.

Kuldeep Pankaj, a resident of Barji village (Bharawar), said he parked his motorcycle after locking it in Surahi (Govardhanpur) and went to watch the match. When he returned, the bike was missing. Despite searching, no trace was found. The stolen motorcycle also had registration, insurance, and other important documents inside it.

Police have registered the case under Section 303(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023. Phulpur SHO Inspector Atul Kumar Singh said the FIR was lodged after receiving the written complaint and that efforts are underway to trace the bike and identify the thief. The investigation is currently ongoing.

Khadi, once a tool of resistance, today stands tall as a mark of sustainability, tradition, and national unity.

As the Indian flag flutters high, it tells a story of courage, resilience, and hope — from the struggle for independence to the vision of a self-reliant India. Every thread of Khadi reflects simplicity with strength, and every colour of the Tricolour echoes the values of peace, progress, and patriotism. item.title: Varanasi on High Alert After Cartridge Found at Airport
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi has been placed on high alert after a cartridge was recovered from a passenger during routine security screening at Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, just days before Republic Day.

The incident has heightened concerns as security agencies across the country remain on maximum vigilance in view of January 26.

According to officials, the passenger, identified as Wasim Akram, a resident of Akbarpur in Bihar, was scheduled to travel from Varanasi to Delhi on an Air India Express flight and onward to Dammam, Saudi Arabia. After the boarding pass was issued, CISF personnel detected a cartridge in his baggage during security screening. The passenger was immediately stopped from travelling and taken for questioning.

Following preliminary inquiry, the matter was handed over to the local police. Multiple agencies, including the police, Intelligence Bureau, LIU and other intelligence units, are now jointly investigating how the cartridge came into the passenger’s possession. Authorities have stated that all angles are being examined, and the investigation is ongoing to rule out any security lapse or larger threat.

item.title: BHU Opens MBA Admissions 2026–27, Apply Till January 31
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal_
item.content:encoded:
Banaras Hindu University (BHU) has started the admission process for MBA and MBA-IB courses for the academic session 2026–27. Eligible candidates can register till January 31. Admissions will be conducted for around 120 seats across both programmes, strictly based on CAT 2025 scores.

Candidates must have appeared in the CAT 2025 examination to be considered. A minimum of 50 percent marks in graduation is required for General category applicants, while SC and ST candidates need at least 45 percent. The final selection will be based on CAT score, followed by Group Discussion and Personal Interview.

Applicants have been advised to ensure that personal details entered during registration match those provided in the CAT application. Required documents include academic mark sheets, certificates, and relevant supporting documents. The registration fee is ₹2000 for General and OBC candidates and ₹1000 for SC and ST candidates.

item.title: DM Satyendra Kumar Highlights Road Connectivity Push in Varanasi
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal_
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar, in an exclusive interaction with Dalimss News, shared key insights into the ongoing and upcoming infrastructure development projects aimed at transforming road connectivity across Varanasi. He said that multiple road expansion, widening, and new connectivity projects are being implemented to ensure smoother traffic flow, reduce congestion, and improve overall commuting experience for residents and visitors alike.

Highlighting the impact of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, the DM said that the project has emerged as a major catalyst for economic growth in the city. “After the completion of the corridor, tourism has witnessed a significant rise, which has directly benefited local businesses, traders, hotel owners, transport operators, and small vendors. The entire ecosystem related to tourism and commerce has received a strong boost,” he stated.

Satyendra Kumar further added that the administration is working on an integrated development model where road infrastructure, parking facilities, pedestrian-friendly zones, and public transport systems are being upgraded simultaneously. Special focus is being given to improving connectivity to major religious, cultural, and commercial hubs to facilitate smooth movement and enhance the city’s global image.

The DM also said that coordination between various departments is being strengthened to ensure timely execution of projects. “Our objective is to build a modern, efficient, and sustainable infrastructure network while preserving the cultural and spiritual heritage of Kashi,” he said.

He expressed confidence that these initiatives will not only ease daily commuting but also contribute significantly to the long-term economic and tourism growth of Varanasi, further establishing it as a world-class spiritual and cultural destination.

item.title: Varanasi to Get World-Class Sports Township Near Ganjari Stadium
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal_
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: In a major boost to sports infrastructure and urban development, District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar has announced ambitious plans to develop a world-class sports township near Ganjari Stadium. Speaking exclusively to Dalimss News, the DM shared key details of the project aimed at transforming Varanasi into a modern sports and connectivity hub.

He said that an inbuilt parking facility for 500 vehicles is being developed at Ganjari Stadium to ensure smooth traffic management and convenience for spectators during large sporting events.

The District Magistrate further informed that the Varanasi Development Authority (VDA) is actively working on developing new areas to improve city connectivity, and that the land acquisition process is already underway for these projects.

Highlighting the larger vision, Satyendra Kumar stated that the areas surrounding the stadium will be developed into a high-end sports township, featuring premium hotels, high-class parking facilities, sports academies, training centres, and multiple sports-related amenities.

“The aim is to build a complete sports ecosystem in Varanasi, capable of hosting national and international events, while offering world-class facilities to athletes and visitors,” he said.

The project is also expected to create employment opportunities, boost tourism, and strengthen the local economy, giving a significant push to overall urban development.

With this initiative, Varanasi is poised to emerge as a major destination for sports, tourism, and modern infrastructure development, while preserving its rich cultural identity.

item.title: Varanasi Police Launch ‘Police Suraksha Mitra’ Program to Boost Public Participation in Crime Prevention
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi Police has launched a new public safety initiative aimed at strengthening community participation in preventing crime and unlawful activities. Under the “Police Suraksha Mitra” program, citizens can now share information related to suspicious or illegal activities directly with the police in a safe, confidential, and user-friendly manner.

The initiative allows people to report issues such as illegal arms, drug trafficking, liquor smuggling, crimes against women and children, forced religious conversion, human trafficking, and other unlawful activities without revealing their identity. To make the process easier, a dedicated WhatsApp Bot number and QR code have been introduced, enabling citizens to send messages, photos, videos, or voice notes instantly.

Police officials have assured that the identity of informants will remain completely confidential and secure. Every credible input received through this platform will be promptly reviewed, and necessary legal action will be taken by the concerned authorities. Updates regarding action taken will also be shared with the informant through WhatsApp wherever possible.

Through this step, the police administration is appealing to the public to come forward, stay alert, and actively cooperate in maintaining law and order.

The initiative reflects the commitment of Varanasi Police to build a safer, crime-free, and peaceful society with the support of responsible citizens.

The officer further stated that investigators are focusing on tracking the financial proceeds allegedly generated through the illegal trade.

He said further legal action will depend on the outcome of the ongoing investigation and subsequent directions from the court.

item.title: Kashi Vishwanath Tilakotsav Preparations Begin, Centuries-Old Tradition Revived in Varanasi
item.dc:creator: shambhavi_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI, UTTAR PRADESH: Kashi is all set to dive into devotion as preparation for Tilakotsav of Baba Vishwanath begins on the occasion of Basant Panchami. According to centuries old tradition, the ceremonial tilak of the Panchbadan movable idol of Baba Vishwanath is performed every year on Basant Panchami at the former Mahant’s residence located at Tedinim. This ritual is observed as “Lokachar” in which the entire city symbolically participates in offering auspicious blessings to the deity.

This year, for the first time, the responsibility of organising the Tilakotsav has been taken up by the Mahant’s family of the Siddhapeeth Badi Sheetla Mata Mandir at Dashashwamedh. With this the series of traditional rituals associated with the divine wedding of Baba Vishwanath will formally commence. These rituals continue until Rangbhari Ekadashi, when the goddess Gauri’s gaunna to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple is celebrated.

According to Up-Mahant Avshesh Pandey (Kallu Maharaj), the honour of organising Tilakotsav is given to a different Kashi resident family every year and this time it has been given to the Badi Sheetla Mata Mandir Family. On Thursday, all ceremonial items will be brought from the temple to the Shri Yantra Peeth at Bhasphatak, from where the traditional rituals will begin on Friday evening at an auspicious time.

The event will feature special worship by 11 Vedic Brahmins, accompanied by the sound of auspicious shehnai. The Tilakotsav will be performed before the evening Saptarshi Aarti at the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, marking the spiritual beginning of Baba Vishwanath’s wedding festivals in Kashi.

item.title: AAP MP Sanjay Singh’s Varanasi Padyatra Ends, FIR Over Manikarnika Ghat Remarks Sparks Controversy
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Aam Aadmi Party’s Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh intensified his attack on the BJP from Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s parliamentary constituency, Varanasi, after concluding his “Rojgaar Do, Samajik Nyay Do” padyatra in the city.

Addressing the media after the padyatra, Sanjay Singh alleged that unemployment, rising inflation and social injustice have become the biggest issues facing the country, but raising these concerns is now being treated as a crime. He said that his padyatra aimed to give voice to unemployed youth, marginalized communities and those who feel excluded from the government’s development narrative.

The political temperature in Kashi rose further after an FIR was registered against Sanjay Singh following his remarks questioning the alleged damage to temples during development work at Manikarnika Ghat, one of Hinduism’s holiest cremation grounds. Singh had publicly raised concerns over religious structures being affected in the name of development, triggering sharp reactions from the ruling party.

Calling the FIR an attempt to silence the opposition, Singh said, “If asking questions about employment and religious heritage leads to FIRs, then democracy itself is in danger.” He accused the BJP government of using police action to suppress dissent, especially when opposition leaders raise uncomfortable questions in politically sensitive regions like Varanasi.

Sanjay Singh also linked the controversy to the upcoming panchayat elections, claiming that the BJP is rattled by growing ground-level discontent. According to him, the padyatra received strong public response, indicating that issues of employment and social justice are resonating even in the Prime Minister’s stronghold.

The BJP, however, has rejected the allegations, maintaining that development work in Kashi is being carried out with respect for religious traditions and accusing the opposition of politicizing sensitive issues for electoral gains.

item.title: Live Cartridge Found in Passenger’s Bag at Varanasi Airport, CISF Foils Security Breach
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
A live cartridge was recovered from a passenger’s bag during routine security screening at Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport in Varanasi, causing a brief security alert. The passenger, identified as Wasim Akram, a resident of Rohtas district in Bihar, was scheduled to travel to Delhi by an Air India Express flight and later board a connecting flight to Dammam, Saudi Arabia.

CISF personnel noticed a suspicious object in the bag during scanner checks and found the live cartridge on manual inspection. The passenger could not provide any valid licence or explanation for carrying the ammunition. He was immediately stopped from flying and detained for questioning.

Airport authorities informed local police, intelligence agencies, and the LIU. Wasim Akram was later handed over to Babatpur police, who are investigating whether the cartridge belonged to a licensed weapon or if there was any criminal intent. The passenger remains in police custody, and the inquiry is ongoing.

item.title: Ajay Rai Attacks Modi–Yogi Govt in Varanasi, Calls It Anti-Sanatan.
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai launched a sharp political attack on the Modi–Yogi government during a program held in Varanasi, accusing the ruling dispensation of being anti-Sanatan and insensitive towards religious traditions.

In support of Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati, Congress workers led by Ajay Rai performed a ceremonial cow worship at a gaushala near the historic Ishwargangi pond. The party took a pledge to protect cows and uphold Sanatan values.

Speaking to the media after the ritual, Ajay Rai said the Congress party stands firmly with Gau Mata, saints, Sanatan traditions, and cultural heritage protected by Lokmata Ahilyabai. He alleged that the insult of Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand and repeated attacks on Sanatan faith prove that the Modi and Yogi governments are anti-Sanatan.

He termed it shameful that a revered religious leader like Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand, who has dedicated his life to spreading knowledge and spiritual values, is being forced to prove his identity. Rai said it reflects poorly on the government’s attitude towards saints and religious institutions.

Targeting the BJP further, Ajay Rai alleged that police action against young priests and elderly saints is condemnable. He claimed that despite projecting itself as a protector of cows, Uttar Pradesh has become the largest exporter of beef, calling it a clear contradiction between the government’s words and actions.

Rai also raised concerns over the beautification of Manikarnika Ghat, stating that its original spiritual essence has been damaged in the name of development. He described the ghat as a global center of Sanatan faith and a sacred gateway to salvation.

Questioning the state government, he demanded clarity on claims related to an idol-linked video allegedly being AI-generated. He said the government must present concrete evidence and disclose the whereabouts of the idol, as ministers and officials themselves had earlier admitted damage to it.

He clarified that the Kumbha Mahadev Temple, along with idols of Nandi and Lord Ganesha, is completely safe, and the statue of Rani Ahilyabai has been preserved and will be reinstalled after project completion.

item.title: Ajay Rai Raises Questions on Manikarnika Ghat AI Video.
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
The controversy surrounding the redevelopment of Varanasi’s Manikarnika Ghat has taken a political turn, with Congress leader Ajay Rai raising fresh questions over the government’s claims and extending support to Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand.

Speaking to Dalimss News during his visit to Varanasi, Rai questioned the state government’s assertion regarding an alleged AI-generated video linked to the Manikarnika Ghat issue. He demanded greater transparency, asking the Uttar Pradesh government to clarify where and how the investigation into the video is being conducted.

“The government should clearly state which laboratory is examining the so-called AI-generated video,” Rai said, adding that vague claims without technical disclosure only deepen public mistrust. Alongside the Manikarnika Ghat matter, the Congress leader also expressed solidarity with Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand, who has recently been at the centre of a controversy during the Prayagraj Magh Mela. Rai described the situation as a matter of respect for religious institutions and said that issues involving saints and spiritual leaders should be handled with sensitivity rather than confrontation.

Rai maintained that Manikarnika Ghat is not merely a redevelopment site but a living symbol of Kashi’s religious, cultural, and historical continuity. According to him, any intervention at such a sacred location must involve consultation with stakeholders connected to the ghat, including priests, traditional workers, and local residents.

The state administration, however, has reiterated that redevelopment work at Manikarnika Ghat is being carried out under established guidelines and that heritage elements are being preserved. Officials have also stated that appropriate action is being taken in accordance with the law regarding the disputed video. The developments highlight a broader debate unfolding in Varanasi — balancing modernization with heritage preservation, and managing religious sensitivities amid large-scale urban transformation.

item.title: Varanasi Meat Ban Debate Divides Youth and Residents
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi Meat Ban Debate: Mixed Opinions from Kashi’s Youth and Residents

Varanasi, known globally for its deep spiritual roots and cultural heritage, is currently witnessing a growing debate over the proposed ban on non-vegetarian food in the city. The issue has sparked strong and diverse reactions from local residents, especially the youth, reflecting a clear divide in public opinion.

A section of people believes that Varanasi is a sacred city and its religious identity should be protected at all costs. According to them, non-vegetarian food should be strictly prohibited, particularly because the city is home to major temples and attracts millions of devotees every year. They argue that a complete ban would help preserve the spiritual atmosphere of Kashi.

Another group, however, strongly disagrees with the idea of a city-wide ban. Many youths feel that food choice is a personal matter and banning non-vegetarian food across Varanasi would be unfair. They point out that the city is not only a religious centre but also a living, modern city where people from different communities, cultures, and backgrounds reside. For them, a blanket ban could affect livelihoods linked to food businesses and limit personal freedom.

There is also a middle-ground opinion gaining attention. Several residents suggest that non-vegetarian food should not be sold or transported in temple zones and heritage areas, out of respect for religious sentiments. At the same time, they believe that other residential and commercial areas should remain unaffected, allowing people to follow their own lifestyle choices without interference.

As the debate continues, it is evident that the people of Varanasi are seeking a balanced approach—one that respects religious beliefs while also acknowledging diversity, employment concerns, and individual freedom. The final decision, many feel, should come after dialogue, sensitivity, and consideration of all viewpoints, so that Kashi’s spiritual identity and social harmony both remain intact.

item.title: Vasant Panchami to Be Celebrated on January 23 in Varanasi
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: The auspicious festival of Vasant Panchami, dedicated to Goddess Saraswati, will be celebrated on January 23, 2026, marking the arrival of spring and the celebration of knowledge and arts.

According to Prof. Bihari Lal Sharma, VC of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, the Magh Shukla Panchami Tithi begins at 2:29 AM on January 23 and will remain effective until 1:46 AM on January 24. Based on the Udaya Tithi (sunrise rule), the festival will be observed on January 23. The most auspicious window for Saraswati Puja and Vidyarambh (initiating education) is from 07:56 AM to 01:59 PM on January 23. This year, the festival coincides with the Sun in Capricorn (Makar) and Moon in Pisces (Meen), along with Purva Bhadrapada Nakshatra and Shiva Yoga, creating a highly beneficial alignment for intellectual pursuits.

Aam Aadmi Party leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh has launched a sharp attack on the Modi–Yogi government, asserting that his party will not be silenced despite alleged pressure through FIRs or imprisonment.

In a strong statement, Sanjay Singh said that even if the government registers an FIR every day or sends opposition leaders to jail, they will continue to speak the truth. He emphasized that the voice of the people will remain loud from Parliament to the streets.

Targeting the government over alleged favoritism towards big corporate houses, Singh accused it of handing over land and lakhs of trees to the Adani Group at throwaway prices. He said the struggle against such policies would continue and claimed that the truth cannot be suppressed.

The AAP leader reiterated that his party stands firmly with the public and will keep raising issues of public interest, regardless of political pressure or legal action.

item.title: UP Board Changes Answer Sheet Format to Curb Fraud.
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal_
item.content:encoded:
The Uttar Pradesh Madhyamik Shiksha Parishad (UP Board) has introduced major changes in its examination system to make board exams more transparent, secure, and well-organized. For the first time, answer sheets used in the upcoming High School and Intermediate examinations will be in a vertical format.

According to board officials, the new answer books will have a redesigned layout. Earlier, answer sheets were printed in landscape format, but now they will be vertical. Each answer book will include two cover pages. The first cover page will carry the UP Board logo, while the last page will feature a special security code to strengthen the evaluation process.

To further enhance security, the first and second answer books will be printed in different colors, helping examiners during evaluation. Every copy will also carry a barcode and a unique code, ensuring confidentiality of student identity while preventing tampering and misuse. The board believes this step will effectively curb irregularities and fraud during assessment.

The UP Board Secretary stated that the objective of these changes is to improve the examination system and ensure fair and unbiased evaluation for students. Special attention has also been given to stitching, page numbering, and print quality of the answer sheets to eliminate the possibility of page replacement or manipulation.

In addition, the board has released subject-wise PDFs for Class 10 in Science, Mathematics, and English. These PDFs provide details on question paper patterns, mark distribution, and important chapters, helping students prepare better for the exams. Board officials said this initiative is aimed at improving student convenience and overall result quality.

item.title: Online Trading Scam Cheats Varanasi Man of Nearly ₹30 Lakh
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
A case of large-scale fraud in the name of online trading and gaming investment has come to light in Varanasi. Sanjay Kumar Patel, a resident of Bhaupur village under the Jansa police station area, has filed a complaint against five individuals, accusing them of cheating him of nearly ₹30 lakh.

According to the complaint, the accused identified as Baba Prajapati, Poonam Prajapati, Jayesh, Suraj, and Suresh were frequent visitors to Sanjay’s mobile repairing shop. During casual interactions, they introduced themselves as operators of a trading and gaming company. They allegedly promised investors a monthly return of six percent along with complete security of the principal amount.

Trusting their claims, Sanjay invested money over a period of two years and transferred a total of ₹17.14 lakh online into different bank accounts of the accused. He also encouraged his acquaintances to invest, following which one of his friends invested around ₹17 lakh in the same accounts.

Problems began when investors demanded the return of their money. The accused initially avoided repayment and, after repeated pressure, returned only ₹5.50 lakh, refusing to pay the remaining amount. They continued to assure Sanjay that the money would be returned soon or adjusted against property.

Later, the accused claimed they would transfer ownership of a piece of land in Mohansarai in Sanjay’s name and demanded ₹20,000 for preparing registration documents. Despite receiving this amount through online transfer, neither the land was registered nor was the pending money returned.

When Sanjay pressed for repayment, the accused allegedly abused him and issued threats of serious consequences. As per the complaint, Sanjay was cheated of ₹18.22 lakh, while his friend Sujit Kumar Singh lost ₹11.88 lakh.

Taking cognizance of the matter, Jansa police have registered an FIR against all five accused under sections related to cheating, abuse, and criminal intimidation. Police officials stated that the bank accounts linked to the accused are being examined and legal action will be taken based on the findings.

item.title: From Kashi Streets to Global Plates: Banarasi Food Goes International
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal_
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi, the cultural and spiritual heart of India, is now preparing to make its mark on the global culinary map. The city’s iconic traditional foods—Banarasi kachori, launglata, tricolour barfi, thandai and Banarasi paan—are set to gain international recognition under the state government’s One District One Cuisine (ODOC) initiative.

The initiative, inspired by the One District One Product (ODOP) model, aims to transform local cuisines into globally recognised brands while ensuring sustainable livelihoods for traditional sweet makers, food artisans and small entrepreneurs. Through structured branding, modern packaging, quality control and marketing support, Banaras’s culinary heritage will be positioned for national and international markets. As part of the programme, Banaras’s signature dishes will be showcased at a special stall during the Uttar Pradesh Day celebrations in Lucknow, offering visitors a taste of the city’s rich food culture. Officials believe this platform will help finalise the district’s cuisine selection under ODOC and introduce the flavours of Kashi to a wider audience. A key focus of the initiative is maintaining authenticity while upgrading standards. Emphasis will be placed on food safety, hygiene, quality certification and compliance with food safety norms. The government also plans to promote GI tagging to protect the originality and cultural identity of Banaras’s traditional recipes. Each dish will carry a product story highlighting its cultural roots, historical background and traditional preparation methods. This approach aims to offer consumers not just a food product, but an experience rooted in Banaras’s heritage. The ODOC initiative is expected to create new economic opportunities for local vendors and artisans, enabling them to expand beyond local markets while preserving age-old culinary traditions. For consumers, it promises access to safe, high-quality traditional flavours that reflect the true essence of Kashi. With this move, Banaras is poised to be recognised not only as a centre of spirituality and culture, but also as a city whose flavours travel from local streets to global plates.

item.title: Retired Railway Employee Duped of ₹23 Lakh in Varanasi
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal_
item.content:encoded:
A retired railway employee in Varanasi was allegedly duped of ₹23 lakh by cyber fraudsters who posed as Crime Branch officials and kept him under so-called “digital arrest” for nearly 24 hours. The victim’s son, a doctor, has lodged an FIR at Sigra police station in connection with the incident.

According to the complaint filed by Dr Chandan Kishor, his father Raghunandan Prasad, a retired railway employee, received a WhatsApp call on December 25, 2025. The caller claimed that a mobile number linked to his Aadhaar card had been used in a money laundering case and that an FIR had been registered in Mumbai. He was told that senior officials would contact him shortly.

Soon after, a video call came from a number displaying a police logo. The caller introduced himself as an officer from the Mumbai Crime Branch and threatened legal action, including jail and heavy fines. The victim was instructed not to speak to anyone during the “investigation” and was warned of serious consequences if he disobeyed.

When Raghunandan Prasad denied any involvement, the fraudsters insisted that he come to Mumbai to submit a written statement. On expressing his inability to travel, he was further intimidated and misled. He was then instructed to transfer all the money from his bank account to another account until the inquiry was completed.

Under pressure and fear, on December 26, the retired employee transferred ₹23 lakh through RTGS to a bank account in Guwahati. The fraud came to light when his son learned about the incident and immediately lodged a complaint on the cyber crime helpline, followed by a written complaint at Sigra police station.

Sigra Station House Officer Sanjay Mishra confirmed that a case has been registered under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. He said cyber experts have been roped in to trace the accused and assured that efforts are underway to arrest the fraudsters at the earliest.

item.title: New Fire Station to Come Up in Phulpur Village of Varanasi
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal_
item.content:encoded:
A new fire station will be constructed in Phulpur village under the Chaubepur police station area of Varanasi district. The project has been initiated following the efforts of Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Minister Anil Rajbhar, with the aim of ensuring quick response to fire-related emergencies in the region.

On Wednesday, a team of administrative officials and fire department officers visited Phulpur to inspect the proposed government land. During the visit, officials carried out land measurement and assessed the technical feasibility required for establishing the fire station. Senior officers also issued necessary guidelines regarding the construction plan.

For a long time, residents of Phulpur and nearby villages had been demanding a permanent fire station in the area. At present, in case of major fire incidents, people have to depend on fire stations located at the district headquarters or far-off areas, leading to delays. The new fire station is expected to significantly improve response time and help protect lives and property.

According to departmental sources, the inspection process has been completed successfully. The fire station will be built on 33 bissa of land. Cabinet Minister Anil Rajbhar is expected to lay the foundation stone of the project soon.

The initiative, taken with the support of Phulpur village head Vishal Singh Chauhan, has been welcomed by local residents, who expressed their gratitude to the minister for addressing a long-pending demand.
