item.title: Varanasi Republic Day Parade to Highlight Women Empowerment.
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi is gearing up for Republic Day celebrations with a strong focus on women empowerment. The Varanasi Police Commissionerate has begun final preparations for the grand parade to be held on January 26, 2026, with this year’s theme centered on showcasing women power.

On Tuesday, Police Commissioner Mohit Agrawal inspected the parade rehearsals at the Police Lines campus. During the inspection, he reviewed discipline, drill, turnout, and overall arrangements, and issued clear instructions to ensure the event remains dignified, well-organized, and inspiring.

The Republic Day parade will feature tableaux based on women empowerment, highlighting the role of women in society and law enforcement. A contingent of women Black Commandos and women mounted police will also participate, symbolizing courage, strength, and discipline.

To honor women police personnel, special events have been planned. On the instructions of the Police Commissioner, a felicitation dinner will be organized on January 26 at 4 pm at his residence for the parade commander, the in-charge of the Women Power Center, and police personnel who delivered outstanding performance in 2025. Additionally, a special screening of the film “Border-2” will be held at 7 pm the same day for all women police personnel to boost their morale.

Cultural programs during the event will blend patriotism with the message of women empowerment. Street plays are also planned to spread a strong social message among the public.

During the inspection, the Police Commissioner also reviewed cleanliness, residential facilities, ongoing construction work, and the maintenance of the newly built museum within the Police Lines campus. He directed officials to further strengthen entry-exit management, CCTV surveillance, lighting, and overall security.

Senior officials including DCP Lines Pramod Kumar, ADCP Lines Vaibhav Bangar, ADCP Women Crime Namrata Srivastava, ADCP/ACP Lines Dr Ishan Soni, ACP (U/T) Mansi Dahiya, along with other officers and personnel, were present during the inspection.

According to the announced schedule, power supply from the Sigra feeder will remain suspended from 11:00 am to 12:00 noon. After this, the Bank Colony feeder will be shut down from 12:00 noon to 1:00 pm. Electricity supply from the Jai Prakash Nagar feeder will also be affected between 1:00 pm and 2:00 pm.

The electricity department has advised consumers to complete important tasks in advance during the shutdown period. Officials said power supply will be restored immediately after the maintenance work is completed.

item.title: Magh Mela Row: Jagatguru Rambhadracharya Defends UP Govt After Notice to Swami Avimukteshwaranand
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Prayagraj: The controversy surrounding the administrative notice served to spiritual leader Swami Avimukteshwaranand during the ongoing Magh Mela has taken a new turn, with Jagatguru Rambhadracharya issuing a strong statement in support of the Uttar Pradesh government and local police authorities.

Addressing the media, Rambhadracharya dismissed claims of administrative excess, stating that no injustice had been committed against Swami Avimukteshwaranand. “He was not subjected to injustice; rather, he has done injustice,” Rambhadracharya remarked, countering allegations that the administration had overstepped its authority.

Clarifying long-standing traditions and regulations associated with the Magh Mela and the Sangam area, Rambhadracharya explained that access to the Ganga ghats is governed by specific customary and administrative norms. “One cannot travel to the Ganga ghat using a chariot,” he stated, emphasizing that even senior spiritual leaders traditionally walk to the Sangam during the holy congregation.

He further defended the police action that stopped the Swami’s vehicle, asserting that the steps taken were in accordance with established rules meant to maintain order and safety during the massive religious gathering. Rambhadracharya also termed the administrative notice issued by the Uttar Pradesh government as “absolutely right.”

The statement has added fuel to an already intensifying debate within religious and political circles. Supporters of Swami Avimukteshwaranand have criticized the administration’s move, calling it an infringement on religious freedom, while others argue that maintaining discipline and uniformity during the Magh Mela is essential given the scale of the event.

Officials from the Uttar Pradesh administration have reiterated that all actions taken were lawful and necessary to ensure smooth conduct of the Magh Mela, which draws millions of devotees from across the country.

As reactions continue to pour in, the incident highlights the delicate balance between religious tradition and administrative regulation at one of India’s largest spiritual gatherings. The unfolding developments are expected to shape broader discussions on governance, faith, and public order in Uttar Pradesh in the days ahead.

item.title: UP Congress Chief Ajay Rai Takes on BJP Over Shankaracharya Controversy : Dalimss News Exclusive
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi/Prayagraj, January 2026 – Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai has sharply criticised the BJP-led state government, alleging it has disrespected the institution of Shankaracharya and Sanatan Dharma, during a march towards Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi on Wednesday. Rai’s remarks reference the ongoing controversy in Prayagraj’s Magh Mela involving Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati.

The controversy began when Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand was allegedly prevented from proceeding for his traditional Mauni Amavasya sacred bath (Shahi Snan) by the Mela administration and police, leading to clashes between his followers and officials, and subsequent protests by the seer. Authorities later issued a notice to the seer questioning his use of the title “Shankaracharya of the Jyotish Peeth” amid a pending Supreme Court dispute over the position.

Speaking in Varanasi, Rai accused the state government of showing a “lack of respect” for religious traditions and institutions and linked the Prayagraj incident with the broader Manikarnika Ghat redevelopment row that has sparked protests from political parties including Congress and AAP over alleged damage to heritage structures.

Rai reiterated that the Congress party has never supported the demolition of heritage nor the insult of Sanatan values or spiritual authorities. He also used the occasion of the march in Varanasi to highlight concerns about development works at sacred sites and called on the BJP government to rethink its approach to cultural and religious sentiments.

State officials have defended the actions in Prayagraj, stating that crowd safety measures at the Magh Mela necessitated restrictions and denying that any religious figure was intentionally disrespected. The Manikarnika Ghat work has been described by authorities as infrastructure improvement, with assurances that all sacred artworks and idols are preserved and will be reinstalled.

item.title: UP Congress Chief Ajay Rai Challenges CM Over Manikarnika Ghat AI Video Claims
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: In the ongoing Manikarnika Ghat controversy, Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee President Ajay Rai on Thursday launched a sharp rebuttal against the claims made by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath regarding the authenticity of viral AI-generated videos and images of alleged damage at the historic cremation ground.

Speaking to reporters in Varanasi, Rai accused the Chief Minister of lying about the facts surrounding the Manikarnika issue. He urged the state leadership to publicly showcase the idol of Ahilyabai Holkar, which has become the focal point of the controversy, if the government’s assertions are indeed true.

“If the Chief Minister is confident about his claims, then he should present the Ahilyabai Holkar idol at the centre of the controversy,” Rai said. “If he proves Congress wrong, we will publicly apologize to the people of Kashi.”

Faith and Public Trust at Stake

Ajay Rai further said that the matter goes beyond political rhetoric and now involves the faith of the people of Varanasi. He warned that if the Chief Minister fails to substantiate his claims, it would be up to the electorate of Varanasi to decide on the Chief Minister’s credibility and trustworthiness.

Rai’s comments come amid heightened political tension following the circulation of manipulated viral content and the subsequent police investigation. Authorities have been probing whether misleading images and videos were used to stir public sentiment against the ongoing Manikarnika Ghat beautification and development project.

Political Backlash and Public Debate

The Manikarnika controversy has triggered widespread debate across political and social circles, with opposition parties calling for transparency and accountability. Rai’s statement underscores the Congress party’s attempt to keep the issue in the spotlight and question the narrative put forward by the state government.

“As long as there is ambiguity about the facts, the people of Varanasi will continue to seek the truth,” he added.

Meanwhile, the administration continues its investigation into the viral posts, emphasizing that the inquiry aims to curb misinformation and maintain public order.

item.title: Varanasi to Replace 200-Year-Old Shahi Nalas
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal_
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi’s centuries-old sewer infrastructure, dating back to the British and Mughal periods, is finally set to undergo a major transformation.

The Uttar Pradesh government has approved a large-scale sewer revamp project aimed at addressing long-standing drainage and sanitation issues in the city’s oldest and most densely populated areas. The project is expected to bring significant relief to more than 10 lakh residents who have been living with chronic sewer overflows and poor drainage conditions.

Under the first phase, 18 old wards of Varanasi have been identified for the installation of a modern sewer network.

Of these, 13 wards have already received administrative approval at the state level, with work having commenced in two wards.

The project involves laying nearly 200 kilometres of new sewer pipelines at an estimated cost of ₹527 crore.

Areas such as Pakka Mahal, Bengali Tola, Shivala, Nagwa, Jangambari, Kazipura, and other historic neighbourhoods along the Ganga ghats will be covered, benefiting nearly 100 localities across the old city.

Officials say the new pipelines will be laid using trenchless technology to minimise disruption in Varanasi’s narrow lanes and densely built neighbourhoods.

Currently, the city relies heavily on nearly 200-year-old brick-lined royal drains, known locally as “Shahi Nalas,” which have collapsed or become dysfunctional over time.

Frequent sewer overflows during both monsoon and non-monsoon periods have turned daily life into a challenge for residents.

Once completed, the project is expected to significantly improve drainage, sanitation, and overall living conditions, marking a decisive shift from colonial-era infrastructure to a modern urban sewer system in one of India’s oldest living cities.

Officials have clarified that the demolition action is being carried out as per legal procedures and prior notices, and the priority remains to maintain peace, safety, and smooth execution of the Dalmandi widening project, which is crucial for improving traffic flow and urban infrastructure in the area.

item.title: AAP Leader Sanjay Singh Leads Padayatra In Varanasi
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal_
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MP Sanjay Singh led a massive foot march (Padayatra) in Varanasi today, launching a scathing attack on the BJP government regarding the Manikarnika Ghat dispute and the recent administrative notice served to Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand.

Manikarnika Ghat Dispute:

Demands: Singh demanded that a case be registered against the "sinners" responsible for demolishing parts of the historic Manikarnika Ghat.

Protest: He asserted that AAP's protest regarding the vandalism at the ghat will continue and stated he would soon reply to the police notice he received.

Support for Shankaracharya:

'Dadagiri': Singh expressed anger over the notice issued to Swami Avimukteshwaranand, terming it administrative "dadagiri" (bullying). He questioned the Mela administration's locus standi to intervene when the matter is already sub-judice in court.

Cow Slaughter Allegation: He alleged that the administration is targeting the Swami because he demands a ban on cow slaughter, whereas the BJP allegedly accepts donations from companies involved in beef exports.

Investment & Elections:

Hollow Promises: mocking the investment summits (referencing New York), Singh asked the government about the whereabouts of the previously claimed ₹45 lakh crore investment in UP, calling BJP's promises hollow.

Poll Strategy: He announced that AAP will contest the upcoming Panchayat elections alone with full strength, and any decision on alliances will be taken only after these polls.

item.title: Amrit Bharat Express To Begin Regular Operations From January 23
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: The regular operations of the Banaras-Sealdah-Banaras Amrit Bharat Express (22588/22587), recently inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi, will commence from January 23.

From Banaras (22588): Operations start on January 23. It will run every Sunday, Tuesday, and Friday.

Timing: Departs Banaras at 10:10 PM, reaches Patna at 1:58 AM, and arrives at Sealdah at 9:55 AM the next day.

From Sealdah (22587): Operations start on January 24. It will run every Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday.

Timing: Departs Sealdah at 7:30 PM, reaches Patna at 2:43 AM, and arrives at Banaras at 7:20 AM the next day.

Stops: The train will halt at DDU, Patna, Jasidih, Asansol, and Durgapur.

Train Features: This "Non-AC Premium" train offers affordable travel with 18 coaches, comprising 8 Sleeper Class and 8 General Second Class coaches.

Howrah-Anand Vihar (13065/13066): Regular runs begin from Howrah on January 22 (Thursdays) and from Anand Vihar on January 24 (Saturdays).

Dibrugarh-Gomti Nagar (15949/15950): Operations start from Dibrugarh on January 30 and from Gomti Nagar on February 1.

item.title: Manikarnika Ghat Row: Police Probe Viral Images, Misinformation Angle Under Scanner.
item.dc:creator: aishwarya_jaiswal_
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi’s Manikarnika Ghat, one of the holiest cremation grounds in the country, has recently come under intense public and administrative focus following the circulation of viral images on social media.

The posts alleged damage to Hindu idols and religious structures during ongoing beautification work, triggering emotional reactions and public protests. As the issue gained traction, authorities moved swiftly to verify the claims and assess the ground reality. Police investigations have found that a large number of viral posts carried strikingly similar images and identical wording, raising concerns about coordinated dissemination.

This prompted investigators to initiate a digital footprint analysis to trace the origin of the first post. Officials have clarified that the inquiry is not limited to the content of the images alone but also focuses on the intent and timing behind their circulation. During site inspections, including the presence of investigating officers, religious activities were observed at locations that were claimed online to have been damaged.

The matter is also being examined in the context of the ongoing Dalmandi road-widening and development project, where large-scale encroachment removal and demolition are underway as part of a government-backed infrastructure initiative.

While no conclusions have been drawn, authorities are assessing whether the Manikarnika controversy was amplified to create pressure against development work. Meanwhile, law enforcement has maintained that its actions are aimed at ensuring public order, protecting religious sentiments, and preventing misinformation.

Officials have reiterated that any findings of deliberate misinformation or conspiracy will be dealt with strictly under the law, while development and religious harmony will continue to be safeguarded side by side.

item.title: Chief Minister Janata Seva–cum–Subsidized Bus Service Launched.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: The Uttar Pradesh government has launched the Chief Minister Janata Seva–cum–Subsidized Bus Service to improve public transport facilities in Varanasi and Ghazipur. The service has started operating from seven major routes in both districts with the aim of providing affordable and convenient travel, especially for rural and semi-urban areas.

Under this scheme, buses are being operated on identified routes to strengthen connectivity and reduce the burden of high travel costs on passengers. Officials said the initiative is part of the state government’s broader plan to enhance last-mile connectivity and ensure better access to public transport.

Meanwhile, preparations are underway to introduce electric buses on remaining routes in the coming days. Once operational, these e-buses are expected to further improve commuting facilities and help reduce pollution. With the expansion of services, the issue of illegal and unregulated transport is also expected to be curbed.

In another development, a mobile passport van service was inaugurated in Chiraigaon. Cabinet Minister Anil Rajbhar launched the service, under which a three-day camp is being organized to provide passport-related services near people’s homes. On the first day, documents of 50 applicants were verified. After verification, passports will be delivered to applicants through post.

The minister said the initiative will especially benefit youth aspiring to go abroad for employment, as they will no longer have to travel long distances or face difficulties in completing passport formalities.

Additionally, six e-bus services are expected to start soon between Ayodhya and Kashi, further strengthening road connectivity between the two religious cities. Officials indicated that the service is likely to begin from January 24.

The new transport initiatives have been welcomed by locals, who see them as a step towards better, affordable, and accessible public service.

item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI/PRAYAGRAJ: The ongoing dispute regarding the legitimacy of the Shankaracharya title has taken a new turn, with Swami Sadanand Saraswati, the Shankaracharya of Sharda Peeth, Dwarka, extending his full support to Swami Avimukteshwaranand.

Amidst the notice issued by the Prayagraj Mela Authority questioning Swami Avimukteshwaranand's status, Swami Sadanand Saraswati has come forward to back him.

This support from another major Peeth adds significant religious weight to Avimukteshwaranand's claim, countering the administration's stance that the matter is sub-judice and the title cannot be used.

This development follows the UP government's recent move to question Swami Avimukteshwaranand's designation as the Shankaracharya of Jyotishpeeth, citing a pending Supreme Court decision.

VARANASI: The upcoming Uttar Pradesh Diwas celebrations on January 24 in Lucknow will have a distinct flavor of Kashi, with special stalls dedicated to Varanasi's world-famous culinary delights.

The Delicacies:

Menu: Visitors in Lucknow will get to savor Varanasi's signature Kachori-Jalebi, Banarasi Pan, Thandai, Launglata, and the famous Heeng Kachori.

Special Inclusion: The GI-tagged Tiranga Barfi, known for its historical significance in the freedom struggle, will also be showcased.

Objective: Vinod Kumar Verma, Assistant Commissioner (District Industries Promotion), stated that the goal is to provide global branding, packaging, and marketing support to Kashi's culinary arts, ensuring they reach international platforms while maintaining original taste and hygiene.

Expert View: Padmashri Dr. Rajnikant, known as the 'GI Man', emphasized that the ODOC initiative will pave the way for GI tagging of these food items, ensuring quality control and protecting the identity of traditional artisans and shopkeepers.

item.title: Varanasi School Students Learn Art Of Manuscript Conservation At IIT-BHU Workshop.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi School Students Learn Art Of Manuscript Conservation At IIT-BHU Workshop

VARANASI: In a unique initiative to connect the younger generation with India's intellectual history, a two-day workshop titled "India's Manuscript Heritage" commenced at IIT-BHU on Tuesday.

Venue: The event is being held at the Dev and Vardhana Goswami Hall, organized by the Department of Humanistic Studies, IIT-BHU.

Participants: Around 70 students from classes 6 to 8 are participating to learn about the preservation of ancient texts.

Objective: Coordinator Prof. Vinita Chandra explained that the goal is to create awareness about manuscript heritage, teach basic conservation skills, and introduce students to potential career paths in manuscriptology.

Key Activities & Speakers:

Field Trip: The students were taken on an educational tour of the BHU Central Library.

Expert Insights: Chief Guest Prof. Gopbandhu Mishra (former VC, Somnath Sanskrit University) spoke on how the oral tradition (Shruti/Parampara) was documented into scripts. Special guest Aditya Vikram Agarwal highlighted the importance of manuscripts in preserving business knowledge. Department Head Prof. PK Panda emphasized the evolution of record-keeping and manuscript culture.

item.title: Varanasi Auto Driver Murder Solved: Accused Vishnu Yadav Shot In Leg During Police Encounter
item.dc:creator: pankaj_yadav
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: The Varanasi Police have cracked the murder case of auto driver Mahesh Yadav within 24 hours. The accused, identified as Vishnu Yadav, was arrested and subsequently injured in a police encounter while attempting to escape.

The Murder (Jan 19): Around 10:00 PM on January 19, police received information about a man lying injured on the road near the Bihari area.

The victim, Mahesh Yadav, a resident of Sundarpur, was rushed to the hospital but succumbed to his injuries during treatment.

Police investigations revealed that the accused and the victim did not know each other previously. The murder was the result of a sudden dispute, likely over money or fare (paise-baji).

After arresting Vishnu Yadav, the police took him to the spot for a crime scene recreation. While returning, the accused snatched a service pistol from a police officer and attempted to flee.

He fired at the police, prompting the team to fire back in self-defense. Vishnu Yadav sustained a bullet injury in his leg and has been hospitalized.

Police are currently verifying his background. So far, no prior criminal record has been found in the Varanasi zone.

item.title: Woman Dies After Spade Attack In Mirzamurad; Villagers Stage Protest With Body, Demand Arrest
item.dc:creator: saurav_yadav
item.content:encoded:
MIRZAMURAD: A 40-year-old woman, Sunita Patel, who was severely injured in a spade attack three days ago in Chitrasenpur village (Kachhwa Road), succumbed to her injuries early Monday morning at the BHU Trauma Centre.

The Incident & Death: • The incident occurred last Saturday when Sunita was attacked on her head with a spade by her neighbor Kuldeep Patel during a dispute over a path. • She was initially rushed to a local hospital and then referred to BHU Trauma Centre, where she died at 3 AM on Monday.

Protest & Demands: • After the post-mortem, when her body reached the village, angry family members and villagers placed it in front of the accused's house. • They staged a protest for three hours, alleging police negligence and demanding: Immediate arrest of the main accused, Kuldeep Patel. Compensation for the victim's family.

Administration's Response: • Officials, including SDM (Rajatalab) Shantun Kumar Sinsinwar and ACP (Rajatalab) Ajay Srivastava, reached the spot and pacified the crowd. • The protest ended after a written assurance regarding the arrest of the accused was given. • Heavy police and PAC force have been deployed in the village as a precautionary measure.

Police Action & Family: • Police have arrested two accused, Vikrama and Chandravati (parents of Kuldeep), and sent them to jail. A hunt is on for the main accused. • A case was initially registered for attempted murder, which will now be converted to a murder case. • The deceased leaves behind three young sons—Ishu (16), Priyanshu (12), and Gyanshu (11)—and an elderly mother-in-law.

item.title: Greater Banaras Project: Varanasi Ring Road Townships Under CM Urban Expansion Plan
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: The Varanasi Development Authority (VDA) is set to transform the city’s outskirts with the ambitious “Greater Banaras” project along the Ring Road, as part of the Chief Minister’s Urban Expansion Scheme. The state government has allocated ₹4,000 crore for township development across four cities, with ₹1,000 crore earmarked specifically for Greater Banaras.

Under this plan, VDA will develop townships over 1,000 acres along the Ring Road, stretching from Harhua to Rajatalab. Modeled on the Greater Noida concept, the project will include four modern townships, creating a well-planned urban expansion.

World-Class Amenities and Local Development

The Greater Banaras townships will feature markets, shopping malls, hotels, hospitals, schools, colleges, sports complexes, and green spaces. This development is expected to boost the growth of nearby villages, generate employment opportunities, and provide residents with modern urban facilities right on the city’s periphery.

The towns between Harhua and Rajatalab will benefit from rapid infrastructural growth. Plans include commercial complexes, IT parks, green areas, and hospitality hubs. Residents will have access to essential services without having to enter the crowded city center, easing population pressure in the historic parts of Varanasi.

About the Chief Minister’s Urban Expansion Scheme

The scheme was launched to promote the development of new townships. Under it, development authorities receive government funding for land acquisition. Any interest earned from these funds can be used for land purchases, with acquisition costs shared equally between the government and the authority.

The land survey for Greater Banaras is expected to be completed by June, after which the acquisition process will begin. The project is projected to open up new employment opportunities and modern facilities for residents, shaping the city’s future in a structured and sustainable way.

item.title: Varanasi Civic Body Waives Water Tax Surcharge For Residential Buildings; Residents Can Pay Arrears By March 31
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: Bringing relief to thousands of households, the Varanasi Municipal Corporation (VMC) has announced a 100% waiver on the surcharge (late payment penalty) for Water Tax (Jal Kal).The Decision: The decision was taken during the House meeting on Monday presided over by Mayor Ashok Kumar Tiwari.

Beneficiaries: The waiver applies to residential and mixed-use buildings.Deadline: Residents have until March 31 to pay their outstanding water tax dues without paying a single rupee as a surcharge.

Exclusion: The administration clarified that fully commercial buildings will not benefit from this waiver.

Background: The move came after Councilor Suresh Kumar Chaurasia raised the issue in the house, pointing out that the Water Department had sent bills with heavy surcharges pending for years without prior notice. Acknowledging the grievance, the Mayor ordered officials to issue revised bills to all eligible consumers by the end of this month.

item.title: UP Statewide Blackout Drill on January 23: Civil Defence Prepares Citizens for Emergency | Varanasi News
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
On January 23, Uttar Pradesh will conduct a statewide blackout mock drill across all 75 districts at 6:00 PM. The exercise is being organised by the Civil Defence Department on the occasion of Uttar Pradesh Day and the birth anniversary of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. Authorities have clarified that the drill is a preparedness exercise and not a real emergency situation.

During the drill, sirens will be sounded for two minutes in both high and low tones to simulate an air-raid warning. Power supply will be temporarily switched off in identified areas, and citizens will be guided to move to designated safe locations. Multiple agencies, including the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA), State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), police, fire services, health department and power authorities, will work in coordination during the exercise.

After the mock warning phase, another siren will signal the end of the simulated threat. Civil Defence volunteers will then demonstrate response measures such as fire control using extinguishers, rescue of people trapped in damaged structures, providing first aid to the injured, and transporting casualties to hospitals through ambulances. Officials have urged citizens to remain calm and cooperate, stating that the objective of the drill is to strengthen disaster response readiness and public awareness, not to create panic. item.title: UP Government vs Swami Avimukteshwaranand : UP Govt Questions Swami Avimukteshwaranand’s ‘Shankaracharya’ Claim
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Prayagraj: In a significant escalation between the Uttar Pradesh government and religious leadership, the Prayagraj Mela Authority has issued a show-cause notice to Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati, questioning his use of the title ‘Shankaracharya’ during the ongoing Magh Mela.

Objection Over Camp Signboard

According to officials, the notice was issued after the administration objected to a signboard displayed at Swami Avimukteshwaranand’s camp, where he has been described as the Shankaracharya of Jyotishpeeth. The Mela Authority stated that the matter related to the Jyotishpeeth Shankaracharya is currently sub-judice before the Supreme Court.

Supreme Court Case Cited

In the notice, the authority stated:

“The matter regarding the post of Shankaracharya is pending before the Hon’ble Supreme Court. Until a final order is passed, no individual can be coronated (Pattabhishek) as the Shankaracharya of Jyotishpeeth.”

The administration further claimed that publicly projecting oneself as Shankaracharya while the case remains unresolved could amount to defiance of the Supreme Court’s authority.

24-Hour Deadline to Respond

The Mela Authority has given Swami Avimukteshwaranand 24 hours to explain the basis on which the title ‘Shankaracharya’ is being used on official displays at the Magh Mela camp. Failure to provide a satisfactory response could invite further administrative action.

Growing Religious–Administrative Tension

The notice comes amid an ongoing debate over religious authority, traditional succession, and the role of the state in matters of faith. Earlier, Swami Avimukteshwaranand had publicly asserted that the appointment of a Shankaracharya is a matter of religious tradition and lies beyond the jurisdiction of the government or constitutional authorities.

Awaiting Response

As of now, Swami Avimukteshwaranand has not issued an official response to the notice. The development has drawn attention from religious circles and legal experts, as it touches upon the delicate balance between religious autonomy and judicial oversight.

The situation is being closely watched as the Magh Mela continues and the Supreme Court case remains pending.

item.title: Varanasi: Swami Avimukteshwaranand Says Government Has No Authority Over Shankaracharya Selection
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi/Delhi: Jyotishpeethadhishwar Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati on Monday made a strong assertion on the autonomy of religious institutions, stating that the authority to appoint or recognize a Shankaracharya lies solely within the traditional religious order and not with the government or constitutional authorities.

Addressing followers and the media, the Shankaracharya emphasized that Sanatan Dharma institutions function independently of the state, strictly following age-old traditions and spiritual lineage.

‘Decision Lies With the Shankaracharyas’

Highlighting the importance of Parampara (tradition), Swami Avimukteshwaranand said that the selection of a Shankaracharya is an internal matter of the religious order.

“Even the President of India does not have the right to decide who is a Shankaracharya. The decision regarding a Shankaracharya is taken by Shankaracharyas,” he stated.

Emphasis on Religious Tradition

The statement underscores the belief that spiritual positions such as Shankaracharyas are determined through established religious customs, guru–shishya tradition, and consensus within the Mathas, rather than through political or administrative processes.

Swami Avimukteshwaranand’s remarks come amid ongoing debates and discussions surrounding religious authority, legitimacy, and the role of the state in matters of faith.

Broader Implications

The assertion reinforces the long-held position of several Hindu religious institutions that spiritual governance must remain separate from political influence, preserving the sanctity and independence of religious traditions.

The statement has sparked discussions within religious and political circles, especially at a time when issues related to faith, tradition, and governance continue to draw public attention.

item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: In a significant move to improve the experience for pilgrims and tourists, the Varanasi Municipal Corporation (VMC) has introduced strict measures to curb overcharging by local vendors.

Mandatory Rate Boards: Addressing frequent complaints about tourists being fleeced with arbitrary pricing, the Corporation has made it mandatory for all food and beverage outlets to display rate boards (price lists).

The Zone: This rule is strictly applicable to the high-traffic zone extending from Maidagin to Assi Ghat.The Goal: The move aims to bring transparency and stop shopkeepers from charging exorbitant amounts from visitors who are unaware of local prices.

Bridge Renamed: During the general house meeting, another major decision was the official renaming of a prominent city bridge. The Kazzakpura Setu will now be known as the 'Baba Lat Bhairav Setu'. The proposal received the final seal of approval from the house.

Summer Preparations: With the summer season approaching, Mayor Ashok Kumar Tiwari issued strict directives regarding water infrastructure:

Cleaning & Repair: Orders have been issued to clean wells and re-bore handpumps on a war footing.

Workforce: To ensure prompt maintenance, one mechanic and two laborers will now be deployed in every ward to handle local civic issues immediately.

item.title: Swami Jitendranand Saraswati Backs Manikarnika Development, Calls Protests “Encroachment-Driven” | Exclusive
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: Amid the ongoing controversy surrounding the Manikarnika Ghat redevelopment project, Swami Jitendranand Saraswati has strongly supported the development initiative, stating that opposition to the project is primarily coming from individuals who have allegedly encroached upon ghats and heritage properties.

Speaking exclusively to Dalimss News, Swami Jitendranand said development is essential for a city like Kashi and accused protesters of acting out of self-interest rather than concern for heritage. “Those opposing development are the same people who have illegally occupied ghats and historic places. This is the real reason behind the protests,” he said.

https://youtu.be/SynwW0uUvE4

Development and Heritage Must Go Together

The seer emphasized that development and heritage preservation are not contradictory. He cited the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor as an example, claiming it has significantly boosted tourism and enhanced the global image of Varanasi.

“Development has strengthened Kashi’s spiritual and economic stature. The Vishwanath Corridor has brought unprecedented tourist inflow,” he added.

Religion and Politics Should Be Discussed Openly

Commenting on the broader debate surrounding religion and politics, Swami Jitendranand stated that no country in the world is truly secular in practice. “Every nation follows a majority religion, and religion should not be treated as a taboo subject in politics,” he said.

Remarks on Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand

Swami Jitendranand also made sharp remarks on Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati, questioning his legitimacy. “He is not a Shankaracharya and has demeaned the dignity of sadhus and saints. His frequent involvement in controversies and public confrontations has harmed the image of the saintly community,” he claimed.

On Dhirendra Shastri’s Tricolour Comment

Reacting to the recent controversy surrounding spiritual leader Dhirendra Shastri’s remarks about adding a crescent moon to the Indian tricolour, Swami Jitendranand said India’s democratic structure remains strong due to its Hindu-majority character. “No Islamic country in the world is democratic. In India, because Hindus are in the majority, minorities enjoy freedom and democracy,” he said.

Manikarnika Issue Continues to Spark Debate

The Manikarnika Ghat redevelopment project has triggered political, religious, and social debate in Varanasi, with voices both supporting and opposing the initiative. While the administration maintains that the project balances heritage conservation with modern infrastructure, critics continue to raise concerns.

Swami Jitendranand Saraswati’s remarks have added a new dimension to the debate, further intensifying discussions around development, religion, and heritage in Kashi.

item.title: Varanasi Police Arrest Absconding Manager From Gurugram For ₹70 Lakh Embezzlement; Carried ₹25k Reward.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi Police Arrest Absconding Manager From Gurugram For ₹70 Lakh Embezzlement; Carried ₹25k Reward

VARANASI: The Varanasi Cantonment (Cantt) Police have achieved a major breakthrough by arresting Saurabh Gupta, a wanted criminal carrying a reward of ₹25,000, for embezzling ₹70 lakhs from a local saree firm.

The Arrest: Location: Acting on precise surveillance inputs, the police tracked down Gupta in Gurugram, Haryana, where he was living in Patel Nagar (Civil Lines). He was arrested on January 18 and brought to Varanasi.

Action: After interrogation, he was produced before the court and sent to jail.Background: Originally a resident of Ganga Nagar Colony, Adampur (Varanasi), Gupta had been evading arrest for years.

The Case (2021): The Scam: The case dates back to September 8, 2021. Devanand Sewaramani Sappu, owner of the Ardali Bazar-based 'Suvidha Saree' firm, had filed a complaint against Gupta (who was his manager/accountant) and others.

Modus Operandi: Gupta allegedly created fake firms and siphoned off funds worth approximately ₹70 lakhsunder the guise of payments for goods.

item.title: VDA Demolishes Illegal Construction In Bankat; Bulldozer Razes Walls Built Without Map Approval
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
The Varanasi Development Authority (VDA) cracked down on illegal construction in the Bankat Gram Sabha area under the Lohta police station on Monday.

The Action:Bulldozer Action: Around 12:00 PM, a VDA enforcement team accompanied by a JCB machine arrived at the site.

They demolished the boundary walls of a plot which, according to reports, belongs to a local businessman.

Reason: Officials stated that the construction was being carried out without getting the necessary map (Naksha) approved by the authority.

Official Statement: VDA officials clarified that the demolition was executed solely due to the lack of approved building plans.

They instructed the land owner to halt all work immediately and resume only after obtaining the required legal approvals and passing the map.

Violent Clash At IIMT University Meerut: Students Throw Chairs And Tables; Girls Flee In Panic A chaotic scene unfolded at IIMT University in Meerut today as two groups of students clashed violently, turning the campus into a battlefield.

A video of the incident has gone viral on social media.The Incident: Escalation: What began as a minor argument quickly escalated into a violent brawl.

Furniture as Weapons: The viral footage shows students attacking each other with chairs and tables, along with exchanging kicks and punches. Panic: The violence created panic on campus, forcing female students to run for safety while bystanders tried unsuccessfully to intervene.

Aftermath & Action: Security Failure: Students have accused the administration of lax security, stating that guards were not present to stop the fight.

Investigation: While the university administration has not issued an official statement yet, police and college management are using the viral video to identify the culprits. Strict action is expected against those involved.

item.title: Kisan Flower Mandi Maldahiya Sealed.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
The Varanasi Municipal Corporation (Nagar Nigam) carried out a major enforcement action on Wednesday near the Kisan Flower Mandi in Maldahiya (Englishia Line), sealing several unauthorised shops and taking control of land worth crores that was allegedly under illegal occupation.

According to officials, the land belongs to the Defence Estate Department and is under the administrative control of the Nagar Nigam. Despite this, illegal occupation and unauthorised rent collection were reportedly taking place in the area. Following instructions from Municipal Commissioner Himanshu Nagpal, the encroachment was removed and the premises were brought under official control. The outer wall of the mandi now clearly displays a notice stating that the property belongs to the Nagar Nigam.

The action followed an internal inquiry in which a “yellow card” issued earlier was cancelled on December 30, 2025, after it was found to be invalid. An appeal filed against the decision was also rejected due to the absence of legal documentation. Officials stated that rent was being collected unlawfully in the name of an unauthorised occupant, even though no legal rights over the land existed.

The Municipal Corporation has now clarified that flower vendors operating in the area will be allowed to continue their business only through a formal agreement with the Nagar Nigam, and rent will be paid directly to the civic body.

The administration has warned that any future illegal occupation or unauthorised recovery of money will invite strict legal action. Officials say the move is aimed at ensuring transparency, lawful management of public land, and protection of traders from illegal practices.

item.title: Congress Stages Sit-In at Gandhi Statue Over Manikarnika Ghat ‘Demolition’, Submits Memorandum to SDM
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi, January 19, 2026: Escalating their protest over the Manikarnika Ghat controversy, members of the District and City Congress Committees staged a sit-in demonstration on Monday, alleging the demolition of the historic Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi.

The protest was led by senior Congress office bearers and witnessed the participation of several party workers. The demonstrators gathered at the Gandhi Statue located inside the Municipal Council (Nagar Palika Parishad) premises, raising slogans against the administration and accusing it of damaging the city’s centuries-old heritage.

Protest Against ‘Heritage Destruction’

Congress leaders alleged that ancient structures at Manikarnika Ghat were being destroyed in the name of redevelopment. They expressed strong resentment over the alleged damage to the legacy of Queen Ahilyabai Holkar, whom they described as a revered guardian of India’s cultural and religious heritage.

The protesters demanded that all activities leading to the destruction of ancient structures be immediately halted and those responsible be held accountable.

Memorandum Submitted to SDM

Following the demonstration, a Congress delegation submitted a formal memorandum (gyapan) to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM). The memorandum urged the administration to protect the historical and religious character of Manikarnika Ghat and ensure transparency in redevelopment works.

Party leaders warned that if corrective measures are not taken, the agitation will be intensified in the coming days.

The Manikarnika Ghat redevelopment project continues to remain at the center of political debate, with the administration maintaining that no heritage structure is being damaged, while the opposition alleges otherwise.

item.title: Varanasi: FIR Against 8 for Spreading Fake AI Videos to Derail Manikarnika Ghat Project, Says CP Mohit Agrawal | Exclusive
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi, January 19, 2026: In an exclusive interaction with Dalimss News, City Police Commissioner Mohit Agrawal revealed that an FIR has been registered against eight individuals for allegedly attempting to derail the ongoing Manikarnika Ghat redevelopment project by circulating fake AI-generated videos and images showing demolition of temples, including the Kumbh Mahadev Temple.

The Commissioner stated that the police are actively investigating the matter. Those named in the FIR have been given 72 hours to present their side of the story. If found guilty, they could face up to five years in prison under relevant sections of the law.

CP Agrawal further claimed that the AI-manipulated images and videos appear to have been created to incite unrest and create an imbalance in public perception. “We are taking this matter very seriously,” he said. “The use of AI technology to spread misinformation about sacred sites is unacceptable, and strict action will be taken against anyone trying to destabilize public order.”

The Manikarnika Ghat redevelopment project, a key initiative in Varanasi, has been under scrutiny and discussion for its scope and significance in preserving heritage while improving infrastructure. The police's quick response underscores the sensitivity of using digital platforms to spread false information, especially concerning religious landmarks.

Authorities have assured that investigations will be thorough and impartial, and the public is urged not to fall prey to unverified content circulating online.

item.title: Manikarnika Ghat Row: Pawan Khera Slams CM Yogi, Calls Alleged AI Videos “Behayaai”
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi, January 19, 2026: The political war of words over the Manikarnika Ghat controversy escalated on Monday as Pawan Khera, Chairman of the AICC Media and Publicity Department, launched a sharp attack on Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.

The controversy centers on videos showing the allegedly broken statue of Devi Ahilyabai Holkar, which CM Yogi had claimed were AI-generated. Responding to this, Khera delivered a pointed retort, dubbing the claim “shamelessness” rather than AI manipulation.

Khera’s Statement: "The Chief Minister said this video is AI. But Chief Minister ji, this is not AI, this is 'Behayaai' (shamelessness)," Khera stated during a press briefing.

Khera also criticized the administration for filing FIRs against individuals who raised the issue, arguing that the government is attempting to shoot the messenger rather than address the actual destruction of the statue. He accused the authorities of using technical excuses to cover up the incident instead of taking responsibility for the damage.

The remarks are likely to intensify the political debate surrounding the Manikarnika Ghat redevelopment project and the handling of heritage sites in Varanasi. The row has already drawn widespread attention, both for its political implications and for the growing discourse around AI-generated misinformation in public controversies.

Authorities have yet to respond to Khera’s comments, but the FIRs remain active as investigations continue.

item.title: Varanasi to Get 347-Acre Sports City Near Ganjari Cricket Stadium : ₹200 Crore VDA Project
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: The Varanasi Development Authority (VDA) has approved the establishment of a sports city on 347 acres near the ongoing international cricket stadium in Ganjari. The proposal sent by the VDA for building the sports city has received government approval with a budget allocation of ₹200 crore.

Officials stated that the plan will be implemented soon, and the project will also include acquiring additional land as needed. VDA has identified land in Ganjari, Harpur, Shivsagar, and Harsos village for this purpose. The sports city will be developed along the VDA Ring Road, covering an area of 200 meters inside and 2,500 square meters per year outside.

Last year, during a visit by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, instructions were given to expedite the process. The government has also initiated land registration procedures, and farmers will receive compensation along with basic amenities.

VDA Vice-Chairman Purn Bora mentioned that the project has been proposed with a budget of ₹200 crore and will start after discussions with farmers about compensation and development plans. Several farmers have already agreed to provide their land.

Strict action on illegal land use: Authorities have been directed to prevent illegal plotting and construction in the area. Anyone violating the rules, including planning officers, engineers, or other staff, will be held responsible.

Traffic management in the city: Due to the development, traffic in areas around Kashi Vishwanath and other city parts will be monitored closely. Roads, sewage systems, electricity, community halls, and parks will be developed to support the sports city infrastructure.

item.title: AAP MP Sanjay Singh Attacks BJP Over Manikarnika Ghat Row, Questions ‘AI’ Claim in Viral Video
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI/DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh on Tuesday launched a sharp attack on the BJP-led Uttar Pradesh government over the ongoing Manikarnika Ghat controversy, accusing it of hurting Hindu sentiments and using police action to suppress dissent. His remarks came after police initiated action against him for allegedly spreading “AI-generated” fake content related to the ghat renovation.

‘Does the Baba Know AI?’

Responding to the allegations, Sanjay Singh questioned the government’s claim that viral visuals showing damage to idols and temple structures were fabricated using Artificial Intelligence. Referring to a video circulating on social media that features a local priest or resident, Singh asked pointedly:

“The baba in this video—does he know AI? Can you see where the statue of Mata Ahilyabai Holkar is lying? Has the BJP gone crazy?”

He asserted that the video reflected ground reality and not a digitally manipulated narrative, challenging the BJP’s explanation of an “AI conspiracy.”

Attack on BJP Narrative

Escalating his criticism, the AAP MP said that concerns over Manikarnika Ghat were being voiced not just by opposition leaders but also by locals and members of the Holkar family. According to Singh, even the descendants of Rani Ahilyabai Holkar have claimed that the statue was demolished or mishandled during the redevelopment process.

He further alleged:

“Locals themselves are witnessing temples being demolished.”

“Temples were demolished earlier as well in the name of building the Kashi Vishwanath corridor.”

“If the same thing had happened in an opposition-ruled state, the BJP would have instigated unrest across the country.”

Defiant Stance Amid FIRs

Terming the police action as an attempt to intimidate the opposition, Sanjay Singh said FIRs would not deter him or his party from raising issues linked to religious faith and heritage.

“They can file more cases if they want. We will continue to speak wherever Hindu sentiments are being hurt,” he said.

Political Tempers Rise

The Manikarnika Ghat redevelopment has increasingly become a flashpoint in Uttar Pradesh politics, with the BJP maintaining that no heritage has been harmed and that misleading videos are being circulated to create unrest. Opposition parties, however, continue to allege damage to historical and religious symbols, demanding accountability and transparency.

As the controversy deepens, the clash between the government and opposition over faith, heritage, and development shows no signs of easing.

item.title: Major Daylight Burglary in Varanasi: Thieves Loot ₹20 Lakh from Retired Teacher’s Home Near Minister’s Residence
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: In a bold daylight burglary that has sparked serious security concerns, unidentified thieves broke into the house of a retired teacher in Varanasi’s Shivpur police station area and escaped with cash and jewellery worth nearly ₹20 lakh. The incident occurred in Shri Krishnapuram Colony, Dadupur Chandmari, an area located close to the residence of Cabinet Minister Anil Rajbhar.

The Incident

The victim has been identified as Nandlal Upadhyay, a retired teacher. According to police, the family had left their house on January 10 to attend the Tehravin (13th-day ritual) of a relative in their ancestral village. Taking advantage of the vacant house, the burglars allegedly broke the main gate locks and carried out the theft.

The burglary came to light when the victim’s brother, Virendra Upadhyay, noticed broken locks on the main gate and alerted the family. Upon returning home, Nandlal Upadhyay found the house in complete disarray, with cupboards and lockers broken open.

Loot Details

As per the complaint lodged with the police, the thieves decamped with:

₹50,000 in cash

Gold jewellery: 4 chains, 10 rings, 1 necklace, 1 mangalsutra

Ornaments: 6 earrings, 2 maang tikkas, 2 nose rings

Silver items: Anklets and household utensils

The stolen valuables reportedly belonged to the victim’s wife, daughter-in-law, and granddaughter.

Police Action

After receiving information via Dial 112, teams from Shivpur Police Station and the forensic unit reached the spot to collect evidence. Inspector Virendra Sonkar said that CCTV footage from nearby areas is being examined to identify and trace the accused.

Local Anger Over Security

The incident has triggered anger among local residents, who alleged a lack of regular police patrolling in the area. Locals claim that incidents of theft have been increasing in recent months, raising concerns about safety even in high-profile localities close to ministerial residences.

Police have assured that the case is being investigated seriously and that the culprits will be arrested soon.

item.title: AAP Varanasi Protests Manikarnika Ghat Renovation, Alleges Insult to Rani Ahilyabai Holkar
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Varanasi unit on Tuesday staged a strong protest against the ongoing Manikarnika Ghat renovation work, alleging that the historic ghat—originally constructed by Rani Ahilyabai Holkar—has been damaged in the name of redevelopment. The protest adds to the intensifying political debate surrounding heritage conservation at one of Hinduism’s most sacred cremation ghats.

The demonstration was led by AAP District President Kailash Patel, along with senior party leaders and workers, who gathered in large numbers to register their opposition. Protesters accused the authorities of undermining the historical and cultural legacy of Rani Ahilyabai Holkar during the corridor construction work.

Raising slogans such as “Rani Ahilyabai Holkar ka apmaan nahi sahega Hindustan” (India will not tolerate the insult to Rani Ahilyabai Holkar), party workers demanded immediate steps to safeguard the ghat’s original structure and heritage value.

AAP leaders asserted that Manikarnika Ghat is not merely a site of religious importance but also a symbol of India’s rich historical legacy. They claimed that any alteration or demolition of structures associated with the Holkar dynasty amounts to an affront to the legacy of Rani Ahilyabai Holkar, who is widely revered for her contribution to temple construction and cultural preservation across India.

Following the protest, an AAP delegation submitted a memorandum to the district administration, urging officials to ensure that no historical structures linked to the Holkar era are damaged during the redevelopment process. The party also demanded transparency in the renovation work and called for consultation with historians and heritage experts before proceeding further.

The Manikarnika Ghat controversy has sparked sharp political reactions in recent days, with multiple parties demanding clarity from the government on whether any heritage structures have been affected. Meanwhile, the administration has maintained that no historical or religious legacy will be harmed during development works.

item.title: Sankat Mochan Mahant Vishambhar Nath Mishra on Javed Akhtar: ‘Our Bond Is Rooted in Culture and Mutual Respect
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Mahant Vishambhar Nath Mishra of the historic Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple has spoken warmly about his long-standing association with renowned poet and lyricist Javed Akhtar, emphasizing mutual respect, cultural dialogue, and shared values. Speaking to Dalimss News, Mahant Mishra recalled that the relationship is rooted in years of interaction through music, literature, and cultural platforms connected to the Sankat Mochan tradition.

Mahant Mishra highlighted that Javed Akhtar has always shown deep regard for Indian culture, classical music, and the inclusive spirit that Sankat Mochan Temple represents. He said that the Sankat Mochan Samman, which was conferred upon Javed Akhtar, was purely a recognition of his contribution to literature, poetry, and cultural discourse, and not a political or ideological statement. According to him, the temple’s tradition has always been to honour artists and thinkers who enrich society through their work.

Clarifying his personal equation with Javed Akhtar, Mahant Mishra stated that their relationship has always remained cordial and respectful. He stressed that dialogue, mutual understanding, and cultural exchange are essential for a diverse society like India. He further added that Sankat Mochan Temple has historically remained a platform for cultural harmony, where music, art, and thought transcend differences and bring people together.

Mahant Mishra concluded by saying that the spirit of Sankat Mochan has always been about unity through culture, and that honouring individuals for their artistic contribution should be seen in that broader cultural context.

item.title: Philosopher Martha Nussbaum Criticizes India’s "IIT Obsession," Urges Shift Toward Critical Thinking
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
A recently viral video clip featuring renowned American philosopher Martha Nussbaum has sparked intense debate across social media platforms in India, reigniting the age-old conversation about the purpose of education versus the pressure of elite admissions.

In the clip, originating from University of California Television (UCTV), Professor Nussbaum offers a sharp critique of the Indian education system’s intense focus on securing seats in premier institutions like the Indian Institutes of Technology (IIT) and Indian Institutes of Management (IIM). She argues that this singular obsession often comes at a severe cost: the stifling of critical thinking, creativity, and independent thought among students.

Nussbaum, a Professor at the University of Chicago globally recognized for her influential work on ethics, justice, and the role of humanities in democracy, highlighted the immense societal and parental pressure placed on young minds.

"Parents will [find] their glory if their child gets into the Indian Institute of Technology and Management," Nussbaum states in the clip. She contrasts this with societal attitudes toward other fields, noting that many parents would feel "ashamed to have a child who's an artist or a writer or a humanist."

Her critique delves deeper than just parental expectations; it attacks the methodology used to achieve these elite admissions. Nussbaum warns that the current system often relies heavily on rote memorization, where students are "stuffed with all the things they need to pass these exams."

The consequence of this approach, she argues, is the production of graduates who, despite high test scores, have not been "taught to think for themselves." They may excel at replicating information but lack the necessary tools for independent inquiry, ethical reasoning, and creative problem-solving—skills crucial for navigating a complex modern world.

A Reflection for the Educational Community

Professor Nussbaum’s observations serve as a timely reminder for educators, parents, and policymakers nationwide. While the pursuit of academic excellence and professional security is understandable, her words urge a re-evaluation of what constitutes a "successful" education.

For educational institutions committed to holistic development, like DALIMSS Sunbeam, Nussbaum's critique reinforces the importance of balancing rigorous academic preparation with the nurture of the humanities, arts, and critical reasoning.

The viral clip suggests that a true education must go beyond merely passing exams; it must equip students with the intellectual independence to question, create, and carve their own unique paths in life, whether as engineers, artists, or humanists.

item.title: Manikarnika Ghat Redevelopment: Mahant Vishambhar Nath Mishra Raises Concerns Over Process
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi’s Manikarnika Ghat, one of the most sacred cremation grounds in Hindu tradition, is at the centre of an ongoing redevelopment effort that has sparked discussion across the city. While authorities describe the project as a step toward improved infrastructure and heritage management, questions are being raised about how deeply local concerns are being factored into the process.

In conversation with Dalimss News, Sankat Mochan Temple Mahant and Banaras Hindu University professor Vishambhar Nath Mishra expressed concern over the manner in which redevelopment decisions are being carried out. He stressed that Manikarnika Ghat is not merely a physical site but a living religious and social space with centuries-old traditions.

Mishra pointed out that redevelopment should not be viewed only from an engineering or administrative perspective. According to him, people directly connected to the ghat — including priests, traditional workers, residents, and religious institutions — must be meaningfully consulted before major structural changes are undertaken.

He emphasised that Varanasi’s identity is deeply intertwined with its ghats, temples, and narrow lanes, making public participation essential for sustainable and respectful development. Mishra noted that ignoring local voices risks disrupting long-standing practices and livelihoods that form the backbone of the city’s spiritual life.

At the same time, the government has maintained that the redevelopment of Manikarnika Ghat aims to improve facilities for pilgrims, enhance safety, and preserve heritage while aligning the site with modern standards. Officials have reiterated that the project is being executed under prescribed norms and with oversight from relevant departments.

As the redevelopment work continues, the concerns highlighted in the Dalimss News interaction reflect a broader debate facing Varanasi — how to balance modernization with preservation, and progress with participation. The outcome of this dialogue may shape not only the future of Manikarnika Ghat but also the direction of redevelopment across the ancient city.

item.title: Manikarnika Ghat Controversy Deepens: Minister Admits Lapse, CM Yogi Blames ‘AI-Generated’ Misinformation
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
In a contrasting statement, Minister Jaiswal admitted that while the Manikarnika Ghat project will ultimately benefit everyone, the execution was flawed. He remarked, "The statues should have been shifted before the construction work began," signaling a lapse in protocol.

Opposition & Context:

Protests: Congress and Samajwadi Party leaders have intensified protests. Congress officials met the DM, claiming that cultural heritage is being destroyed in the name of development.

Historical Significance: The Ghat was originally built by Queen Ahilyabai Holkar in 1771 and renovated in 1791. The foundation for the current modernization was laid by PM Modi in 2023.

Official Stance: DM Satyendra has reiterated that the statues are safe and authorities are tracing those spreading "AI-generated" fake videos.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath strongly refuted allegations regarding the destruction of Queen Ahilyabai Holkar's statue at Manikarnika Ghat, terming the circulating videos as "fake" and "AI-generated."

The CM's Statement: Addressing the controversy during his visit today, CM Yogi stated:

Safety Assurance: "The statue of Queen Ahilyabai Holkar is safe and preserved. Once the renovation is complete, it will be reinstated with grandeur. The claim that temples are being destroyed is a lie."

AI Conspiracy: He accused the Congress party of creating fake videos using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to mislead the public and defame Kashi. "Using AI to show broken temples is a crime. We will not tolerate this," he warned.

Attack on Opposition: Mocking the Congress leadership, he used the proverb, "Sau chuhe khakar billi Haj ko chali" (A cat going on a pilgrimage after eating 100 mice), calling their comments hypocritical.

item.title: Ajay Rai Terms CM Yogi's Visit A 'Cover-Up'; Challenges Govt To Take Media To Manikarnika
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks_
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI/LUCKNOW: Escalating the political battle over the Manikarnika Ghat controversy, Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee President Ajay Rai launched a scathing attack on Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, dismissing his visit to Varanasi as a mere "cover-up" exercise.

The Challenge: Responding to the CM's claim that videos of broken statues were AI-generated, Rai issued an open challenge. He stated that if the government has the courage and the images are indeed fake, they should take all journalists to the site to clarify the reality.

Rai accused the BJP of destroying the mythology and culture of Kashi, stating that those who claimed "Mother Ganga called them" have become enemies of the river and the city.

He pointed out the irony that the BJP celebrated Queen Ahilyabai Holkar's 300th birth anniversary with coin releases just six months ago, only to run bulldozers over her statues now.

Rai condemned the government for filing FIRs to silence the truth instead of admitting mistakes. He asked if the government would also register an FIR against Yashwant Rao Holkar, the trustee who had issued a letter and shared photos confirming the damage. During his address, Rai showed a video where a BJP minister allegedly admitted to the demolition. He also displayed a letter from the Ahilyabai Holkar Trust that mentioned the breaking of the statues.

item.title: Complete Waste of Time": Sanjeev Sanyal’s Bold Take on UPSC in the Age of AI
item.dc:creator: _dalimss_editorial_team
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI – In a statement that has sparked intense debate across classrooms and coaching centers alike, Sanjeev Sanyal, a renowned economist and member of the Prime Minister’s Economic Advisory Council (PM-EAC), has termed the obsessive pursuit of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) exam as a "complete waste of time" for today's youth.

As students and parents navigate an educational landscape increasingly influenced by technology, Sanyal’s comments serve as a provocative wake-up call regarding the future of work.

The AI Disruption Speaking at a recent public appearance, Sanyal argued that the traditional model of degree-based education and exam-centric preparation is rapidly becoming obsolete. His primary contention is that Artificial Intelligence (AI) will soon outperform humans not just in retaining information, but in delivering cutting-edge knowledge and handling administrative tasks—the very core of civil services.

"The obsession with UPSC for job security is misguided," Sanyal stated. He emphasized that as automation and data-driven governance reshape administration, the relevance of rote learning and multi-year exam preparation is diminishing.

Skills Over Degrees Sanyal’s advice to the younger generation is clear: shift the focus from chasing "safe" government jobs to acquiring dynamic skills. He advocates for:

Apprenticeships: Gaining real-world experience early.

AI-Ready Learning: Understanding how to leverage technology rather than compete with it.

Skill Development: Focusing on critical thinking and adaptability over memorization.

This perspective aligns with the government's broader push for technological self-reliance, exemplified by the IndiaAI Mission, which has allocated over ₹10,300 crore to build robust AI infrastructure.

A Divided Opinion The remarks have triggered a nationwide conversation.

The Supporters: Many educators and tech experts view this as a necessary reality check, urging a curriculum overhaul that prioritizes innovation.

The Critics: Aspirants and social commentators argue that for many, especially from underprivileged backgrounds, the UPSC remains a crucial pathway to social mobility and stability that the private sector cannot yet match.

On social media platforms like X (formerly Twitter), the debate has been vigorous. While some mock interview experts acknowledged the need for modernization, they underscored the tension between India's traditional career aspirations and the rapid pace of technological advancement.

What This Means for Students For the students of Dalimss and beyond, this debate highlights a critical pivot point. The future economy may reward those who can create and innovate using AI, rather than those who simply memorize facts. As the debate continues, there are growing calls for the UPSC itself to evolve, potentially incorporating AI proficiency and critical problem-solving into its selection framework.

item.title: Comedian Zakir Khan Finds Solace In Varanasi; Enjoys Tea On Ganga Ghats Amid Fan Frenzy
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks_
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: Renowned stand-up comedian Zakir Khan visited the holy city of Varanasi on Saturday, seeking a break from his busy schedule to experience the city's spiritual calm.

Zakir spent his time exploring the iconic Ganga Ghats and took a boat ride on the river. Adopting the persona of a common tourist, he was seen sitting on the steps, enjoying Tulsi tea and biscuits by the riverside. Although he tried to keep a low profile, fans eventually recognized the star, leading to a spree of selfies.

A Spiritual Connection: Reflecting on his visit, the "Sakht Launda" fame artist shared his deep connection with the city.

"I feel a unique sense of peace here. Spiritual places like Kashi provide mental solace amidst a busy life. The echoing Aartis and the flow of the Ganga attract me," he said.

item.title: From Bollywood Villain to Spiritual Seeker: Pradeep Kabra Finds Peace in Varanasi
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: Bollywood actor Pradeep Kabra, best known for his menacing negative roles in films like Wanted, Simmba, and Dilwale, has arrived in Varanasi, showing a completely different side of his personality.

The Viral Reel: The actor shared an emotional reel from the Ganga Ghats that is trending on social media.

The Scene: Walking barefoot on the ghat steps, Kabra is asked what he has lost. He smiles and replies, "Mera man kahin kho gaya hai" (My mind/heart is lost somewhere).

The Vibe: The video captures the spiritual essence of Kashi, featuring Sadhus and the serene river, presenting Kabra as a humble tourist rather than a celebrity.

Reactions: The video has garnered significant attention, including a comment from Harsha Richhariya (famed for the Mahakumbh), who commented, "Deep message." Fans are appreciating seeing the "reel-life villain" in such a peaceful, real-life avatar.

Officials will present updates on infrastructure works, civic facilities, and security preparedness.

As with every high-profile visit, the administration remains in action mode. The review meeting is seen as crucial, as it will provide the Chief Minister with direct feedback on ground-level implementation of government schemes and the current law and order scenario in Varanasi.

item.title: Manikarnika Ghat Controversy: Varanasi Mayor Calls Temple Damage Allegations Political
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: Amid controversy over development work at Manikarnika Ghat, Mayor Ashok Kumar Tiwari on Friday clarified that no temple or heritage structure has been damaged during the project. He said all construction work is being carried out in a planned manner, following religious traditions and norms.

The mayor, along with South Varanasi MLA Dr Neelkanth Tiwari and Municipal Commissioner Himanshu Nagpal, inspected the ghat after allegations were raised about the breaking of a statue of Queen Ahilyabai Holkar. Officials stated that the statue has been safely preserved and will be reinstalled after the completion of the project.

Mayor Tiwari said claims of temple demolition are politically motivated. He recalled similar opposition during the development of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor and said no heritage was harmed there either. “If anyone has proof of damage to heritage, they should present it,” he said.

He appealed to political groups not to spread misinformation or divide the Sanatan community. The mayor also highlighted the need for development at Manikarnika Ghat, citing the lack of basic facilities such as seating areas and toilets for visitors and families performing last rites.

Officials assured that the Kumbha Mahadev Temple remains in its original place, with Nandi and Ganesh idols completely safe and regular worship continuing. Local priests and residents met the inspection team and urged that the sanctity of the cremation ghat and its heritage be preserved.

The Manikarnika Ghat development project is being carried out under the guidance of the Prime Minister and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, officials said, adding that any shortcomings in the work will be addressed.

LUCKNOW/VARANASI: A severe cold wave accompanied by dense fog has thrown normal life out of gear across Uttar Pradesh today. The blanket of fog has significantly impacted road and rail traffic throughout the state.

Visibility Report: According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), visibility levels plummeted this morning due to the thick fog:

Zero Visibility: Recorded in Saharanpur, Ghaziabad, Bareilly, and Kanpur.

Low Visibility (50-100m): Major cities including Lucknow, Varanasi, and Prayagraj struggled with very low visibility, forcing vehicles to move at a snail's pace with headlights on.

Impact: Commuters faced severe difficulties during the early hours. Highway traffic has slowed down considerably, and several trains are reportedly running late due to the poor visibility conditions.

item.title: Varanasi Voters Alert: Check Your Name in Electoral Roll on Jan 18, BLOs Available at Booth
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
If you are a voter in Uttar Pradesh, especially in Varanasi, this update is important for you. Under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls, the Election Commission has intensified efforts to help citizens verify their voter details and protect their voting rights.

As part of this initiative, Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will be available at all polling booths on January 18, from 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM, in mission mode. Voters can visit their respective booths to check their names in the draft electoral roll. Along with the draft list, booths will also display names of voters marked as absent, shifted, deceased, or duplicate, allowing people to identify and correct any issues on the spot.

To make the process easier, the Election Commission has ensured that Form 6 (for new voter registration), Form 7 (for deletion), and Form 8 (for correction or modification) will be available at all booths in adequate numbers. Eligible citizens can apply for name inclusion, correction of details, or raise objections directly at the booth itself. Election officials have been instructed to ensure timely presence of BLOs and smooth facilitation for voters.

The response to the SIR process has been significant so far. In the last 24 hours alone, over 55,000 applications were submitted for voter registration across the state. Since the release of the draft voter list on January 6, more than 3.43 lakh citizens have applied to be included. The Election Commission has urged all voters to verify their names at the earliest and complete the required process within the stipulated timeline to ensure that their right to vote remains secure.

item.title: Action to Be Taken Against Vehicles Without Number Plates in Varanasi
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: The Varanasi Police will initiate strict action against vehicles operating without number plates as part of a drive to strengthen traffic management and road safety in the city.

Police Commissioner Mohit Agrawal has issued clear instructions to take action against such vehicles during routine traffic checks. The directive was given while reviewing traffic arrangements to ensure smooth and safe movement on city roads.

As part of the inspection, the Police Commissioner conducted a field visit to areas including Nadesar, Andhrapul, Roadways, Englishiya Line, and Lahartara, assessing ground-level traffic conditions and enforcement measures.

During the inspection, shopkeepers were warned against encroachments on roads, which often cause traffic congestion. The police have been instructed to run coordinated enforcement drives involving Traffic Police and Civil Police to take action against traffic rule violators.

Special emphasis has been laid on:

Vehicles running without number plates

Illegal roadside encroachments

Unauthorized parking in no-parking zones

Vehicles illegally stationed on main roads

The Police Commissioner directed officials to launch focused campaigns to curb traffic violations and ensure disciplined road usage across the city.

Authorities stated that sustained enforcement will continue to improve traffic flow and enhance commuter safety in Varanasi.
