item.title: Uttar Pradesh to Get Six New Highway Corridors, Boosting North–South Connectivity
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Lucknow: Uttar Pradesh is set to witness a major infrastructure push with the proposed construction of six new north–south highway corridors, aimed at improving connectivity and easing movement across multiple districts of the state.

According to the proposal, the corridors will significantly enhance road travel between northern and southern regions of Uttar Pradesh, making transportation smoother for commuters and facilitating faster movement of goods. The project is expected to benefit several districts by reducing travel time and improving access to economic and industrial hubs.

The proposal for the North–South Corridor Project has received in-principle approval, and preparations are underway to secure cabinet clearance. Once approved, construction is expected to be completed within two years.

Officials stated that the corridors will be developed in phases, with different stretches being constructed by agencies including the Public Works Department (PWD) and NHAI, depending on the segment. Some sections will involve upgrading existing highways, while others will be newly constructed.

Key Corridors Highlighted

Kushinagar–Varanasi Corridor: Connecting Kushinagar, Deoria, Ghazipur, Jaunpur, and Varanasi, spanning approximately 220 km.

Shravasti–Prayagraj Corridor: Covering Shravasti, Ayodhya, Sultanpur, and Prayagraj, with a total length of around 262 km.

Other corridors will link major districts across eastern, central, and western Uttar Pradesh, strengthening statewide road infrastructure.

The government believes that these corridors will accelerate economic activities, improve regional development, and create employment opportunities. Better road connectivity is also expected to support tourism, trade, and emergency services.

Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has reportedly emphasized fast-tracking the project, directing officials to ensure timely approvals and execution.

Once completed, the six corridors are expected to transform road travel in Uttar Pradesh, providing a seamless north–south transportation network across the state.

item.title: AAP MP Sanjay Singh Begins Padyatra from Mirzapur to Varanasi, Targets Unemployment Issue
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
MIRZAPUR/VARANASI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MP Sanjay Singh kicked off the third phase of the party's Padyatra (foot march) today, marching from Mirzapur towards Varanasi.

The Agenda: The march focuses on two core issues: Social Justice and Employment. Hundreds of party workers, carrying Tricolors and AAP flags, joined the Rajya Sabha MP as they began the journey to Prime Minister Modi's parliamentary constituency.

Attack on Govt: Addressing the gathering at the start of the march, Sanjay Singh launched a scathing attack on the state government regarding the unemployment crisis.

The Quote: "Today, Uttar Pradesh holds the unfortunate record of having the highest number of unemployed youth in the country. We are walking to demand justice for them," Singh declared.

The Route: The Padyatra will cover the distance between Mirzapur and Varanasi, aiming to mobilize youth and raise awareness about the party's platform on jobs and education.

item.title: Varanasi’s Gangapur to Get First Nature-Based Sewage Treatment Plant for Eco-Friendly Wastewater Reuse
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: Gangapur Nagar Panchayat is set to get its first nature-based Sewage Treatment Plant (STP), aimed at addressing the long-standing problem of untreated wastewater from households. The project, approved by the state government, will treat domestic wastewater and reuse it for agricultural irrigation.

The STP will be constructed at a cost of ₹1.82 crore and will have a treatment capacity of 0.84 million litres per day (MLD). Officials said the plant is designed on an eco-friendly, nature-based model that relies on natural processes for wastewater treatment, reducing operational costs and environmental impact.

According to the plan, wastewater generated from households will be collected and treated before being supplied to nearby agricultural fields. This is expected to help farmers by providing an additional source of water for irrigation, while also preventing untreated sewage from polluting land and water bodies.

The project is part of the Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) 2.0 and is among five such STPs proposed in urban local bodies across the state for the financial year 2025–26. Gangapur has been included as one of the selected locations due to its growing population and increasing sewage load.

Local officials said the work will begin soon and the STP is expected to benefit nearly 12,000 residents. Once operational, around 2,500 households will be connected to the system, improving sanitation and overall environmental health in the area.

Authorities believe the project will serve as a model for sustainable wastewater management, combining cleanliness, water conservation, and support for agriculture in the region.

item.title: Varanasi Security Alert: CJI Justice Surya Kant Visits, Traffic Restrictions, No Vehicle Zones & Diversions Jan 16-17
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: The holy city is under a heavy security blanket today as the Chief Justice of India (CJI), Justice Surya Kant, along with Allahabad High Court Chief Justice Arun Bhansali and a delegation of 5 Supreme Court and 18 High Court judges, arrives for a two-day visit.

The Schedule:

Today (Jan 16): The judicial delegation will arrive in Varanasi and perform darshan-pujan at the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. They will stay overnight at the Taj Hotel.

Tomorrow (Jan 17): The team will proceed to Chandauli for a district-level program.

Traffic Advisory (Crucial for Commuters): Divisional Commissioner S. Rajalingam and ADCP Traffic Anshuman Mishra have issued strict guidelines to ensure security and smooth movement:

No Vehicle Zone: The Maidagin to Godowlia route is completely closed to vehicles.

Evening Diversions: From 6:00 PM, vehicles going from Godowlia to the temple will be diverted via Pandey Haveli and Ramapura.

Entry Restrictions:

Heavy Vehicles: Goods carriers from Padao/Sujabad are banned from entering the city after 3:00 PM (diverted to Ramnagar).

Cars: Four-wheelers from the same route are banned after 5:00 PM.

Tourist Buses: Banned at Nammo Ghat. Parking is designated at Basanta College and Pani Tanki Railway Ground.

Saturday Alert: On Jan 17, four-wheeler traffic from Chandauli to Varanasi via Ring Road Phase-2 will be suspended from 8:00 AM.

item.title: Bank Retirees Protest in Varanasi: AIBRF Raises Pension, Welfare & OROP Demands
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
All India Bank Retirees’ Federation (AIBRF), Uttar Pradesh — District Unit Varanasi — has announced a dharna–pradarshan to raise long-pending demands of retired bank employees. The protest highlights serious concerns related to pension revision and post-retirement welfare, reflecting the growing dissatisfaction among bank retirees.

Key demands include pension updation in line with the RBI formula, withdrawal of GST on group insurance policies for retirees, and the provision of special allowance for employees who retired after 2012. The federation has also called for a direct dialogue mechanism with the Indian Banks’ Association (IBA) to address retirees’ issues transparently and effectively.

In addition, the retirees have demanded the implementation of a uniform “one rank, one pension” principle for bank employees and the regularisation of ex-gratia payments as per established norms. According to the federation, these demands are essential to ensure dignity, financial security, and social justice for those who devoted decades of service to the banking sector.

The demonstration reflects collective unity and determination, with retirees urging policymakers and banking authorities to recognise their contributions and take immediate steps to resolve these longstanding issues.

“AIBRF Zindabad, Hamari Ekta Zindabad” — the slogan echoes the spirit of solidarity and the resolve to continue the struggle until justice is delivered.

item.title: Manikarnika Ghat Redevelopment Sparks Political Storm: SP–Congress vs BJP Over Kashi Heritage
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI, FRIDAY, JANUARY 16, 2026: The ongoing redevelopment project at Varanasi’s iconic Manikarnika Ghat has triggered a massive political storm. The Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress have launched scathing attacks on the BJP government, accusing it of destroying Kashi's spiritual heritage and disrespecting Queen Ahilyabai Holkar.

Opposition’s Fury:

Akhilesh Yadav (SP Chief): Termed the action as "disrespectful" to Queen Ahilyabai Holkar and Sanatan heritage. He warned, "Avinashi (Indestructible) Kashi will become the cause of BJP's destruction."

Priyanka Gandhi Vadra (Congress): Called the demolition a "grave sin" (ghor paap), alleging that the government is erasing history for the commercial interests of a few.

Mallikarjun Kharge (Congress President): Questioned PM Modi, asking if the motive was to benefit "business friends" and why ancient statues were thrown into rubble instead of being moved to a museum.

The Controversy: The ₹25 Crore redevelopment project involves dismantling parts of the ghat to rebuild it.

The Spark: A viral video showed debris from a demolished Madhi (structure built by Ahilyabai Holkar in 1791), leading to allegations that ancient statues were damaged.

Holkar Trust: Yashwant Holkar, head of the Maharani Ahilyabai Trust, visited the site and demanded the restoration of the statues, stating that the disrespect was "unforgivable." He noted that two out of four statues of the Queen were found broken.

Administration & Locals React:

DM Satyendra Kumar: Denied allegations of destruction, stating that all statues are safe and will be reinstalled. He blamed "fake AI-generated videos" for the confusion.

Dom Raja Family: Vishwanath Chaudhary of the Dom Raja family supported the project, clarifying that the beautification was requested by his family and that the idols are safe.

item.title: Manikarnika Ghat Redevelopment Row: Congress Issues 7-Day Ultimatum Over Heritage Concerns
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
The controversy surrounding the redevelopment work at Manikarnika Ghat has intensified after the Congress party issued a seven-day ultimatum to the district administration, demanding a halt to any action that may affect religious and historical heritage at the site.

The issue gained attention after videos circulated on social media showing Rajmata Ahilyabai Holkar’s statue and other artistic elements lying amid debris during demolition work carried out as part of the Manikarnika–Scindia Ghat corridor project. The matter was later taken cognisance of by both the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) and the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO), which directed the administration to ensure that redevelopment proceeds along with proper conservation of heritage structures.

Responding to the allegations, District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar stated that no heritage had been damaged and that all statues and artefacts were safely removed and placed under protection at the Culture Department premises. He added that the statues, including that of Ahilyabai Holkar, would be reinstalled with due respect after the completion of redevelopment work.

Meanwhile, Congress leaders and workers gathered in Varanasi and submitted a memorandum to the District Magistrate, urging immediate intervention. Raghvendra Chaubey, President of the Varanasi Metropolitan Congress Committee, said the party is not opposed to development but insists that it should not come at the cost of history and faith.

The administration, however, maintains that the project aims to improve facilities for pilgrims and tourists while preserving the spiritual and historical significance of the ghats. Officials have reiterated that all work is being carried out as per prescribed norms and under expert supervision.

As the deadline set by the Congress approaches, the focus remains on whether dialogue between the administration and stakeholders can defuse the situation, ensuring that redevelopment and heritage conservation move forward together in one of Hinduism’s most sacred landscapes.

VARANASI: In a major relief for patients across Purvanchal, the Sir Sunderlal Hospital at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) is set to undergo a massive transformation. Following a directive from the Union Ministry of Health, the hospital administration has initiated a master plan to construct a new OPD Block and upgrade infrastructure to international standards.

The Crisis: Known as the "AIIMS of Purvanchal," the hospital sees a daily footfall of over 7,000 patients from UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Nepal.

The Struggle: Patients like 55-year-old Ramsoorat Pandey from Ballia report arriving at 5:00 AM to stand in line, only to see a doctor by evening due to massive overcrowding.

New Infrastructure: A dedicated new OPD block to de-congest the current facility. The University Construction Department has begun working on the design.

Digitization: Complete digitization of patient records to reduce paperwork and waiting time.

Staffing: To tackle the shortage of specialists and paramedical staff, the administration is planning salary hikes to attract top talent.

Innovation: Collaboration with IIT-BHU to patent and use indigenously developed medical devices.

item.title: Serial Hoaxer Arrested for Repeated Bomb Threats to Kashi Express
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: The Government Railway Police (GRP) Cantt has cracked the case of repeated bomb threats to the Kashi–Dadar Express with the arrest of a serial offender from Mumbai. The accused, identified as Rajesh Shukla, had triggered panic on three separate occasions by making false bomb threat calls targeting the train.

According to officials, Shukla, a native of Machhlishahr in Jaunpur district, was working at Vasudev Paradise Apartment in Mumbai. A GRP team led by Inspector Rajol Nagar tracked him through technical surveillance and arrested him from a PCO booth in Mumbai, from where the threatening calls were made. He has been brought to Varanasi on transit remand for further legal proceedings.

Pattern of Repeated Hoaxes

GRP officials revealed that Shukla is a habitual offender who repeatedly targeted railway authorities with fake threats:

June 2: He issued bomb threats for the Kashi–Dadar Express and Kamayani Express. Though arrested, he was later released on bail.

November 18: Shukla again made a hoax call using a complex 15-digit number to evade tracking. The train was halted and thoroughly searched in Bhadohi.

January 6: A third threat was made, forcing authorities to stop and inspect the train in Mau, once again causing panic among passengers and disrupting rail operations.

Investigation and Evidence

Circle Officer Kunwar Prabhat Singh said that investigators recovered a diary containing contact numbers of senior officials from the accused, raising concerns over his intent to repeatedly misuse sensitive information.

Police traced the accused using Call Detail Records (CDR), eventually identifying the PCO from which the calls were made. The PCO owner confirmed that Shukla was a frequent caller, leading to his arrest.

Impact and Official Response

Repeated hoax threats not only cause panic among passengers but also result in major operational disruptions and waste critical security resources. Railway authorities have reiterated a zero-tolerance policy against such acts, warning that strict legal action will be taken against anyone found spreading false security threats.

Further investigation is underway to determine whether the accused acted alone or had any additional motives behind the repeated hoax calls.

item.title: Beyond the Textbook: What We Can Learn from Japan’s "Whole Child" Approach By DALIMSS News Education Desk
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_education_desk
item.content:encoded:
When we think of Japan’s education system, we often picture high test scores and advanced technology. But there is a quieter, more profound layer to Japanese schooling that is capturing the attention of educators worldwide. It isn't about how much math a child knows, but rather, who the child becomes.

At DALIMSS, we believe that education is a preparation for life, not just for exams. Japan’s holistic approach offers a fascinating blueprint for building character, responsibility, and empathy alongside academic excellence.

1. Dotoku: The Class for the Heart In Japan, moral education is not an afterthought—it is a formal subject known as Dotoku. Unlike standard subjects with right or wrong answers, these classes are discussions designed to encourage critical thinking about kindness. Students debate ethical dilemmas, discussing values like honesty, hard work, and justice. The goal isn't to memorize rules, but to internalize the question: "How do my actions affect others?"

2. O-Soji: Dignity in Labor Perhaps the most famous aspect of Japanese school life is O-Soji (cleaning time). You won’t find janitors cleaning the classrooms or hallways in many Japanese schools—the students do it themselves.

The Lesson: This isn't about saving money; it is about respect. When a child scrubs the floor they walk on or wipes the desk they study at, they learn to value their environment. It teaches humility and the vital lesson that no work is "beneath" anyone.

3. The Power of the Pack: Group Harmony While many educational systems prioritize individual achievement (being the valedictorian or the star athlete), Japanese schools emphasize Wa (harmony). Activities are often structured around small groups (han). From eating lunch together in the classroom—often serving one another—to solving problems collectively, the focus is on the success of the team. Children learn that true leadership often means ensuring no one is left behind.

4. Emotional Intelligence and Resilience The curriculum pays close attention to emotional regulation. Teachers guide students on how to apologize sincerely, not just as a ritual, but as a means to restore relationships. By engaging with nature and the changing seasons through traditional arts and festivals, students also learn mindfulness and an appreciation for the world outside their screens.

The Takeaway for Our Community The Japanese model reminds us that the "Hidden Curriculum"—the lessons learned in the corridors, the playground, and during lunch—is just as important as the one in the textbooks.

item.title: That Woke Up the Internet: Why Parenting Was Never Meant to Be a Solo Act
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_education_desk
item.content:encoded:
A recent video circulating on social media has struck a raw nerve with millions of viewers. It depicts a poignant, unvarnished reality: a new mother, physically exhausted and emotionally drained, struggling to care for her newborn alone while her husband is away for work.

The clip is not just a glimpse into one woman’s home; it is a mirror reflecting the silent struggles of modern parenthood. The video argues a strong case for the joint family system, suggesting that the isolation of nuclear living is unnatural for raising children.

At DALIMSS, we believe in the holistic well-being of the family unit. This viral moment begs the question: Is she right? Do we need to return to the "village" model of raising children?

The Reality of the "Fourth Trimester" To understand why this video resonated so deeply, we must acknowledge the sheer physical toll of early motherhood. The period immediately following birth—often called the Fourth Trimester—is a time of intense healing.

Physical Recovery: The mother is recovering from major physical trauma (birth/C-section).

Sleep Deprivation: Fragmented sleep impacts cognitive function and emotional regulation.

Hormonal Shifts: Drastic changes can lead to postpartum blues or depression.

When a mother faces this alone, without a partner or extended family, the risk of burnout skyrockets. The video highlights that human beings are biologically wired to raise offspring in groups, not in isolation.

The Case for the Joint Family The viral clip champions the Joint Family System as the solution. There is undeniable wisdom in this traditional structure:

Shared Responsibility: The burden of cooking, cleaning, and holding the baby is distributed among grandparents, aunts, and uncles.

Intergenerational Wisdom: New parents have immediate access to experienced mentors.

Emotional Buffer: The constant presence of family can combat the crushing loneliness that often accompanies maternity leave.

The Verdict: In an ideal, healthy joint family, the support mechanism is unmatched. The video is correct in asserting that having "many hands" makes the load lighter.

Redefining "The Village" in Modern Times However, we must also acknowledge that the traditional joint family isn't an option (or a healthy environment) for everyone. Jobs take parents to different cities, and family dynamics can be complex.

If you don't have a joint family, you still need a village.

The lesson from this viral video isn't necessarily that everyone must live in a joint family, but rather that isolation is the enemy. Modern parents must actively build their own village:

Trusted Community: Neighbors, close friends, and other parents who can step in.

Professional Support: Recognizing that hiring help (nannies, cleaners) is not a luxury, but often a necessity for mental health.

Partner Involvement: When the father is present, parenting must be an equal partnership, not just "helping out."

The DALIMSS Perspective: Happy Parents, Thriving Children From an educational standpoint, the environment at home directly impacts a child's development.

"You cannot pour from an empty cup."

If a primary caregiver is depleted, anxious, and unsupported, it becomes incredibly difficult to provide the emotional co-regulation a baby needs.

Secure Attachment: A supported mother is more responsive to her baby's cues.

Emotional Intelligence: Children raised in environments with multiple loving caregivers often develop strong social skills.

item.title: Tragedy on the Roads: Speeding Car Injures Young Girl in Varanasi Hit-and-Run
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI — A shocking hit-and-run incident has sparked outrage across the city after a speeding vehicle struck a young girl and fled the scene without stopping. The accident, which occurred in a bustling area of Varanasi, has left the victim with serious injuries and renewed calls for stricter traffic enforcement.

The Incident According to eyewitness reports, the girl was crossing the road when a car, allegedly driving at a reckless speed, knocked her down. Witnesses stated that the driver made no attempt to slow down or assist the victim, speeding away immediately after the impact.

Local residents acted swiftly, rushing the injured girl to a nearby hospital where she is currently undergoing urgent medical treatment. Her condition remains a point of concern for the community.

Police Investigation Underway Local authorities have registered a case against the unidentified driver. Police officials confirmed that they are currently scanning CCTV footage from cameras installed in the vicinity to trace the registration number of the vehicle and identify the culprit. Officials have assured the public that strict legal action will be taken once the driver is apprehended.

Public Outcry and Safety Concerns The incident has led to a demand for accountability from Varanasi residents, who are urging the administration to implement tighter traffic monitoring and harsher penalties for reckless driving.

item.title: Rohaniya Sewer Project: ₹1,400 Crore Network to Improve Drainage and Sanitation
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: Rohaniya in Varanasi is poised for a major infrastructure upgrade with the development of an extensive sewer network costing approximately ₹1,400 crore. Acting on the initiative of Mayor Ashok Kumar Tiwari, the Varanasi Municipal Corporation (Jal Nigam) has sent a detailed project report (DPR) to the state government for approval.

The project aims to strengthen basic civic amenities in newly expanded urban areas of the city. Under the proposal, a comprehensive sewer system will be developed across 13 newly extended wards of the Rohaniya Assembly constituency. The plan is expected to provide long-term relief from waterlogging, drainage issues, and sanitation-related problems that residents have been facing for years.

According to officials, the project has been designed keeping in mind the requirements of the next 30 years. Along with main sewer lines, branch sewer lines will also be constructed to ensure that every household can be connected to the sewer network.

Once implemented, the project will benefit nearly three lakh residents, offering relief from waterlogging and contaminated water, especially during the monsoon season. Authorities believe that improved drainage will prevent dirty water from accumulating on roads, significantly reducing the risk of infectious diseases and improving overall public health.

The areas covered under the proposal include Kandwa, Karondi, Dafi, Susuwahi, Narsur, Chhitaipur, Bhagwanpur, Chitaipur, Kanchanpur, Karmasa, Lahartara, Shivdaspur, and Manduadih, among others.

Officials said that the sewer and drainage systems in these areas have deteriorated due to rapid and unplanned urbanisation. With budget approval from the state government, the tender process will begin immediately, and construction work will be expedited.

The ambitious project is expected to bring a significant improvement in living conditions and mark a new phase of planned urban development in Rohaniya and adjoining areas of Varanasi.

item.title: John Mayer's Mumbai Debut Postponed, Fans Outraged Over Last-Minute Reschedule
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai, India – American singer-songwriter John Mayer's highly anticipated debut concert in Mumbai, originally slated for January 22, 2026, at the Mahalaxmi Race Course, has been postponed to February 11, 2026. The last-minute announcement by organizer BookMyShow Live has ignited a wave of frustration and anger among fans, many of whom are demanding full refunds for non-refundable travel and accommodation expenses.

The sudden change, reportedly linked to the recent passing of Bob Weir, a close collaborator and founding member of the Grateful Dead whom Mayer considered a brother, has left fans reeling. This marks Mayer's inaugural performance in India, an event many had been planning for months.

Social media platforms are abuzz with expressions of discontent. "What about the non-refundable accommodation and flight tickets? The show was literally a week away," lamented one fan, highlighting the logistical nightmares faced by attendees from across India and beyond. Another comment echoed the sentiment, stating, "Feeling horrid for everyone who booked tickets and hotels... this is such a terrible look from BMS."

The rescheduling to a mid-week date in February has further complicated matters for those who had adjusted work schedules and made travel arrangements. While BookMyShow has confirmed that existing tickets will remain valid for the new date, there has been no immediate mention of an option for refunds, exacerbating the disappointment among ticket holders. The lack of transparency regarding refund policies has fueled the outrage, with many feeling left in the lurch.

Fans are now left grappling with the financial implications of non-refundable bookings and the inconvenience of a rescheduled event, casting a shadow over what was once a highly anticipated musical milestone.

item.title: Manikarnika Ghat Upgrade Brings Better Facilities, Locals Urge Protection of Heritage.
item.dc:creator: _dalimss_news_desks_
item.content:encoded:
Manikarnika Ghat Redevelopment Draws Mixed Reactions Over Heritage and Change

Varanasi: Redevelopment work at the historic Manikarnika Ghat is underway as part of a ₹17–18 crore infrastructure project aimed at improving facilities for pilgrims and families performing last rites. The project includes better access roads, paved pathways, ramps, seating areas, organised wood storage zones, improved drainage, and enhanced safety and cleanliness measures.

Authorities say the initiative focuses on convenience, crowd management, and hygiene while ensuring smooth movement around one of the world’s oldest cremation sites. However, recent demolition activity linked to the project has triggered concern among locals and heritage observers, with allegations that historic structures may have been affected. The district administration has ordered an inquiry and clarified that no intentional damage to protected heritage sites has been carried out.

https://youtu.be/2Iqn8t1Gd6g

Dalimss News visited the spot and spoke to local residents and pilgrims. Most people said they support development, but stressed that heritage and traditional character must be preserved.

“We are not against development, but Manikarnika Ghat’s identity should remain untouched,” said a local resident. “Facilities are needed, but ancient structures and rituals must be protected,” another visitor added.

As work continues, the Manikarnika Ghat redevelopment highlights the ongoing challenge of balancing modern infrastructure with cultural and historical preservation in Varanasi.

item.title: ₹527 Crore Approved to Replace 200-Year-Old Sewage System in Varanasi’s Old City.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
In a massive infrastructural overhaul for the holy city, the state government has approved a budget of ₹527 crores to replace the crumbling sewage system in 13 old wards of Varanasi.

The Project: Approximately 200 kilometers of new sewer lines will be laid to replace the 200-year-old "Shahi Nala" and British-era brick drainage systems that are currently causing frequent overflows and waterlogging.

Key Features:

Trenchless Technology: To minimize disruption in Varanasi’s famous narrow lanes (galis), the work will be done using trenchless technology. Instead of digging up the entire road, pits will be made at corners to insert pipes.

Beneficiaries: Over 4 lakh residents across 100 neighborhoods—including Hukulganj, Prahalad Ghat, Shivala, Nagwa, and Bengali Tola—will benefit.

Dual Upgrade: Mayor Ashok Kumar Tiwari stated that drinking water pipelines will also be replaced simultaneously to avoid digging up the streets twice.

Next Steps: Municipal Commissioner Himanshu Nagpal confirmed that proposals for 5 remaining wards are expected to get Cabinet approval this week.

item.title: Makar Sankranti Date Explained: Why the Festival Will Be Celebrated on January 15 for the Next 54 Years.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks_
item.content:encoded:
If you are confused about whether to celebrate Makar Sankranti on the 14th or 15th, astronomical calculations have settled the debate not just for this year, but for decades to come. Experts state that for the next 54 years (until 2080), the festival will fall on January 15.

The Science Behind The Shift: According to Jyotishacharya Daivagya Krishna Shastri, the Sun's transit into a new zodiac sign gets delayed by 20 minutes every year.

This creates a cumulative gap of 24 hours (one full day) every 72 years.

Historically, the festival was celebrated on Jan 12 (1792-1863), then Jan 13 (1864-1936), and then Jan 14 (1936-2008).

We are now in the cycle where the transition happens late on the 14th, making the morning of the 15th the auspicious time (Punya Kaal) for the holy dip and donations.

This Year's Timing: Tonight (Jan 14, 2026), the Sun will enter Capricorn (Makar Rashi) at 9:39 PM. Since the transit is at night, the holy period begins the next sunrise. Therefore, the festival is being celebrated on Thursday, January 15.

Zodiac Advice: Devotees are advised to donate items based on their zodiac signs—such as jaggery for Leo, sesame/blankets for Capricorn, and green vegetables for Gemini—to gain maximum spiritual benefit.

item.title: Makar Sankranti Se Pehle Dalmandi Road Widening Par 2 Din Ka Brake, Demolition Roki Gayi.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
The ongoing road widening work in the Dalmandi area of Varanasi has been temporarily halted for two days in view of the upcoming Makar Sankranti festival, according to local administration officials.

The demolition drive, which began as part of the Dalmandi road widening project, was paused to ensure smooth law and order arrangements and to avoid inconvenience during the festive period.

Officials stated that the decision was taken keeping public movement, religious sensitivity, and crowd management in mind.

The Dalmandi project aims to widen a narrow and congested stretch to improve traffic flow and connectivity in the old city area. In recent days, the demolition action had drawn attention due to its impact on local shops, residential structures, and the broader discussions surrounding properties falling within the project’s alignment.

While the administration maintains that the project is essential for long-term urban planning and traffic management, affected shopkeepers and residents have raised concerns regarding notice, compensation, and rehabilitation procedures.

The temporary halt, however, does not indicate a cancellation of the project.

Authorities have clarified that the pause is strictly for the festival period and that further action will be reviewed after Makar Sankranti.

At present, there is no official announcement on whether any changes will be made to the execution plan once the demolition drive resumes.

Stakeholders continue to seek clarity on timelines, compensation mechanisms, and the next phase of the project.

The situation remains under observation, with further updates expected after the two-day pause.

item.title: Dog Bite Cases Par Supreme Court Ka Sakht Rukh, State Sarkar Par Dali Jimmedari.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks_
item.content:encoded:
The Supreme Court has taken a firm position on the growing problem of stray dog attacks across the country, expressing serious concern over the failure to effectively implement existing rules and regulations.

During the hearing, the Court indicated that in cases where a person is injured or killed due to a dog bite, the responsibility would lie with the State Government, and compensation may have to be paid for such lapses.

The bench observed that rules related to the management of stray dogs already exist, but poor enforcement has led to an alarming rise in incidents, particularly affecting children, the elderly, and the sick.

The Court made it clear that dog bite cases cannot be treated merely as unfortunate accidents when authorities have failed to act. It emphasized that ensuring public safety is a core duty of the State and local administrations.

The Court also addressed the role of individuals and organisations feeding stray dogs, stating that if a dog is under someone’s supervision, it would be considered a pet and would require proper licensing.

The judges clarified that the issue is not about being for or against animals, but about balancing animal welfare with human safety.

The Supreme Court reiterated that accountability must be fixed and that authorities cannot avoid responsibility by citing administrative difficulties.

The matter is scheduled for further hearing, where the Court will examine action plans submitted by States and local bodies.

item.title: Assi Ghat Parking Project Fast-Tracked, Varanasi Mayor Sets April 30 Deadline.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks_
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: In a major relief for tourists and locals struggling with traffic congestion near the famous Assi Ghat, the Varanasi Municipal Corporation has fast-tracked the construction of the proposed parking facility. Mayor Ashok Kumar Tiwari has set a strict deadline of April 30 for the project's completion.

The project had been pending approval of its technical drawing and design. During a review meeting on Tuesday, the Mayor directed officials to coordinate with Banaras Hindu University (BHU) to expedite the approval process.

As soon as the drawing design is approved by BHU, the work must commence on a war footing, the Mayor instructed. He emphasized that the parking facility is crucial for managing the crowd at the ghat.

The Mayor has drawn a line in the sand regarding the timeline. If the construction agency fails to complete the parking facility by April 30, a heavy financial penalty will be imposed on them. He stated that delays in public utility projects will no longer be tolerated.

item.title: Varanasi DM Cracks Down on Alaknanda Cruise: Irregularities Lead to ₹5,000 Fine
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
In a move to ensure the strict enforcement of safety and environmental protocols on the River Ganga, the District Magistrate (DM) of Varanasi has imposed a financial penalty of ₹5,000 on the operators of the Alaknanda Cruise. The action follows a series of complaints regarding violations of prescribed operational norms.

Administrative Action and Lapses Official sources confirmed that the district administration initiated a review after reports of irregularities surfaced during the cruise's daily operations. Upon investigation, the authorities identified several lapses in compliance with the standard operating procedures (SOPs).

The monetary penalty was issued as per existing regulations to serve as a deterrent. The DM emphasized that no operator, regardless of scale, is exempt from the rules designed to protect the sanctity and safety of the Ganga.

Directives for Future Operations The District Magistrate has issued a stern warning to the cruise management, directing them to prioritize the following areas:

Cleanliness & Waste Management: Strict adherence to protocols to prevent river pollution.

Safety Standards: Ensuring all passenger safety equipment and navigational guidelines are up to date.

Environmental Compliance: Maintaining standards that do not disturb the ecological balance of the river.

"The administration is committed to maintaining the sanctity of the Holy Ganga. Regular monitoring and surprise inspections will continue to ensure that public sentiments are respected and government regulations are followed to the letter," stated an official spokesperson.

Warning of Stricter Penalties The administration has made it clear that this fine serves as a preliminary warning. Should the operators fail to rectify the reported issues or repeat similar violations, the cruise service could face stricter legal action, including the potential suspension of its operating license.

item.title: Varanasi DM Fines Alaknanda Cruise ₹5,000 After Sewage Discharge Video Goes Viral.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi DM Fines Alaknanda Cruise ₹5,000 For Dumping Sewage In Ganga

VARANASI: Acting swiftly on the viral video showing sewage discharge into the River Ganga, Varanasi District Magistrate (DM) Satyendra Kumar has imposed a fine of ₹5,000 on the operators of the Alaknanda Cruise.

The Incident: A video recently surfaced showing fecal matter being discharged from the cruise's valve directly into the river at Ravidas Ghat. The Pollution Control Board immediately issued a notice seeking an explanation.

The Explanation: A probe committee formed by the Municipal Corporation investigated the matter. The cruise operators claimed that the vessel was undergoing maintenance and the septic tank was clean. However, a staff member accidentally used the toilet while the "emergency valve" was being checked, causing the waste to bypass the tank and fall into the river.

New Orders: Along with the fine, the DM has ordered the operators to install a holding tank on the emergency valve to ensure that even in such scenarios, no waste enters the holy river. Meanwhile, local boatmen have expressed anger, claiming that authorities are lenient with big cruise operators while being strict with small boatmen.

item.title: After Vishwanath Corridor, Manikarnika Project Ignites Fresh Debate in Varanasi.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
Manikarnika Corridor Project Triggers Mixed Reactions in Varanasi

VARANASI: After the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, Varanasi is once again at the center of discussion due to the proposed Manikarnika Corridor project.

Manikarnika Ghat is one of the most sacred places in Hinduism and is closely linked to the spiritual identity of Varanasi, one of the oldest cities in the world. For centuries, the ghat has been known as a place where people believe the soul attains liberation.

In recent days, demolition work in the Manikarnika area has raised concerns among local residents, priests, and heritage lovers. Several small temples and old structures, some believed to be more than 100 years old, have been removed as part of the development work.

The action has led to public anger, with many locals saying that an important part of the city’s history is being lost. On social media, #SaveManikarnika has been trending, especially on Instagram, showing growing opposition to the demolitions.

Supporters of the project say the corridor will improve facilities such as cleanliness, crowd control, and access for pilgrims and tourists. They also point to the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, which faced protests in the beginning but later became a major religious and tourist attraction.

Officials have stated that the work is being done as per approved plans and that efforts will be made to protect the religious importance of Manikarnika Ghat while improving infrastructure.

As the project continues, the debate remains between preserving tradition and promoting development in the ancient city of Varanasi.

item.title: Varanasi Weather News: 14–18 January Tak Cold Wave Ka Khatra.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks_
item.content:encoded:
After a brief period of relief due to sunshine, cold conditions are expected to return across Purvanchal, including Varanasi.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a Yellow Alert from January 14 to January 18, warning of a possible increase in cold conditions, fog, and cold winds due to an approaching western disturbance.

According to weather officials, snowfall in the hilly regions and the movement of a western disturbance are likely to affect the plains over the coming days.

As a result, cold winds may increase, leading to a drop in perceived temperatures and a rise in morning fog. Visibility may be affected in several areas, especially during early hours, which could impact daily activities and travel.

Recent weather data shows that temperatures had risen slightly above normal, providing temporary relief from cold conditions. However, meteorologists indicate that this phase is likely to end soon as atmospheric changes move toward eastern Uttar Pradesh.

Residents are advised to remain cautious during foggy conditions and stay updated with official weather advisories during the alert period.

item.title: Chinese Manjha Par Sakht Action | Makar Sankranti Se Pehle Varanasi Police Alert.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
Ahead of the Makar Sankranti festival, the Varanasi Police have issued a strict alert regarding the illegal sale and use of Chinese manjha, which has been declared completely banned due to its serious threat to human life and public safety.

Police Commissioner Mohit Agarwal has clearly stated that the sale, storage, and use of Chinese manjha is prohibited.

The sharp and synthetic thread has been responsible for several incidents of injuries, fatalities, and harm to birds in the past, especially during the festive season.

To ensure effective enforcement, citizens who spot the sale of Chinese manjha anywhere in the city can lodge a complaint directly between 12 PM and 1 PM by calling 9670705555. The identity of the complainant will be kept strictly confidential.

As part of the enforcement strategy, police personnel will conduct checks in civil dress by posing as customers at shops. Any shopkeeper found involved in the illegal sale of Chinese manjha will face strict legal action as per the law.

The police have appealed to citizens to celebrate Makar Sankranti responsibly and to cooperate with authorities in preventing the use of banned materials that pose a danger to lives and public safety.

item.title: Mathura Hospital Shocked as Snakebite Victim Walks In Carrying Live Snake.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
MATHURA: A scene of absolute chaos and disbelief unfolded at the Mathura District Hospital today when a snakebite victim walked into the emergency ward carrying the live snake inside his jacket.

The Incident: The man, a resident of a nearby village, had arrived at the hospital seeking treatment for a snakebite. As is standard protocol to determine the correct anti-venom, the attending doctors asked him if he knew which type of snake had bitten him.

The Shocking Reveal: Instead of describing the reptile, the man calmly unzipped his jacket and pulled out the live snake, which he had captured and tucked away after being bitten. The sight of the wriggling reptile in the emergency room caused panic among the medical staff and other patients, sending them scurrying for safety.

Status: After the initial shock subsided, the doctors secured the snake and administered the necessary treatment to the man. His condition is reportedly stable.

item.title: New Banaras, New Station | A Symbol of Kashi’s Development.
item.dc:creator: _dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
Kashi, the eternal city of spirituality and tradition, is witnessing a remarkable transformation. While its ghats, temples, and centuries-old heritage continue to define its soul, the city is also embracing development with a modern vision.

The newly transformed Banaras Railway Station perfectly reflects this change. With improved infrastructure, enhanced cleanliness, better passenger amenities, and efficient management systems, the station now offers a comfortable and seamless experience to pilgrims and travelers alike.

As lakhs of devotees arrive in the holy city every year, the modern station welcomes them with efficiency, ease, and pride. This transformation beautifully highlights how Kashi is moving forward where tradition and development coexist, and where even a railway station narrates the inspiring story of a progressive and changing Kashi.

item.title: Viral Video Par Action, Vivekananda Cruise Ki Inquiry Shuru.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: The Varanasi Municipal Corporation (Nagar Nigam) has swung into action following a public outcry over a viral video allegedly showing the 'Vivekananda Cruise' discharging sewage into the holy River Ganges.

Nagar Nigam Forms Inquiry Committee: Taking serious cognizance of the matter, the Nagar Nigam has constituted a special investigation committee.

Mandate: The committee is tasked with verifying the authenticity of the video and inspecting the cruise's waste disposal mechanisms.

Objective: They will determine if the discharge was indeed untreated sewage or compliant effluent. The committee has been directed to submit its report at the earliest.

The Controversy: Local boatmen recorded and circulated a video claiming that the luxury cruise was dumping untreated fecal waste directly into the river, violating religious sentiments and environmental norms. They alleged that while small boatmen face strict scrutiny, big operators often flaunt rules. The District Magistrate has also ordered a strict probe, stating there will be "zero tolerance" for polluting the Ganga.

Operator Denies Charges: The operator of the Vivekananda Cruise has dismissed the allegations, stating that the liquid seen in the video was "normal water" and not sewage. They claimed the vessel is equipped with a modern Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) and follows all environmental standards.

item.title: CRUISE SEWAGE ALLEGATION RAISES GANGA CONCERNS
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI, UTTAR PRADESH: A fresh controversy over pollution of holy Ganga river has surfaced in Varanasi after the allegedly showing untreated sewage discharge from the Vivekananda cruise into the river went viral on social media. The incident, where the alleged discharge occurred near the ghats of varanasi, when it was reportedly recorded by the local boatmen in recent days, has raised a serious concern about environmental norms, who is responsible, what exactly was released into the river, why such lapse has occurred and how waste disposal system on luxury cruise being monitored.

According to local boatmen who recorded the video, the cruiser was seen releasing dirty water directly into Ganga. They allege that this action is hurting religious sentiments and is also posing threat to cleanliness of the river.The boatmen also expressed their anger, claiming that small boat operators face strict scrutiny and large cruise operators often escape rigorous checks.

After acknowledging the matter, Nagar Nigam has constituted a special investigation committee to examine the cruise’s waste disposal system, compliance with environmental regulations and the authenticity of the viral video. The DM has also ordered an immediate inquiry, stating that no compromise will be made on the sanctity of the Ganga.

On the other hand, the cruise operator has denied all the allegations, stating that only normal water was released into the river and the cruise is equipped with a proper disposal system which adheres to all environmental standards.

item.title: Varanasi Skies Come Alive with Grand Kite Festival Ahead of Makar Sankranti.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: The skies of Varanasi turned colorful today as the Municipal Corporation launched a grand Kite Festival to celebrate the upcoming Makar Sankranti. mirroring the enthusiasm of the Kite Festival organized by PM Narendra Modi in Ahmedabad.

16 Teams in the Fray: A total of 16 teams have registered for the competition, showcasing their skills and traditional kite-fighting techniques. The atmosphere is electric, with citizens cheering for the 'pecha' (kite cutting battles) in the sky.

Mobiles vs. Manjha: Participants expressed joy at seeing the youth embrace the tradition. One participant interestingly remarked, "There was a time we got beaten by parents for flying kites all day. Today, kids get beaten for being on mobile phones. It is refreshing to see youngsters come out and enjoy this heritage sport of Banaras."

The Grand Finale: The competition is fierce, with a cash prize of ₹51,000 announced for the winner. The final matches will be played tomorrow (Wednesday), where the ultimate champion of the Kashi skies will be crowned.

item.title: Pahadiya Mandi Demolition Drive Se Vyapari Naraz, Vyapar Prabhavit.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
Traders and commission agents at Pahadiya Mandi have expressed strong disappointment over the ongoing demolition drive being carried out by the mandi administration. During conversations with this correspondent, traders said the action has created uncertainty and disrupted daily business operations within the mandi. According to the traders, several permanent and temporary structures that have been in use for years were demolished as part of an anti-encroachment campaign. They stated that these sheds and constructions were earlier developed to safeguard agricultural produce and support smooth trading, based on directions given by previous mandi officials. The traders now question how the same structures are being classified as illegal.

Many traders told this correspondent that the lack of prior consultation or dialogue has added to their frustration. They claimed that no effective hearing was provided before the action began, leaving them unprepared and affecting both traders and farmers who depend on the mandi for storage and sale of produce. Traders also warned that if the situation continues without a resolution, business operations at Pahadiya Mandi could be suspended. They urged the mandi administration to initiate talks and find a solution through mutual discussion rather than unilateral action. When contacted, mandi officials said the demolition drive is being conducted in accordance with existing rules and guidelines. Officials maintained that the objective is to remove encroachments and ensure proper functioning of the mandi, while indicating that further discussions with stakeholders may take place.

item.title: Varanasi Commissioner Issues Stern Warning After Filthy Condition Found at Public Toilet.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desks
item.content:encoded:
A routine inspection turned into a strict reprimand for civic officials on Monday when Varanasi Municipal Commissioner Himanshu Nagpal expressed severe displeasure over sanitation standards at key tourist spots.

The Inspection: Mayor Ashok Kumar Tiwari and Commissioner Nagpal conducted a joint inspection of Godaulia, Dashashwamedh, and Manmandir Ghats.

Commissioner's Action: Upon visiting a Sulabh Shauchalay (public toilet) at Dashashwamedh Ghat, the Commissioner found the facility filthy and the urinals damaged.

Reprimand: He issued a stern warning to City Health Officer Dr. S.K. Chaudhary and the manager of the Sulabh facility.

Stray Animals: Observing stray animals roaming the streets, he directed Veterinary Officer Dr. Santosh Pal to launch an immediate drive to catch them.

Mayor's Checks: Meanwhile, Mayor Ashok Kumar Tiwari inspected the 'Rain Basera' (night shelter) at Dr. Rajendra Prasad Ghat. Going a step further to ensure accountability, he called the contact numbers listed in the visitor register to take direct feedback from the travelers regarding the facilities.

item.title: Direct Varanasi–Bangkok Flight to Start from Feb 1, Air India Express Announces.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: Good news for travelers from Purvanchal and Bihar! Air India Express is all set to launch a direct flight service between Varanasi and Bangkok starting next month.

The Shift from Lucknow: Following a dip in passenger traffic, the airline decided to discontinue its Lucknow-Bangkok service and shift the route to Varanasi. This move is expected to significantly benefit tourists and business travelers from Eastern UP and Bihar, who previously had to travel via Delhi or Kolkata.

Flight Schedule (Starting Feb 1):

Departure (IX-215): Leaves Varanasi at 12:35 PM, arrives in Bangkok at 6:05 PM.

Return (IX-216): Leaves Bangkok at 7:05 PM, arrives in Varanasi at 9:35 PM.

Fares: Booking has already commenced. The initial one-way fare from Varanasi is priced around ₹8,857 to ₹9,057, while the return fare is approximately ₹9,548.

item.title: UP Government Declares 15 January Public Holiday for Makar Sankranti.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
The Uttar Pradesh government, led by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, has issued a revised order regarding the Makar Sankranti holiday.

The Change: Previously, January 14, 2026, was marked as a restricted (optional) holiday. However, amending this decision, the administration has now declared January 15 (Thursday) as a full public holiday.

What Remains Closed: Under the Negotiable Instruments Act, all government offices, schools, colleges, and banks across the state will remain closed on January 15.

Holiday Count: With this declaration, the total number of public holidays in UP for 2026 has increased from 25 to 26. Consequently, the number of restricted holidays has come down to 31. The decision was taken after reconsidering the date of the festival to ensure a uniform holiday across the state.

item.title: Varanasi Police Seize 88 Kg Chinese Manjha Under Operation Chakravyuh, One Arrested.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi Police Seizes 88kg Deadly Chinese Manjha Under 'Operation Chakravyuh', One Arrested

VARANASI: In a major crackdown against the banned lethal kite string, the Varanasi Cantt Police has arrested one individual and seized a massive haul of 88 kilograms of Chinese Manjha.

The Raid: Acting under the special campaign "Operation Chakravyuh," the police team raided a kite shop near Sarasoli Bazar in the Cantt area. The accused was caught red-handed with the banned synthetic string and a winding machine.

Zero Tolerance: The use of Chinese Manjha has been causing severe injuries to humans and birds alike. This seizure serves as a strong warning to illegal sellers.

The Team: The successful operation was led by Cantt Station In-charge Shivakant Mishra, along with Ardali Bazar Outpost In-charge Umashankar, Sub-Inspector Balwant Kumar, and Constables Ashish Mishra and Atul Kumar Pandey.

item.title: Pramod Tiwari Criticises Modi Government Over MNREGA, Extends Birthday Wishes to Priyanka Gandhi.
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Senior Congress leader, Rajya Sabha MP, and Deputy Leader of the Opposition Pramod Tiwari extended greetings and best wishes to Congress General Secretary and MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on her birthday. Addressing the media, Tiwari also strongly objected to what he described as changes made by the Modi government to the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MNREGA). He said the scheme, which once had the protection of a statutory guarantee, has been altered in a manner that undermines its original intent.

“After 1947, no one could have imagined that a government would come to power that would remove the name of the Father of the Nation from the world’s largest employment guarantee scheme,” Tiwari said.Tiwari alleged that the most impractical change is the removal of the employment guarantee, arguing that MNREGA has now been reduced to a regular welfare scheme with no assured work. He further claimed that earlier, work planning decisions were taken jointly at the gram panchayat, block, and district levels, whereas now decisions are being taken centrally.

He also pointed out that the scheme, which earlier functioned throughout the year, has now been restricted to 10 months, with a two-month break. Additionally, he raised concerns over the revised funding pattern. He further alleged that earlier Mahatma Gandhi’s statue was shifted from the main entrance of Parliament, and now the government has removed his name from what he called the largest employment guarantee programme in the world, calling it a “black chapter” in Indian democracy.

item.title: Ayodhya to Varanasi in Just 2 Hours: New Expressway Project Gains Momentum
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
In a major development for Uttar Pradesh’s infrastructure, the journey between two of India’s most iconic spiritual hubs—Ayodhya and Varanasi—is set to become faster and smoother. The proposed six-lane, high-speed, access-controlled expressway is officially moving forward, promising to slash travel time from the current 4-5 hours to a mere two hours.

Bridging Heritage with Speed This ambitious 200 km corridor is designed not just for speed but for connectivity. By reducing the physical distance between the cities by nearly 50 km, the expressway will serve as a vital link for millions of pilgrims, tourists, and families travelling between the Ram Temple in Ayodhya and the Kashi Vishwanath Temple in Varanasi.

Current Status: What’s Happening Now? As of January 2026, the project has entered a critical planning phase:

NHAI Action: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has issued tenders for the Detailed Project Report (DPR).

Consultants: The process to select a consultant is currently underway.

Timeline: The DPR is expected to take approximately 18 months to complete. While actual construction will follow this phase, the groundwork is effectively being laid today.

The Route Map The expressway is planned to integrate seamlessly with the region's existing and upcoming road networks. The route will:

Start: At Rampur Halwara.

Pass Through: Dasharath Samadhi.

Integrate: With the Purvanchal Expressway.

Link: Further connectivity to Prayagraj and Chitrakoot.

A Hub of Development This project is part of a larger vision to transform regional infrastructure. It complements the upcoming 67 km Ayodhya Ring Road, a ₹2,500 crore project slated for completion by 2027. Together, these developments will significantly improve access to nearby districts like Gonda and Basti, easing congestion and unlocking economic growth for the entire Purvanchal region.

For the DALIMSS community, this signifies a future of safer, faster, and more efficient travel, bringing the cultural heritage of Uttar Pradesh closer than ever before.

item.title: From Varanasi Classrooms to the Shark Tank: City Alumna Shaily Mehrotra Joins Season 5 Panel
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
In a development that has brought immense pride to the city, Varanasi’s own Shaily Mehrotra, Founder and CEO of the global skincare giant Fixderma, has been announced as a new investor "Shark" for the upcoming Season 5 of Shark Tank India.

Mehrotra’s addition to the panel is celebrated not just for her massive business success—building a ₹1,500+ crore empire—but for her deep-rooted connections to the cultural capital of India. Before becoming a titan in the Indian startup ecosystem, Mehrotra laid her educational foundation in Varanasi, completing her intermediate education at the city’s Kendriya Vidyalaya (39 GTC).

Her journey from a local student to leading a dermatology-led global brand serves as a powerful inspiration for students across the city, proving that global success can take root right here in Banaras.

A "Founder-First" Approach

Mehrotra is expected to bring a unique and grounded perspective to the Shark Tank panel. Unlike many modern entrepreneurs who rely heavily on early venture capital, Mehrotra famously "bootstrapped" Fixderma for over 15 years. She grew the company into a market leader through grit and strategic vision without initial external funding. On the show, she is anticipated to champion sustainable growth and "founder-first" values, emphasizing long-term substance over short-term hype.

Continuing the Connection to Banaras

Despite her global schedule, Mehrotra’s bond with Varanasi remains strong. Beyond her business achievements, she continues to give back to the community that raised her. She heads the "Fix My Life Foundation," an NGO headquartered in Varanasi dedicated to the upliftment and support of underprivileged women and children in the region.

Shaily Mehrotra’s debut on Shark Tank India Season 5 is eagerly awaited, as the city cheers for one of its own taking a center seat on India's biggest business stage.

item.title: Kashi Jewellers Implement Strict Security Rules: Face Coverings Not Allowed in Varanasi Gold Markets
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh: Following incidents in Jhansi, jewellery markets in Kashi are now enforcing strict security measures to ensure safety for both shopkeepers and customers. Under the new directive, individuals wearing burqas, hijabs, helmets, masks, or any other face coverings will not be permitted to enter jewellery shops or make purchases.

Kamal Singh, president of the Varanasi unit of the Uttar Pradesh Goldsmith Association, stated: "We will not sell any items to customers who hide their faces. This is necessary because in case of any incident, it becomes difficult to identify the person responsible. For safety reasons, we request that customers remove their face coverings when entering the shop so that we can ensure security and peace of mind."

The guideline has been communicated to all major jewellery hubs across eastern Uttar Pradesh, including Resham Katra, Thatheri Bazaar, Sudiya, Govindpura, Chhattatala, and Karnaghanta. Shops have also displayed posters informing customers of the rule.

Jewellers clarified that the move is strictly for security purposes and is not intended to restrict personal or religious attire. With Varanasi’s gold markets bustling with activity, shopkeepers and authorities are urging customers to comply with the new rules to maintain a safe shopping environment.

This step comes as part of a broader effort by market associations to prevent thefts, robberies, and other incidents, prioritizing the safety of both patrons and business owners.

item.title: CM Yogi Adityanath Reviews Magh Mela Preparations in Prayagraj, Launches Magh Mela Service App
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
PRAYAGRAJ: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath visited Prayagraj on Saturday to oversee the preparations for the upcoming Magh Mela. During his visit, he held a high-level review meeting with officials and public representatives.

To facilitate a smoother experience for millions of pilgrims, CM Yogi inaugurated the Magh Mela Service App. This digital tool aims to provide guidance and essential information to devotees visiting the holy fair. The Chief Minister began his visit with spiritual observances. He took a holy dip at the Triveni Sangam—the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati rivers. Later, he offered prayers at the Lete Hanuman Ji Temple and fed cows on the premises.

Addressing an event marking the 726th birth anniversary of Jagadguru Ramanandacharya, CM Yogi emphasized social unity. He recalled the saint's message from 700 years ago, stating that everyone has the right to seek God, regardless of caste or community.

item.title: Varanasi Hit-and-Run: Speeding Car Mows Down Girl, Driver Absconds
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
A shocking incident of reckless driving has sparked outrage across the city after a young girl was seriously injured in a hit-and-run accident. The incident, which took place in a busy commercial area of Varanasi, has once again brought the issue of road safety and traffic enforcement into the spotlight.

The Incident According to eyewitnesses on the scene, the victim was attempting to cross the road when a car, reportedly travelling at high speed, struck her. Bystanders stated that the driver made no attempt to slow down or stop after the impact, fleeing the scene immediately and leaving the victim critically injured on the road.

Local residents displayed quick thinking and humanity, rushing the girl to a nearby hospital. She is currently admitted and undergoing treatment for her injuries.

Police Action and Investigation The Varanasi Police have registered a case regarding the incident and have launched a manhunt for the absconding driver.

CCTV Surveillance: Investigating officers are currently scrubbing footage from CCTV cameras installed in the vicinity to trace the vehicle’s registration number and identify the driver.

Official Statement: Police officials have assured the public that the investigation is a top priority and that the accused will face strict legal action once apprehended.

Public Outcry for Safety The incident has led to a wave of anger among Varanasi residents, who are demanding immediate intervention from local administration. Citizens are calling for:

Stricter Enforcement: A crackdown on over-speeding and reckless driving in city limits.

Better Monitoring: Increased police presence and traffic cameras in high-density areas to prevent such tragedies.

As the city prays for the young girl's recovery, this incident serves as a grim reminder of the need for vigilance and responsibility behind the wheel.

item.title: Bulldozer Action Begins in Dalmandi, Heavy Police Deployment on Ground
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Dalmandi witnessed a major administrative action on Tuesday as authorities began demolition proceedings in the area. After initial action using hammers, a bulldozer was brought in to speed up the process.

Officials said the building was not vacated even after the deadline had expired. As a result, workers entered the premises after breaking the shutter, while heavy police deployment was made to maintain law and order.

Within half an hour, the upper portion of the building was demolished. During the action, women present inside the house protested against the demolition. A women police team entered the building to handle the situation and ensure safety.

Officials said that a bulldozer will fully arrive shortly to continue the demolition work. Security arrangements remain tight in the area to prevent any untoward incident.

item.title: SIR Draft Out: Is Your Name on the Voter List? Here is How You Can Check Online
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
Uttar Pradesh: Are you ready to cast your vote in the upcoming assembly elections? The most critical first step is ensuring your name appears on the official voter list. The draft for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has officially been released, making it mandatory for every voter in Uttar Pradesh to verify their status. In a recent report for Dalimss News, I, Anamika Pandey, broke down exactly how you can check your name from the comfort of your home and what to do if you cannot find your details. Why is this Important? The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a crucial update to the electoral rolls ahead of the future Legislative Assembly elections. The draft list has been published by the District Election Officer. To ensure your right to vote remains intact for the 2027 elections, you must verify that your name is included in this specific draft. Step-by-Step: How to Check Your Name Online The Chief Electoral Officer has made the process simple and digital. You do not need to visit government offices; you can check your status online. Follow this step-by-step guide: Visit the Official Website: Go to the official website of the CEO Uttar Pradesh at ceouttarpradesh.nic.in or the Voter Service Portal. Locate the SIR Section: Look for the pop-up or notification regarding the "Special Intensive Revision (SIR) – 2026." Search Details: Select the option to "Search Your Name in Last SIR" or check by EPIC Number (your Voter ID number). Enter Required Information: Select the State (Uttar Pradesh). Select the Year (2026). Choose the Role Type (SIR DraftRoll - 2026). Enter your District and Assembly Constituency. Enter EPIC & Captcha: Input your Voter ID (EPIC) number and the captcha code displayed on the screen.

6. Click Search: Hit the search button to view your status. If your name is on the list, your details will appear on the screen. What If Your Name is Missing? If the search returns "No Result Found," do not panic. The Election Commission has clarified that this is a draft list, not the final one. Contact Your BLO: If your name is missing, immediately contact your Booth Level Officer (BLO). Find Out the Reason: Ask why your name was removed. File an Objection: You can file an objection or correction request within the stipulated time frame to get your name re-added. As the Election Commission repeatedly emphasizes: Your right to vote is only secure if your name is on the voter list. Do not wait until the last minute—check your status today.

item.title: Ayodhya Goes Fully Vegetarian: Meat, Eggs, and Online Non-Veg Delivery Banned Across Temple City
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
AYODHYA: In a major decision to maintain the sanctity of the temple town, the Ayodhya administration has imposed a complete ban on the sale of non-vegetarian food.

The Directive:

Total Ban: The sale of meat, fish, and eggs is strictly prohibited within the city limits.

Scope: This rule applies to all hotels, dhabas, restaurants, and home-stays.

No Online Delivery: The ban extends to e-commerce and food delivery platforms; online ordering of non-veg food within Ayodhya is now restricted.

Authorities have made it clear that any establishment found violating these norms will face strict legal action. The move is aimed at respecting the religious sentiments of millions of devotees visiting the Ram Mandir.

item.title: Varanasi Police Raid Drug Trader’s House in Codeine Syrup Case, Seize Key Evidence; Accused Absconding
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: Intensifying the crackdown on the illicit drug trade, the Varanasi Police conducted a late-night raid at the residence of Prashant Upadhyay, a close associate of the main accused in the high-profile Codeine Cough Syrup case, Shubham Jaiswal.

The Operation: Led by ACP (Crime) Vijay Pratap Singh, a joint team from Kotwali, Adampur, and Ramnagar police stations searched Prashant’s house in the Madrauli (Manduadih) area for over two hours. Prashant, who owns 'Radhika Enterprises' and 'Rajendra Drug Agency', is currently absconding.

Seizures & Evidence: Although Prashant was not found, police seized significant incriminating evidence, including:

Fake documents and financial records.

Codeine syrup wrappers and vials.

Laptops and pen drives containing transaction details.

The Connection: Police are investigating Prashant's links to Shubham Jaiswal and a firm named 'Shaili Traders'. It is suspected that Prashant, a major player in the Saptasagar Medicine Market, facilitated transaction worth crores in the illegal syrup trade under FIR number 235/2025.

item.title: SOG–Chowk Police Crack Karnghanta Theft Case in Varanasi, Recover Over 2 Kg Gold; ₹1 Lakh Reward Announced
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: In a significant "Good Work" operation, a joint team of the Special Operations Group (SOG) and Chowk Police has successfully cracked the recent high-profile theft case in the Karnghanta area.

The police operation resulted in the arrest of five accused involved in the crime. The team recovered a massive haul of more than 2 kilograms of gold jewelry from their possession.

The successful team was led by SOG In-charge Gaurav Singh and Chowk SHO Dilip Kumar Mishra, along with several sub-inspectors and constables including Prakash Chauhan, Pushkar Dubey, and Alok Kumar Yadav. Appreciating the swift action and recovery, Police Commissioner Mohit Agarwal has announced a cash reward of ₹1 lakh for the police team.

item.title: Alleged Tinder Dating Scam Near Sigra Raises Concern in Varanasi
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi has witnessed an alarming case of an alleged dating-related fraud, reportedly operating from a bar located near the IP Sigra area.

According to a multiple reviews shared by a victim online, an organized scam is being run using online dating platforms, particularly Tinder, to lure unsuspecting men into the establishment and extract exorbitant amounts of money.

As per the allegation, women hired by the bar allegedly connect with men through dating apps and invite them for a casual meeting or date at the said location. Once inside the bar, the victim claims that the woman orders multiple drinks, which are presented as alcoholic beverages but are allegedly non-alcoholic or cold drinks served in a misleading manner.

He further alleged that the drinks are billed at extremely inflated rates, with charges reportedly going up to ₹2,000 for just 30 ml. Victims are allegedly pressured or forced to pay the final bill, leaving them with little choice due to the situation created inside the premises.

The matter has sparked concern over the misuse of dating platforms and the safety of individuals meeting strangers through such apps. The complainant has stated that they plan to approach the police soon and seek a formal investigation into the issue.

Authorities have not yet issued an official statement regarding the allegations. However, citizens are being advised to remain cautious while meeting unknown individuals through online platforms and to verify venues before visiting.

If proven, such practices would amount to serious violations of consumer rights and criminal law. Police action is expected once a formal complaint is registered.

item.title: Varanasi’s Daughter-in-Law Sushmita Receives Ati Vishisht Rail Seva Puraskar 2025 for Averting Major Train Accident
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi has another moment of pride as Ms. Sushmita, an Assistant Loco Pilot with North Central Railway and the daughter-in-law of Varanasi, has been conferred with the prestigious *Ati Vishisht Rail Seva Puraskar 2025* by the Ministry of Railways.

The award recognises her exceptional presence of mind, alertness and swift decision-making that helped avert a major accident while on duty. On 6 November 2024, while operating Train No. 20175 between Banaras (BSBS) and Hardattpur (HDT), Ms. Sushmita noticed an open level crossing (No. 7C) with vehicles moving across the track. Sensing the imminent danger, she immediately took emergency action, safely controlled the train, and informed the on-duty Station Master and concerned control officials.

Her timely intervention ensured passenger safety and prevented a potentially serious mishap. The incident was duly recorded in the railway safety management system, highlighting her adherence to protocol and commitment to duty.

Ms. Sushmita was formally honoured during a national-level ceremony, where senior railway officials praised her professionalism and dedication. Her achievement has brought pride not only to the North Central Railway zone but also to Varanasi, with locals hailing her as an inspiration for women in uniform and the railways.

The recognition stands as a testament to the critical role played by frontline railway staff in ensuring the safety of millions of passengers every day.

item.title: VDA Holds Meeting with Ganjari–Madhani Farmers to Promote Land Pooling Scheme, Assures Transparency and Consent
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI In a significant move to accelerate planned development, the Varanasi Development Authority (VDA) Vice Chairman Shri Purna Bora convened a meeting with farmers from the Ganjari and Madhani areas on Friday.

The Objective: The primary aim was to educate farmers about the Land Pooling Scheme and address their concerns. Addressing the gathering, VC Purna Bora termed the scheme as "modern and transparent," ensuring that the farmers' interests are prioritized.

How Farmers Benefit: The VC explained that under this scheme, the authority develops essential infrastructure like roads, sewers, electricity, and parks on the pooled land. A designated portion of this developed land is then returned to the farmers, the market value of which becomes significantly higher than the original agricultural land.

Assurances Given: Officials, including Secretary Dr. Ved Prakash Mishra and Additional Secretary Gudakesh Sharma, clarified doubts regarding compensation and timelines. The VC appealed to farmers not to believe in rumors, assuring them that "consent is paramount" and the scheme will generate employment and business opportunities in the region.

item.title: Kerala and Haryana Storm into Women’s Semifinals at Senior National Volleyball Championship in Varanasi
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
