VARANASI: High-voltage action unfolded on the sixth day of the 72nd Senior National Volleyball Championship at the Dr. Sampurnanand Sports Stadium in Sigra, with quarterfinal matches deciding the top contenders.

Women's Category Dominance: In the women's division, the teams from Kerala and Haryana displayed stellar performances to book their spots in the semifinals. The players showcased powerful smashes and coordinated defense, overcoming their opponents to advance to the next stage. The stadium was packed with sports enthusiasts cheering for the spikers as the tournament heads towards its thrilling conclusion.

item.title: Mirzapur’s Maa Vindhyavasini Temple Records ₹51 Lakh in Devotee Offerings
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
MIRZAPUR: A massive counting exercise was undertaken at the renowned Maa Vindhyavasini Dham in Mirzapur, revealing a significant collection from the devotees' offerings.

The Counting Process: Under strict security and administrative supervision, the temple authorities opened 27 donation boxes (Danpatras) placed within the temple premises. The counting process, which lasted for several hours, concluded with a total of approximately ₹51 lakhs.

Officials stated that the amount reflects the offerings made by thousands of devotees who visit the Shaktipeeth to seek blessings. The counted currency included notes of various denominations and coins. The funds will be deposited into the temple trust's account for maintenance and development activities.

item.title: Agra Police Arrest 81-Year-Old Fugitive After 42 Years
item.dc:creator: dalimss_news_desk
item.content:encoded:
AGRA: Proving that crime files are never truly closed, the Kotwali Police in Agra achieved a remarkable breakthrough by arresting an accused who had been absconding for over four decades.

The Case (1983): The accused, identified as Shahzad (81), was wanted in connection with an attempted murder case registered way back in 1983. Immediately after the case was filed, Shahzad went underground and managed to evade the law for 42 years.

The Arrest: Despite the passage of time, the police continued their pursuit. Acting on specific intelligence, the Kotwali police team finally tracked down the octogenarian. Shahzad was arrested, produced before the court, and subsequently sent to jail, bringing a decades-old legal chapter to a close.

item.title: SPEEDING CAR MOWS DOWN GIRL IN VARANASI: DRIVER ON THE RUN
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
A horrific hit-and-run incident has once again shaken the conscience of Varanasi, raising serious questions about road safety and reckless driving in our city.

In a tragic turn of events reported earlier today, a speeding car brutally hit a young girl who was crossing the road in a busy part of the city. The impact was severe, leaving the victim critically injured on the spot. Instead of stopping to help, the driver reportedly accelerated and fled the scene, leaving the girl fighting for her life.

Eyewitness Accounts According to locals who witnessed the horror, the vehicle was being driven at a dangerously high speed, completely disregarding traffic norms.

"The car didn't even slow down. It hit her with such force, and before anyone could react, the driver sped away. It was heartless," said a shopkeeper near the accident site.

Good Samaritans rushed the victim to a nearby hospital, where she is currently undergoing urgent treatment. Her condition remains critical.

Police Action & Investigation Local police have registered a case against the unidentified driver. Teams are currently scanning CCTV footage from cameras installed at nearby intersections and shops to trace the vehicle’s registration number.

Senior officials have assured DALIMSS News that the accused will be identified soon. "We are analyzing the footage. Strict legal action will be taken against the culprit for this reckless act," a police official confirmed.

The Public Demands Answers This incident has sparked outrage among Varanasi residents, who are tired of the rising cases of rash driving in the city. From Sigra to Lanka, citizens are asking: How many more innocent lives must be risked before speeding laws are strictly enforced?

Residents are demanding:

Immediate arrest of the absconding driver.

Increased police patrolling in high-traffic zones.

Stricter penalties for hit-and-run cases.

item.title: Police Raid Associate of Drug Kingpin in Major Crackdown on Codeine Syndicate
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
In a significant escalation against the illicit drug trade gripping the region, the Varanasi Police executed a targeted late-night raid at the residence of Prashant Upadhyay, a key associate linked to the high-profile Codeine Cough Syrup racket.

The raid is part of the ongoing investigation into the network surrounding the main accused, Shubham Jaiswal, and marks a tightening of the noose around the city's illegal pharmaceutical supply chain.

The Operation: Late-Night Search in Manduadih The operation was spearheaded by ACP (Crime) Vijay Pratap Singh, leading a joint task force comprising officers from the Kotwali, Adampur, and Ramnagar police stations.

Location: The team descended upon Upadhyay’s residence in the Madrauli area of Manduadih.

Duration: The intensive search operation lasted for over two hours.

Suspect Absconding, Businesses under Scrutiny Prashant Upadhyay, who remains at large, is identified as a major player in the Saptasagar Medicine Market. He operates two key entities: 'Radhika Enterprises' and 'Rajendra Drug Agency'.

Investigators suspect Upadhyay played a critical role in facilitating financial transactions worth crores for the illegal syndicate, specifically linked to FIR number 235/2025.

Key Seizures & Incriminating Evidence While the suspect managed to evade capture, the police team recovered substantial evidence connecting him to the illicit trade. Seized items include:

Digital Evidence: Laptops and pen drives suspected to contain detailed transaction logs.

Physical Evidence: Wrappers and vials of Codeine syrup found on the premises.

Documents: Fake documentation and financial records pointing to money laundering or falsified sales.

The 'Shaili Traders' Connection Police are now deepening their probe into Upadhyay’s connection with a firm named 'Shaili Traders' as well as his direct dealings with the jailed kingpin, Shubham Jaiswal. The recovery of digital records is expected to expose further links in the supply chain of the banned syrup.

The police have launched a manhunt to apprehend Upadhyay, stating that his arrest is crucial to dismantling the financial backbone of this drug network.

item.title: Minister AK Sharma Conducts Surprise Night Inspection of Shelters Amid Cold Wave
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
In a move to ensure the safety of the city's most vulnerable during the ongoing severe cold wave, Uttar Pradesh Urban Development and Energy Minister, Mr. AK Sharma, conducted a surprise inspection of night shelters (Rain Baseras) in Varanasi late last night.

The Minister's visit, which began after 10:00 PM, was aimed at assessing the ground reality of the facilities provided to the homeless. He was accompanied by Municipal Commissioner Mr. Himanshu Nagpal and other senior officials.

Ground Reality Check at Sikraul The inspection focused on the shelter located at Bhimnagar in Sikraul Ward. Minister Sharma took a hands-on approach, interacting directly with the occupants to inquire about their comfort and well-being.

Quality Control: He personally checked the quality of the blankets provided to ensuring they were sufficient for the biting cold.

Hygiene & Sanitation: The condition of the toilets and general cleanliness of the facility were reviewed.

Relief Measures: To further support those seeking refuge, the Minister distributed food packets to the occupants.

Zero Tolerance for Sleeping in the Open Emphasizing the government's commitment to public welfare, Minister Sharma issued strict directives to the accompanying officials.

"No one should be found sleeping in the open during this cold," the Minister stated firmly.

He directed the Varanasi Municipal Corporation to launch daily night patrols to identify homeless individuals sleeping on pavements or public spaces and ensure they are immediately shifted to the nearest night shelter.

Tech-Enabled Monitoring During the inspection, Municipal Commissioner Himanshu Nagpal briefed the Minister on the modernization of these facilities. He highlighted that the shelter is now equipped with:

CCTV Cameras for security and monitoring.

Wi-Fi Facilities to ensure better connectivity and management.

The surprise visit sends a strong message to the administration to remain on high alert and ensure that the city's relief measures effectively reach those in need during this harsh winter spell.

item.title: Confronting India’s Growing Teacher Shortage
item.dc:creator: sushant_
item.content:encoded:
As the new academic year unfolds across the nation, a silent crisis is making itself felt in the corridors of India’s schools. While student enrollment continues to rise, the number of qualified educators standing at the front of the classroom is not keeping pace. It is a challenge that is stretching the fabric of our education system, particularly in the rural heartlands.

The shortage of qualified teachers is no longer just a statistic—it is a daily reality that is redefining how our classrooms function and putting immense pressure on the educators who remain.

The "Super-Teacher" Syndrome With fewer hands on deck, the teachers currently in the system are being asked to do the impossible. In many schools, the concept of a "subject specialist" is becoming a luxury.

Multitasking to the Max: Educators are increasingly handling multiple classes simultaneously or teaching subjects outside their core specialization to fill the gaps.

The Burnout Factor: This increased workload leads to significant emotional and physical exhaustion. When a teacher is stretched too thin, their ability to be patient, creative, and responsive diminishes, leading to inevitable burnout.

The Ripple Effect on Students The most concerning aspect of this shortage is the direct impact on the students. Education is, at its heart, a relationship between teacher and student. When that relationship is diluted by overcrowding and overworked staff, the consequences are tangible:

Loss of Individual Attention: In a packed classroom managed by a single, overworked teacher, the quiet student struggling in the back often goes unnoticed. The time available for 1-on-1 mentorship is shrinking.

Stagnating Learning Outcomes: Without focused guidance, foundational concepts can be missed. Over time, these small gaps in understanding widen, leading to a decline in overall academic performance.

Reduced Holistic Growth: Teachers burdened with heavy administrative and academic loads have less energy for extracurriculars, mentorship, and emotional support—key pillars of a child's development.

A Call for Value and Support At DALIMSS, we recognize that teachers are the architects of the future. The current national scenario serves as a stark reminder of why we must value, support, and retain our educators.

Addressing this shortage requires a systemic shift—better incentives for rural postings, robust teacher training programs, and a societal change that restores the dignity and desirability of the teaching profession. Until then, patience and cooperation between parents and schools are more vital than ever to ensure our students continue to thrive despite the challenges.

item.title: The Quiet Shift: Why Modern Parents Are Focusing on the "First 1,000 Days"
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
A quiet but profound shift is happening in paediatric clinics across the country. Gone are the days when a child’s check-up was solely about plotting weight and height on a growth chart. Today, DALIMSS families and doctors are having deeper conversations—discussions that look beyond physical milestones to the very foundation of a child’s future: their brain development.

Medical experts call it "The First 1,000 Days"—the critical window from conception to a child’s second birthday. During this period, the human brain develops at a pace never repeated again, forming over one million new neural connections every single second.

As we navigate 2026, here is how forward-thinking families are optimizing this golden window of opportunity.

1. The Power of the Plate: Nutrition for Neurons The modern pantry is changing. Parents are increasingly moving away from convenient, ultra-processed snacks and turning back to basics. The focus isn't just on filling a tummy, but on fueling a growing brain.

Label Literacy: Families are becoming "label detectives," actively reducing added sugars which can lead to energy crashes and poor concentration.

Brain Foods: There is a renewed focus on the "Big Three" for brain health: Iron (for memory and attention), Iodine (for cognitive development), and Omega-3s (for healthy brain structure).

The New Normal: Instead of sugary cereals, more children are starting their day with proteins (eggs, yoghurt) and complex fats (nuts, seeds) that provide sustained energy for learning.

2. Connection Over Content: Rethinking Screen Time Perhaps the most significant topic of discussion is the "digital diet." Paediatricians are noticing that while screens are a part of life, early exposure is being heavily curbed.

Passive vs. Active: The concern isn't just about "bad" content, but about what screen time replaces. Every hour spent passively watching a screen is an hour lost for messy play, stacking blocks, or looking at a parent's face—interactions that teach empathy and problem-solving.

Analogue Enrichment: We are seeing a resurgence in "old school" stimulation: reading aloud, singing songs, and unstructured outdoor play. These activities build vocabulary and emotional security far better than any educational app.

3. The Safety of Routine In a fast-paced world, consistency is a superpower. The first 1,000 days are when a child builds their internal sense of security.

Sleep is Sacred: Establishing predictable sleep routines isn't just about rest; it's when the brain processes the day's learning.

Responsive Caregiving: "Serve and return" interactions—where a baby babbles and a parent responds—are the building blocks of communication. This emotional consistency lowers stress hormones (cortisol), allowing the brain to develop without interference.

A Community Commitment At DALIMSS, we understand that raising a child is a community effort. This shift towards holistic health—prioritizing what children eat, how they sleep, and how they play—is not a trend; it is an investment in the next generation of thinkers, leaders, and innovators.

Note: This article provides general wellness information and is not a substitute for medical advice. For specific concerns regarding your child's health or supplementation, please consult a qualified paediatrician.

item.title: Scheduled Supply Interruption in Sarnath and Surrounding Areas
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI — Residents of Sarnath and neighboring localities are advised to prepare for a scheduled power outage on Thursday, due to essential maintenance work on the local electrical infrastructure.

🕒 Timing and Duration According to an official announcement, the electricity supply will be suspended for three hours.

Start Time: 11:00 AM

End Time: 2:00 PM

📍 Affected Areas The outage will impact households and businesses in the following specific areas:

Sarnath

Purana Pul

Ledhupur

🔧 Reason for Maintenance Executive Engineer Hari Om Soni of the Urban Electricity Division (Sarnath) stated that the disruption is necessary to facilitate critical installation work at the Sarnath-Ledhupur substation. Specifically, the maintenance teams will be working on the 'Orbit City' feeder to ensure long-term supply stability.

📢 Advisory for Residents Authorities have requested residents to cooperate during this period. You are advised to:

Complete all water-related and electricity-dependent chores before 11:00 AM.

Keep mobile phones and emergency lights charged.

Plan your afternoon schedule accordingly to minimize inconvenience.

item.title: Youth Leader Shubham Seth Stages Hunger Strike For Goldsmith Community Demands In Varanasi
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI: Accusing the administration of long-standing negligence, youth leader Shubham Seth 'Golu' staged a one-day hunger strike (Ann-Jal Tyag) at Shastri Ghat on Tuesday to demand recognition for the Swarnakar (Goldsmith) community.

Two Key Demands: Leading the protest, Seth demanded the installation of a grand statue of Maharaj Narhari Das, the revered saint and deity of the community. Additionally, he called for the construction of a 'Maharaj Narhari Das Smriti Dwar' (Memorial Gate) in the Chowk Nichi Bagh area to honor the community's heritage.

"Neglect Won't Be Tolerated": Speaking to the media, Seth stated that despite running from pillar to post for the last month, the administration has ignored their requests. "The Swarnakar society has a massive contribution to this city's history, yet we have to hit the streets for the respect of our deity," he said. He warned that the agitation would intensify if the demands were not met soon.

item.title: "Banaras is a Feeling": PM Modi Redefines the Essence of Kashi as a Living Experience Beyond Words
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi describes Varanasi not just as a city, but as a "feeling that must be lived." Read how the PM highlights Kashi's unique blend of chaos, calm, tradition, and devotion

DALIMSS News Bureau | Varanasi

In a moving tribute to his parliamentary constituency, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has once again captured the soul of the spiritual capital, describing Varanasi not merely as a geographical location, but as an emotion that defies description.

Addressing the unique character of the holy city, the Prime Minister remarked that "Banaras isn’t just a city you can describe in words or pictures; it’s a feeling that must be lived."

A City Revealed Through Experience The Prime Minister emphasized that the true essence of Kashi cannot be understood from a distance. It is a city that reveals itself only to those who walk its narrow lanes and breathe its air.

The Sensory Experience: From the timeless ghats of the Ganga and the echo of temple bells to the aroma of street food and the melody of music, every corner tells a story.

Chaos and Calm: He highlighted the city's beautiful contradiction—where the chaos of everyday life coexists with profound spiritual calm.

Tradition and Devotion: It is a place where ancient traditions are not museum exhibits but are woven into the fabric of daily life.

"Je Banaras Ke Jaanna Chahat Hau..." Echoing this sentiment during his recent interactions, including the inauguration of the 72nd National Volleyball Championship in the city, PM Modi used a local Banarasi saying: "Je Banaras ke jaanna chahat hau, uka Banaras aawe ka pari" (Whoever wants to know Banaras, has to come to Banaras).

He noted that visitors, whether they are pilgrims or athletes, eventually become part of this "living feeling," experiencing the hospitality and the "Ganga-Jamuni" culture that defines the city.

Connecting Heritage with Modernity While celebrating the timeless spirit of Kashi, PM Modi also reinforced his vision of "Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi" (Development as well as Heritage). He pointed out that while the city retains its ancient soul, it is rapidly adopting modern infrastructure—from the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor to the new sports facilities at Sigra Stadium—ensuring that the "feeling" of Banaras is accessible to the world.

"To really know Banaras, you have to be here... experience its chaos and calm, tradition and devotion, all woven together in everyday life." — PM Narendra Modi

item.title: Halted by Nature: MV Ganga Vilas Unable to Reach Varanasi Due to Low Water Levels; Tourists Arrive by Road
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
The world's longest luxury river cruise, MV Ganga Vilas, was forced to turn back at Patna due to low water levels in the Ganges. Read how the foreign tourists completed their journey to Varanasi on DALIMSS News.

DALIMSS News Bureau | Varanasi

The journey of the world’s longest luxury river cruise, MV Ganga Vilas, faced an unexpected hurdle this week as nature intervened in its schedule. The vessel, which was en route to Varanasi, was forced to terminate its upstream journey at Patna due to critically low water levels in the Ganges (National Waterway-01).

While the ship could not dock at the ghats of Kashi, the spirit of the journey remained unbroken as the tourists were safely transported to the holy city by road.

Stuck at Patna: Safety First The cruise had departed from Kolkata on November 12, carrying 30 foreign tourists hailing from Germany, Switzerland, and the USA. The voyage was progressing smoothly until it reached the waters near Patna, Bihar.

Upon assessment, navigation experts deemed the water depth in the stretch between Patna and Varanasi insufficient for the massive vessel to proceed safely. Prioritizing passenger safety and vessel integrity, the decision was made on Friday to turn the cruise back toward Kolkata.

The Journey Continues: From River to Road Ensuring that the guests did not miss out on the cultural essence of their trip, the cruise management quickly arranged alternative transport. The group of 30 tourists was shifted to luxury buses and brought to Varanasi by road.

Despite the change in logistics, the tourists' itinerary remains packed with the spiritual highlights of Kashi. They are scheduled to:

Visit the revered Kashi Vishwanath Temple.

Explore the historical site of Sarnath.

Witness the mesmerizing Ganga Aarti at the Dashashwamedh Ghat.

Background: A Flagship Initiative This voyage marked what would have been the MV Ganga Vilas's third trip to Varanasi since its historic inauguration by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in January 2023. The cruise has been a symbol of India's growing river tourism potential.

Reports indicate that while 25 of the tourists will return after the tour, five have fallen in love with the spiritual vibe of the city and have opted to extend their stay in Kashi.

Key Takeaways The Incident: MV Ganga Vilas halted at Patna due to low water depth.

The Passengers: 30 tourists from Germany, Switzerland, and the USA.

The Outcome: Tourists reached Varanasi by bus to complete their pilgrimage and sightseeing.

Tags: #VaranasiNews #MVGangaVilas #RiverTourism #Kashi #Banaras #GangaAarti #NationalWaterway1 #DALIMSS #TravelUpdate

item.title: Unlocking Kashi's Potential: Manoj Tiwari Lauds PM Modi’s Vision Behind Sigra Stadium’s Transformation
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
BJP MP Manoj Tiwari highlights the massive transformation of Varanasi's Sigra Stadium, crediting PM Narendra Modi’s visionary leadership for unlocking Kashi's potential. Read the full report on DALIMSS News.

DALIMSS News Bureau | Varanasi

Varanasi, the spiritual capital of India, is witnessing a modern renaissance, and according to BJP Member of Parliament Manoj Tiwari, this shift is a testament to decisive leadership. Speaking on the city's development, Tiwari emphasized that Varanasi has always possessed immense potential, but it required the "right leadership" to translate that potential into reality.

The focal point of his praise was the recently redeveloped Sigra Stadium (Dr. Sampurnanand Sports Stadium), which stands as a new symbol of pride for Kashi.

From Neglect to Pride: The Sigra Stadium Story For years, the Sigra Stadium was seen as a neglected space with crumbling infrastructure. However, under the parliamentary constituency of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the venue has undergone a complete metamorphosis into a world-class multi-sports complex.

Highlighing this change, Manoj Tiwari stated that the stadium is no longer just a ground but a "source of pride" for the city's youth and athletes. The redevelopment is part of a broader initiative to strengthen the sports infrastructure in Uttar Pradesh, providing local talent with international-standard facilities.

"Right Leadership" Unlocks Potential Tiwari remarked that the resources and spirit of Kashi were always present.

"Varanasi has always had immense potential; it just needed the right leadership," Tiwari observed.

He credited the Prime Minister's vision for identifying these gaps and executing projects that blend the city's ancient heritage with modern aspirations. This approach aligns with the vision of a "New India", where Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities become engines of growth.

Key Highlights of the Development Modern Infrastructure: The Sigra Stadium now boasts modern amenities suitable for various national and international sports events.

Visionary Leadership: The transformation is attributed to PM Modi's direct supervision and commitment to his constituency.

Youth Empowerment: The upgraded facilities are expected to boost the morale of young athletes in the Purvanchal region.

Conclusion As Varanasi continues its journey of transformation—from the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor to the smart city projects—voices like Manoj Tiwari’s reinforce the sentiment that political will combined with a clear vision can rewrite the destiny of a city. For the residents of Varanasi, the new Sigra Stadium is not just concrete and steel; it is a promise of a brighter, fitter future.

Tags: #VaranasiDevelopment #SigraStadium #ManojTiwari #PMModi #Kashi #NewIndia #SportsInfrastructure #DALIMSSNews #UttarPradesh #VisionaryLeadership

item.title: Compassion in Kashi: Russian National Natasha Dedicates a Decade to Caring for Varanasi’s Stray Dogs
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
Meet Natasha, a Russian national who has spent 10 years in Varanasi selflessly serving stray dogs. Read this heartwarming story of compassion and humanity on DALIMSS News.

DALIMSS News Bureau | Varanasi

In the ancient, winding lanes of Kashi, where spirituality permeates every corner, a remarkable story of selfless service is warming hearts across the globe. Transcending borders and language barriers, Natasha, a Russian national, has become a beacon of hope for the city's stray animals.

For the past 10 years, Natasha has made Varanasi her home, dedicating her life to a singular mission: the care and protection of the city's street dogs. Her story is a powerful reminder that humanity has no nationality.

A Decade of Selfless Service While many tourists visit Varanasi for its ghats and temples, Natasha’s connection to the holy city is rooted in animal welfare. Her daily routine revolves around the voiceless souls of Banaras.

Daily Feeding: She ensures that the stray dogs in her locality receive nutritious food every single day.

Medical Care: Beyond food, she attends to their injuries and health, often acting as their primary guardian.

Warmth in the Winter: Dressing Over 100 Dogs As the biting cold of Northern India sweeps through Varanasi, the plight of street animals often goes unnoticed. However, Natasha has taken extraordinary measures to ensure her four-legged friends survive the chill.

Reports indicate that she has personally dressed over 100 stray dogs in warm clothes. From custom-fitted sweaters to cozy jackets, Natasha ensures the animals are protected from the harsh weather, treating them with the maternal care usually reserved for family members.

"Her love knows no boundaries. From feeding them daily to personally dressing over 100 dogs in warm clothes during winter... Humanity truly has no nationality."

A Viral Sensation of Kindness Visuals of Natasha tending to the dogs have circulated widely on social media, credited to @killer_alok_singh. The images of dogs clad in colorful winter wear, wagging their tails around their Russian caretaker, have sparked conversations about compassion and service above self.

For the students and readers of DALIMSS News, Natasha’s story serves as a living lesson in empathy. It illustrates that you do not need to be a local to care for a community; you simply need a heart willing to serve.

item.title: Shocking Lapse: Doctors Forced to Treat Patients Under Mobile Flashlights at Pt. Deendayal Hospital
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI – A severe infrastructure failure disrupted medical services at the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Government Hospital on Tuesday, as a major power outage left wards plunged into darkness, forcing medical staff to resort to desperate measures.

Total Blackout in Critical Wards In a concerning turn of events, the electricity supply to the prominent government facility failed during active hours. Reports indicate that the hospital's emergency backup systems—including generators and inverters—failed to kick in, leaving patients and staff without light or power.

Witnesses at the scene described a chaotic situation where doctors were compelled to perform check-ups and attend to patients using the flashlights of their mobile phones.

Infrastructure Questions Raised Visuals emerging from the hospital showed distressed attendants and patients navigating pitch-black corridors. The failure of the power backup systems has drawn sharp criticism regarding the maintenance and emergency preparedness of the facility.

The incident is particularly significant as the hospital serves as a key healthcare hub in the Prime Minister's parliamentary constituency. The lapse has sparked serious questions about the administrative oversight of essential medical infrastructure in the city.

item.title: Major Railway Update: Buddh Purnima Express Terminal Shifted to Banaras Station
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI – In a significant development for railway passengers in the region, the Indian Railways has announced a major operational change for the popular Rajgir–Varanasi–Rajgir Buddh Purnima Express. Effective March 2026, the train will shift its terminal operations from Varanasi Junction (Cantt) to the Banaras Railway Station (formerly Manduadih).

Key Changes for Passengers According to Saraswati Chandra, Chief Public Relations Officer of East Central Railway, the train currently operating as 14223/14224 Rajgir–Varanasi–Rajgir Buddh Purnima Express will no longer originate or terminate at Varanasi Junction.

Starting March 8, 2026, the train will:

Originate/Terminate: Banaras Railway Station (BSBS).

Operate under: New train numbers (to be announced).

Departure Time: 08:15 PM from Banaras Station.

Route: The train will proceed via Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya (DDU) Junction.

Operational Shift to Banaras Division This move marks the transfer of the weekly superfast express to the Banaras Railway Division. Previously managed elsewhere, the complete maintenance and operational responsibility of the Buddh Purnima Express will now be handled directly at the world-class coaching complex at Banaras Railway Station.

Passenger Advisory Railway authorities have advised all passengers, especially those planning travel between Rajgir and Varanasi after March 2026, to take careful note of this change. Travelers should double-check the following before booking:

Boarding Station: Ensure you select Banaras (BSBS) instead of Varanasi Junction (BSB).

Train Number: Look out for the updated train numbers in the reservation system.

This update is part of ongoing efforts to decongest Varanasi Junction and utilize the expanded capabilities of the Banaras Railway Station.

item.title: Winter Chill Tightens Grip on Varanasi: "Cold Day" Conditions and Flight Disruptions Reported
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
VARANASI — A sharp drop in day temperatures coupled with strong westerly winds has gripped Varanasi, creating severe "Cold Day" conditions across the city. Despite a marginal rise in minimum temperatures, the lack of sunshine and icy winds have kept citizens shivering, with significant disruptions reported in air travel.

Temperature Dip & The "Windy Chill" On Monday, the city witnessed a drastic drop in the maximum temperature, which plummeted to 15°C—a significant 7.7°C below the seasonal normal. The minimum temperature was recorded at 11°C.

Meteorologists noted that the gap between day and night temperatures narrowed to just 4 degrees, intensifying the perception of cold. Experts attribute this weather pattern to the La Niña effect and the Jet Stream, which is currently funneling icy winds from the snow-clad mountains directly into the plains.

Air Travel Disrupted The adverse weather conditions have heavily impacted operations at Babatpur Airport. Low visibility and dense fog led to the cancellation of three major flights on Monday, including SpiceJet and Air India Express services on the Delhi-Varanasi-Delhi route. Additionally, six other flights faced significant delays, causing inconvenience to passengers.

Forecast: A Damp New Year? Looking ahead, the weather department has cautioned that New Year’s Eve celebrations might face a wet interruption. A new Western Disturbance, currently active over Afghanistan, is influencing weather patterns in the region.

While heavy rainfall is not expected, meteorologists predict that parts of Purvanchal, including Varanasi, may witness drizzle or light rain starting December 31. Residents are advised to plan their New Year celebrations accordingly.

Advisory for Students and Staff:

Please ensure you are dressed in adequate winter wear to protect against the icy winds.

Commuters should exercise caution during early morning hours due to potential fog and low visibility.

item.title: Varanasi Pays Tribute to Sahibzadas on Bal Diwas, Honors Supreme Sacrifice and Courage
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
On the solemn occasion of Bal Diwas, the sacred city of Varanasi bowed in deep reverence to the unparalleled sacrifice of Guru Gobind Singh Ji’s Sahibzadas, whose bravery and unwavering faith continue to inspire generations. The city witnessed a heartfelt tribute commemorating the martyrdom of Sahibzada Ajit Singh, Sahibzada Jujhar Singh, Sahibzada Zorawar Singh, and Sahibzada Fateh Singh, whose courage remains etched in the soul of the nation.

At the revered ghats of the Ganga, devotees gathered to light the “Shraddha ka Deep”, symbolizing remembrance, devotion, and eternal gratitude. As countless lamps illuminated the riverbanks, the atmosphere resonated with reverence, reflecting not just on the waters of the Ganga but also in the hearts of those present.

A Tribute of Faith and Courage

The event served as a powerful reminder that Bal Diwas is not merely a celebration of childhood, but also a moment to honor young souls who stood firm in faith and righteousness. The Sahibzadas, despite their tender age, chose courage over fear and sacrifice over submission, becoming timeless symbols of strength and devotion.

Speakers at the event emphasized that the sacrifice of the Sahibzadas continues to inspire generations to uphold truth, justice, and moral courage. Their story stands as a guiding light for today’s youth, reminding them that age is no barrier to bravery and conviction.

A City United in Remembrance

As prayers echoed along the ghats, Varanasi transformed into a spiritual landscape of remembrance and reflection. The collective homage reaffirmed the city’s commitment to preserving history, honoring sacrifice, and passing forward the values of resilience and righteousness.

On this Bal Diwas, Varanasi stood united in reverence, ensuring that the legacy of Guru Gobind Singh Ji’s Sahibzadas continues to live on — not just in history, but in the hearts and actions of future generations.

— Report by Dalimss News, Varanasi

item.title: Wrestler Yogeshwar Dutt Seeks Blessings at Kashi Vishwanath, Speaks on the Path of Moksha
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi: Olympic medalist and celebrated Indian wrestler Yogeshwar Dutt visited the sacred city of Varanasi on Monday, where he offered prayers at the revered Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva.

Amid the spiritual atmosphere of the temple complex, Dutt was seen performing rituals with deep devotion. Wearing a marigold garland and folding his hands in reverence, the renowned sportsperson immersed himself in prayer, reflecting a moment of humility and faith.

Speaking to the media after his darshan, Yogeshwar Dutt shared his spiritual thoughts, saying, “Kashi Vishwanath ke darshan se jo shanti milti hai, woh shabdon mein bayaan nahi ki ja sakti. Moksha hi jeevan ka antim lakshya hai, aur Shiv bhakti uska maarg dikhati hai.” He emphasized that true fulfillment in life comes not only through achievements but through spiritual awakening and inner peace.

Despite the winter rush of devotees, the Olympic medalist’s presence drew significant attention. Devotees and fans gathered to catch a glimpse of him, some seeking blessings and others capturing moments with the sports icon. Security arrangements were in place as Dutt peacefully completed his darshan and rituals. His visit once again highlighted the timeless spiritual magnetism of Kashi, which continues to attract people from all walks of life — from saints and scholars to athletes and global icons.

item.title: Traffic Restrictions Imposed in Varanasi Ahead of New Year Rush
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi is witnessing a massive influx of tourists ahead of New Year celebrations, prompting the city administration to enforce strict traffic regulations to ensure smooth movement and public safety. The Varanasi Traffic Police have announced a comprehensive traffic diversion plan, which will remain in effect from December 29, 2025, to January 5, 2026.

According to ADCP (Traffic) Anshuman Mishra, vehicular movement toward the Kashi Vishwanath Temple and surrounding areas has been strictly restricted. Even during moderate crowd conditions, four-wheelers will not be permitted in sensitive zones such as Jagatganj, Lahurabir, Maidagin, Visheshwarganj, and Golgadda.

Key Traffic Diversions Announced

Vehicles moving from Jagatganj to Lahurabir will be diverted via Chaukaghat or Teliabag.

Traffic coming from Visheshwarganj will not be allowed to proceed towards Golgadda.

Entry towards Assi Ghat has been restricted; vehicles from Bank of Baroda Tiraha will be diverted towards Ravidas Gate, while those coming from Nagwa Chauraha will be redirected towards the BHU Trauma Centre.

Authorities have urged residents and visitors to strictly follow traffic advisories and cooperate with police personnel deployed across the city.

AI-Based Crowd Management Initiative

In a major step towards smart urban management, Municipal Commissioner Himanshu Nagpal announced the development of an AI-powered pedestrian navigation system under the Sustainable Cities Challenge. The technology aims to guide tourists through Varanasi’s narrow lanes and help prevent overcrowding during peak pilgrimage days.

Officials believe this initiative will significantly enhance crowd control, improve safety, and offer a smoother experience to pilgrims and tourists alike during the festive season.

— Report by Dalimss News, Varanasi

item.title: Severe Cold Wave Grips Varanasi, 12-Year Temperature Record Broken
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
Varanasi is reeling under an intense cold wave as icy westerly winds continue to sweep across the region, pushing temperatures to their lowest levels in over a decade. On Sunday, the city recorded a maximum temperature of just 13.5°C and a minimum of 8.8°C, marking one of the coldest days witnessed in the last 12 years.

According to meteorological data, this sharp dip in temperature places Varanasi among the coldest districts in Uttar Pradesh, alongside Ghazipur. The last comparable cold spell was recorded in December 2012, when the maximum temperature dropped to 13.3°C, and earlier in 2003, when it stood at 13.6°C. In recent years, such conditions have been rare, with 2019 recording a low of 13°C on December 28.

Westerly Winds Intensify the Chill

Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh attributed the sudden plunge in temperature to strong westerly winds blowing at speeds of up to 7 km/h, combined with the impact of La Niña conditions and fresh snowfall in the Himalayan region. These cold air currents have descended into the plains, significantly intensifying the chill factor across eastern Uttar Pradesh.

Humidity levels surged to 93 percent, further worsening the cold conditions and contributing to dense fog across the region. Visibility in the early morning hours dropped to nearly 800 meters, affecting both road and rail movement.

Cold Day Conditions Declared

Weather experts confirmed the declaration of a “Cold Day”, a meteorological classification used when the maximum temperature falls to 13°C or below, while the minimum remains at or under 8°C. Such conditions pose health risks, particularly for the elderly, children, and those exposed to outdoor environments for long durations.

Authorities have advised residents to avoid early morning outings, keep themselves adequately warm, and follow health advisories issued by local administrations.

As the cold wave persists, the Meteorological Department has indicated that similar conditions may continue over the next few days, urging citizens to remain cautious.

— Report by Dalimss News, Varanasi

item.title: Chaos in Ardali Bazaar as SUV Drags College Student’s Bike for 700 Metres, Police Intervene
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
A major law-and-order situation erupted in Ardali Bazaar, Varanasi, after a speeding Fortuner SUV allegedly dragged a college student’s motorcycle for nearly 700 metres, triggering panic, public outrage, and stone-pelting in the area. The incident caused heavy traffic disruption and prompted immediate police intervention.

According to eyewitnesses, the incident occurred when a Fortuner vehicle, allegedly being driven recklessly, collided with a two-wheeler belonging to a college student. Instead of stopping, the driver reportedly continued driving, dragging the bike along the road, which enraged locals and passersby. Within minutes, the area witnessed chaos as people gathered and raised slogans against the reckless act.

Police Intervention and Temporary Unrest

On receiving information, Cantt Police rushed to the spot and managed to control the situation. Tension escalated briefly when a few individuals resorted to stone-pelting, prompting police to deploy additional forces to prevent the situation from worsening. Traffic movement remained disrupted for a considerable time before being restored.

Both parties were later brought to the police station, where discussions were held in the presence of officials. After preliminary inquiry and mediation, the matter was settled mutually, and legal action was initiated as per procedural norms.

Crackdown on Cow Smuggling Intensified

Meanwhile, senior police officials have directed increased patrolling across Ring Road and adjoining areas following reports of cow smuggling activities. Special checking drives have been launched, and instructions have been issued to maintain strict vigilance, especially during late-night hours.

Authorities have reiterated that any attempt to disturb law and order or violate animal protection laws will be dealt with sternly.

Police Appeal

The Varanasi Police have appealed to citizens to maintain peace, follow traffic rules, and immediately report any suspicious activity. Officials emphasized that strict action will continue against reckless driving and unlawful acts to ensure public safety.

— Report by Dalimss News, Varanasi

item.title: Youth Murdered Over Verbal Dispute in Baragaon, One Arrested
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
A shocking incident of violence shook the Baragaon area of Varanasi on Friday night, where a 23-year-old youth was brutally murdered following a heated argument that escalated over a verbal abuse involving a family member.

The deceased has been identified as Ashwani Singh alias Monal, a resident of Bhelkha village. According to police sources, Ashwani had gone to his friend Mohit Patel’s residence in Idilpur for a get-together and dinner. During the gathering, an argument broke out between Ashwani and another local youth, Lavkush Patel alias Lalu, reportedly under the influence of alcohol.

Dispute Turned Deadly

Police investigations reveal that the dispute intensified after Ashwani allegedly used an offensive remark involving Lavkush’s sister, which enraged him. The situation was momentarily defused, but the anger simmered.

Later that night, as Ashwani was returning home alone, he was ambushed near a garden area between Idilpur and Pratappatti. Lavkush, along with his associates Arjun Patel and Aryan Patel, allegedly surrounded him and attacked him with sharp weapons, leading to his death on the spot.

Swift Police Action

Upon receiving information, police reached the scene and initiated an investigation. Based on the complaint lodged by the victim’s brother, a case was registered under relevant sections of the IPC.

DCP Akash Patel confirmed that the prime accused Lavkush Patel has been arrested, while teams have been deployed to apprehend the remaining accused who are currently absconding.

Tension in the Area

The brutal killing sparked tension in the locality, prompting increased police deployment to prevent any further unrest. Authorities have assured strict action against those involved and urged residents to maintain peace.

The incident once again highlights how minor disputes, fueled by anger and alcohol, can spiral into tragic consequences.

— Report by Dalimss News, Varanasi

item.title: Severe Cold Grips Varanasi and Purvanchal, Cold Day Alert Issued
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
A severe cold wave continues to affect Varanasi and the entire Purvanchal region, with temperatures plunging sharply and dense fog blanketing the area. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a cold day alert, warning residents to remain cautious as harsh weather conditions are expected to persist over the coming days.

According to weather officials, the minimum temperature has dipped below 9°C, while the maximum temperature remains nearly 6.3°C below normal, indicating unusually cold conditions for this time of year. Cold westerly winds sweeping in from the Himalayan region, coupled with the influence of a western disturbance, have intensified the chill across eastern Uttar Pradesh.

Sun Remains Hidden, Fog Persists

Residents reported that the sun failed to appear throughout the day, keeping the atmosphere cold and damp. Dense fog during early morning and late evening hours has reduced visibility, affecting road and rail movement across several districts, including Varanasi, Jaunpur, Ghazipur, and Mirzapur.

Health Advisory Issued

Health officials have advised citizens—especially the elderly, children, and those with respiratory ailments—to take necessary precautions. People are urged to avoid early morning outings, wear adequate warm clothing, and stay indoors whenever possible.

Weather Outlook

Meteorological experts have indicated that cold day conditions are likely to continue for the next few days, with little relief expected until wind patterns shift. Authorities are closely monitoring the situation and have urged the public to stay alert.

— Report by Dalimss News, Varanasi

item.title: Two-Day Water Supply Disruption in Varanasi Ahead of New Year
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
Residents of Varanasi are set to face a two-day disruption in drinking water supply as the Jal Kal Department undertakes major maintenance work at the Bhadaini Pump House, one of the city’s most critical water supply units. The shutdown will remain in effect from Sunday evening through Monday, impacting large parts of the city.

According to officials, the disruption is necessary to facilitate the installation of Air Release Valves (ARVs) and flow meters, aimed at improving water distribution efficiency and long-term supply management. After multiple rounds of technical review, authorities approved a mega shutdown on December 28 and 29 to safely carry out the work.

Areas Affected

Water supply to most parts of Varanasi will remain suspended during this period. However, officials clarified that Varunapar areas will continue to receive water supply without interruption.

Advisory Issued for Residents

Jal Kal General Manager Anup Kumar Singh urged residents to store sufficient water in advance, especially on Sunday morning, when limited supply will still be available. He assured that all efforts are being made to complete the maintenance work within the stipulated time so that normal supply can be restored at the earliest.

About Bhadaini Pump House

Established in 1907, the Bhadaini Pump House is one of the oldest and most vital water supply facilities in Varanasi. Drawing water directly from the Ganga River, it plays a crucial role in supplying potable water to large sections of the city. Regular upgrades and maintenance are essential to ensure uninterrupted and safe water distribution.

Authorities have appealed to residents for cooperation during the temporary inconvenience, emphasizing that the upgrade work will strengthen the city’s water supply system in the long run.

— Report by Dalimss News, Varanasi

item.title: VDA Cracks Down on Illegal Constructions in Zone-4, Multiple Buildings Sealed
item.dc:creator: sushant
item.content:encoded:
The Varanasi Development Authority (VDA) has intensified its campaign against unauthorized constructions, taking strict action in Zone-4 by sealing several buildings found to be violating approved building norms. The move comes as part of an ongoing drive to enforce urban planning regulations and ensure orderly development across the city.

According to officials, inspections revealed that several structures were constructed in clear violation of sanctioned building maps, including unauthorized floors, illegal extensions, and deviations from approved layouts. Despite repeated notices issued earlier, the violations were not rectified, prompting the authority to take strict enforcement action.

Action Under Building Regulations

VDA officials stated that the sealing drive was conducted in accordance with the Uttar Pradesh Urban Planning and Development Act. Properties found violating approved plans were immediately sealed, and further legal proceedings have been initiated against the concerned owners.

Officials emphasized that unauthorized constructions not only disrupt planned urban development but also pose serious safety risks to residents and surrounding structures.

Public Advisory Issued

The VDA has appealed to citizens and builders to strictly adhere to sanctioned building maps and obtain necessary approvals before undertaking any construction activity. Authorities warned that violations will invite strict legal action, including sealing, penalties, and possible demolition.

Drive to Continue

Officials confirmed that the enforcement drive will continue across other zones of the city in the coming days. Surprise inspections will be carried out to identify illegal constructions and ensure compliance with building regulations.

The VDA reiterated its commitment to planned urban development and urged residents to cooperate in maintaining the city’s safety, order, and infrastructure integrity.

— Report by Dalimss News, Varanasi
